title: GH#1004: feat: find email addresses protection cannot hide
body:
## Summary

Resolves #1004.

- Add an explicit Security-panel home-page check and `wp seoprostack email-protection check [<url>]` using the same address/context/source-hint rows.
- Keep HTTP requests bounded to the site's own host and port, with no cookies, redirects, settings changes or ordinary-load requests.
- Document schema, plugin script data and template limitations in README.md and the setting description; update all three changelogs without a version bump.

## Files and reference patterns

Implementation stays in `includes/features/class-seoprostack-email-protection.php`, following the hardening setting-panel hook and added-keys CLI registration patterns. Documentation changes are limited to README.md, changelog.txt and readme.txt.

## Runtime Testing

Risk: high (explicit admin request); testing level: runtime-verified.

Verified head: `5e7e47c8664700774a481c68afd9b08893772fd8`.

- `scripts/lint.sh`: all checks pass, including PHPCS and PHPStan.
- `scripts/preflight-release.sh --offline`: zero errors. Four expected release/listing warnings: two Unreleased headings, WordPress.org slug choice, existing version tag on the release commit. No version bump or publication is intended.
- `scripts/plugin-check.sh`: zero errors in both builds (Plugin Check 2.1.0, WordPress 7.1.4). Existing unrelated warnings remain in unchanged updater, whole-admin theme and database feature files; no finding names the changed feature.
- Disposable WordPress through `scripts/test-site.sh up`: real home-page requests find schema, inline script JSON, JSON attribute, ordinary attribute and template text, but not the protected post-content address. Rank Math 1.0.280 was active with its Local SEO email set; the hint names that exact field.
- Browser verification: Security panel before and after the manual check at desktop 1440px and mobile 390px; expected rows and hint present, protected address absent, zero console errors and no page-level horizontal overflow. Logged out afterwards.
- Repeated CLI/runtime check on minimum WordPress 6.2 / PHP 7.4.33 produces the same rows, with an empty debug log.
- Direct runtime assertions: ordinary panel rendering makes zero HTTP requests; duplicate addresses aggregate all four contexts; entity addresses are detected; protected attributes are ignored; cross-host, cross-port, non-HTTP and credential-bearing URLs are rejected before HTTP.

Docker fixture note: the published loopback port is on the Docker host, so a disposable must-use fixture maps that exact connection back to the web container with `CURLOPT_CONNECT_TO`. The production URL validation and safe HTTP API remain unchanged; no fixture ships.

## Acceptance self-review

| Criterion | Result | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| JSON-LD and script email reported, protected content omitted | Satisfied | Real public-page fetch, CLI and browser rows |
| Rank Math Local SEO hint | Satisfied | Active Rank Math 1.0.280, matching stored email, browser and CLI hint |
| CLI prints the same rows and findings exit 0 | Satisfied | Default and explicit-home CLI invocations |
| No request on ordinary admin loads | Satisfied | Browser initial state plus zero-request runtime assertion |
| All three requested checks have no errors | Satisfied | lint, offline release preflight and Plugin Check pass |

Direct diff/self-review found no material defect. Review bundle SHA-256: `8b5973e2ce0bcd26d1409928be4f3fa66334946e7333ab5ed547cc5caceb1dce` (injection scan clean).

## Decisions

The admin checks the home page; the optional same-site URL is available through CLI. Results are not persisted. Duplicate addresses aggregate their contexts. No unverified Yoast option is named; unmatched sources receive generic guidance.

title: GH#1011: Website Setup board starter tasks (fluentboards_tasks); release 1.3.95
body:
## What

Fluent Boards starter data adds a **Website Setup** board: one task per account and key a site needs, in running order, each with plain steps, links, where its key belongs (never in the task) and when it is done.

1. Setup Hosting (Hostinger, referral link; plan with SSH)
2. Setup Cloudflare (domain DNS and security)
3. Setup aidevops (your AI assistant)
4. Setup SSH Access for aidevops
5. Connect your AI to this Board (Fluent Boards → Settings → MCP for AI Agents; optional)
6. Setup Premium Plugin Updates (GPL Vault): **GitHub builds only** (`starters/github/`, left out of the WordPress.org build at the owner's request)
7. Setup Business Email (Purelymail)
8. Setup Email Sending (Amazon SES + FluentSMTP)
9. Setup File Storage (Cloudflare R2)
10. Setup Google Cloud (budget alert; Search Console)
11. Setup Payment Processing (Stripe, PayPal, Paddle, Polar)

### Code

- New starter item type `fluentboards_tasks` (`includes/class-seoprostack-starters.php`): `board`, `title`, `description` (Markdown), `after`. Matched by title on the board (archived included). Created with `TaskService::createTask()` in the first stage, placed with `Task::moveBetweenTasks()` after `after`, else the previous starter item, else at the top. The stage is renumbered first with `Task::reIndexTasksPositions()`: Fluent Boards stores positions to 2 decimals, and repeated midpoints tied in testing (0.495 → 0.50).
- Remove keeps tasks that were edited, closed, archived, commented on, or that have attachments or subtasks.
- `starters/github/<name>.json` is merged into the starter of the same name; `.distignore-wporg` excludes it, and `scripts/preflight-plugin.sh` parses it.
- Other plugins add tasks to the board through `seoprostack_starters` (SEO Pro Directory will: wpallstars/seoprodirectory#243).
- README: a Website Setup board section with what to click without AI, what an AI runs over SSH, and why to set up SSH first. Release 1.3.95.

## Verification

- Throwaway Docker WordPress with Fluent Boards 2.2.2 (wp.org):
  - Fresh site: 13 items added, in order 1–11; a second add added 0.
  - Edited one task: Remove took back 11 and kept the edited task and its board.
  - PSD-style board (default stages plus legacy cards): generic tasks at the top in order, plus another plugin's tasks after Setup Google Cloud. No position ties.
- `scripts/lint.sh phpstan` OK; PHPCS clean; `php -l`.
- `scripts/preflight-release.sh --ref HEAD`: 0 errors (`wporg: no starters/github`, every `.wporg-links` text replaced).
- `scripts/plugin-check.sh`: no errors in either zip.
- Links checked to load (200) on 2026-10-29.

Resolves #1011

- Keys in Fluent Forms meta `seoprostack_form_key`; `wp seoprostack form-keys list|set|unset`, plus `set --copy-from=<meta-key>` to adopt keys held under an older meta key. Starter data forms accept `key`.

title: GH#1018: Watermark pictures: Never watermark box on each picture; release 1.3.98
body:
Resolves #1018

## What

**Watermark pictures** gets a **Never watermark** box on each picture, and release **1.3.98**.

- `_seoprostack_watermark_skip` post meta (`SEOProStack_Watermark_Images::SKIP_META`, `skipped()`): `'1'` leaves a picture unmarked. Code that adds pictures (such as a site's own page photographs) may set it too.
- `unmarkable()` returns `watermark_never`, so new uploads, **Add watermark**, bulk actions, **Mark every picture** and `wp seoprostack watermark-images` all leave it alone; batches count it as *left alone*, not failed.
- `add()` checks it before a marked picture's mark comes off to be made again, so **Mark again** leaves an already-marked, ticked picture as it is. **Remove watermark** still unmarks it.
- The box shows in the picture's details in Media → Library, the editors' media windows and the attachment edit screen (`attachment_fields_to_edit` / `attachment_fields_to_save`), while Watermark pictures is on, or wherever it is already ticked so it can be cleared. A hidden `seoprostack_watermark_skip_shown` field means a save from a screen that did not show the box never clears it.
- The media window saves compat fields without redrawing them (core's `AttachmentCompat` renders on `add` only), so ticking hides **Add watermark** at once with an inline handler; the row is `display: block` in core's CSS, so it sets `style.display`, not `hidden`. **Remove watermark** stays.
- README, `readme.txt` and `changelog.txt`: the feature and 1.3.98.

## Verification

On an isolated review copy (Lloydminster), the changed file in place of 1.3.97's, then 1.3.97's file put back (SHA-256 `465a4aa7…`, from `fc1454f8`):

- WP-CLI on a regional photograph: a save without the shown field changes nothing; ticked → meta `1`, `unmarkable()` = `watermark_never`, `add()` = `watermark_never`; unticked → meta removed; meta restored.
- Media Library grid modal, unmarked picture 4048: before `Add watermark`; tick → save 200, row hidden at once; reopen → ticked, no Add link; untick → save 200; reopen → unticked, `Add watermark` back.
- Same on marked picture 4189: `Remove watermark` stays throughout; help text says it is marked now.
- Attachment edit screen, 4189: tick → Update (Rank Math's `updateMeta` first, then the form) → `post.php … message=1` → ticked after reload; untick → Update → unticked after reload. No JS errors or dialogs.
- Test meta on 4048, 4189 and 3260 left empty, as before; the temporary admin session revoked.
- `php -l`; `scripts/preflight-release.sh --no-docker --offline`: 0 errors, 1 warning (WordPress.org slug, already on main); `scripts/plugin-check.sh`: no errors (GitHub zip 6 and WordPress.org zip 3 warnings, all in other files and already on main).

title: GH#1020: Kadence query loops skip the full REST API boot, theme mods decoded once; release 1.3.99
body:
## Summary

Two Kadence costs paid on every front-end page, fixed in **Fixes for other plugins** (on by default), and release 1.3.99.

- **Kadence Blocks Pro query loops** no longer boot the whole REST API. While a `kadence/query-*` block whose query has not run renders (no REST server running yet), `$wp_rest_server` is a `SEOProStack_Kadence_Query_Server` (new `includes/class-seoprostack-kadence-query-server.php`) holding only `GET /wp/v2/kadence_query/query`, with Kadence's own callback, `permission_callback` and args. Kadence's own `rest_do_request()` dispatches there. The global is cleared as dispatch starts and after every block, so any other route or later REST use gets the full server. REST requests are untouched.
- **Kadence theme mods** are decoded once per request: `pre_option_theme_mods_{stylesheet}` (Kadence or a child theme) returns the value decoded once per site and stored string in `wp_load_alloptions()`, through `option_{name}` filters as `get_option()` does.

Not fixable here: Kadence Blocks 3.8.0 design tokens read `wp_kb_design_tokens` 268 times per page (`Token_Store` is `final`, and its DB layer has no short-circuit filter).

## Evidence

Web-SAPI profile, Burnaby network site `/service/construction-company/` (WooCommerce, MCP Adapter, Fluent apps, Ultimate Multisite), three alternating A/B pairs using the same mechanism as a request-local prototype:

| | Query block (inclusive) | Peak memory |
|---|---|---|
| Before | 689 / 708 / 751 ms | 78 MB |
| Light server | 168 / 220 / 194 ms | 70 MB |

title: GH#1027: Kadence Blocks design token reads once per request; release 1.3.101
body:
Resolves #1027

## What

**Fixes for other plugins** now keeps Kadence Blocks 3.8.0's design token reads for the request. Kadence's `Token_Store` queried `SELECT * FROM {prefix}kb_design_tokens WHERE slug = '…'` about 1,900 times per page (about 280 ms), even with no tokens saved. Release 1.3.101.

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-fixes.php`: `kadence_token_reads()` on `query` (`PHP_INT_MAX`), registered with Kadence Blocks 3.8.0+ and core's own `wpdb` class only. First read through `get_row()` runs; its rows are collected as the next query starts; later identical reads get `$wpdb` set as running them would (flush, cloned rows, `last_query`, `num_rows`, `func_call`, `check_current_query` re-armed through a closure in `wpdb`'s scope) and `''` stops `query()` before the server. Any other statement naming the table forgets every kept read; direct `$wpdb->query()` always runs.
- README fixes list and changelog, `changelog.txt`, `readme.txt`, version 1.3.101.

## Verification

Tested the branch's method on production data without installing it (the method extracted from this file into a test class under WP-CLI):

- Front page content, separate processes: 1,612 → 62 queries. HTML off vs on differs only on Fluent Forms' per-request line, which two runs without the fix differ on too.
- MySQL temporary table with a row: kept `OBJECT`/`ARRAY_A` rows equal fresh reads; empty results stay `null`; mutating a returned row does not leak; after an `UPDATE` the next read queries again and sees the new document, then is kept again; `check_current_query` is `true` afterwards; a direct `query()` of the same SQL runs and returns 1 (the first draft returned `false` here; fixed by setting `func_call` and requiring this exact SQL).
- `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`: all passed.

title: GH#1022: Count in-progress media uploads as waiting
body:
## Summary

Resolves #1022.

- Keep active uploads waiting, preserving the early DONE marker and durable retry job
- Publish actual restore/PUT failures explicitly, with the error and count-cache invalidation
- Recover waiting inventories with lost retry jobs through --retry-failed
- Update the three existing changelogs (scope correction persisted on the issue)

## Files and reference pattern

Implementation: includes/features/class-seoprostack-media-storage.php, following existing deferred-upload waiting and failed-inventory handling. Documentation: README.md, readme.txt, changelog.txt. No new state or schema; only complete uploaded inventories can serve bucket URLs.

## Runtime Testing

Risk: high (upload state transitions). Testing level: runtime-verified. Isolated WordPress 7.1.4, PHP 8.3, MinIO, from the committed release build. Final head 7f433a16 changes only the readme wording after implementation head 249fec01.

| Acceptance | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Active upload is not failed | Paused at the existing cache-control hook before PUT; a second WP-CLI process saw waiting=1, failed=0, inventory/state waiting, Waiting to upload label, local attachment URL, and a future retry job. Completed as uploaded=1. |
| Actual failure and explicit retry | Wrong test secret produced HTTP 403 SignatureDoesNotMatch, failed=1, saved error and failure label. Correcting the secret and running wp seoprostack media-storage upload --retry-failed --limit=1 produced uploaded=1, failed=0. |
| Killed run is recoverable | KILL of the isolated uploading container left waiting=1 and a durable retry job. After making that job due, status still showed waiting, and ordinary upload --limit=1 completed it. |
| Missing-job recovery | A waiting inventory with the current DONE marker and no retry option was recovered through --retry-failed. |
| Restore failure | Removed local files, then used the wrong secret: failed=1 with the restore error; removed-file serving stayed on the confirmed bucket inventory. Corrected secret, switched removal off and retried: local file restored. |
| Serving safety | In-progress and PUT-failed pictures used local URLs; serving readers still require uploaded complete inventories. Removed-file fallback remains unchanged. |

## Checks and review

- scripts/lint.sh: PHP, JS, ShellCheck, actionlint, PHPCS and PHPStan passed; no JS build is configured.
- scripts/preflight-release.sh --offline: zero errors; both release builds passed PHP 7.4 syntax. Release-only warnings: Unreleased headings, existing version tag and WordPress.org slug. Core comparison not run because no adjacent starter checkout is configured.
- The initial added changelog exceeded the readme size cap; shortened the old entry. Final readme is 10,197 bytes (under 10 KiB). Final exact-head scripts/preflight-release.sh --offline --no-docker on 7f433a162774 passed with zero errors and four release-only warnings. Both zips already passed PHP 7.4 syntax on the unchanged implementation.
- Independent read-only source review found no defects in upload transitions, restore failure handling, serving gates or retry-stranded handling. It inspected current source; diff attribution and runtime evidence were verified by the primary executor.
- Debug log inspected: only two test-script setup errors (file ownership in an initial byte-change probe and unavailable SIGKILL constant in an initial self-kill probe), corrected before successful scenarios. No plugin-origin warning/error was observed; intentional storage failures were retained as safe status errors.

No release, production deployment or credentials change is requested. No new test infrastructure or production test interface is added.

## Automation handoff

PR ready, exact head pushed, working tree clean. One immediate remote observation showed no terminal failures (including SonarCloud, Codacy and Qlty). The single full-loop-helper.sh merge 1033 wpallstars/seoprostack attempt stopped at the required-checks-pending safety gate. Handed to pulse for check/review events; no polling or bypass. Isolated WordPress and MinIO resources were removed after verification.

title: GH#1036: Link cards keep pictures whole, use high-res site icons and show the external link icon; release 1.3.105
body:
## Summary

- **Picture shapes** (`imageShape`, `blocks/link-card/block.json`): *Its own shape* (default, also for existing cards: the attachment's width/height clamped 1–2), *Wide, as in social previews* (1.91:1), *Square*, *Fill the card's height* (the old cropped look). `render_block()` adds `is-shape-*` and a `--sps-link-card-ratio` on the picture's frame. Beside the text the frame sits inside the card, 8em high in every card (≤40% of the width), so social preview pictures (and their words) show whole and a list of cards lines up. *Fill* now follows the text's height (picture positioned absolutely).
- **High-res site icons** (`imageKind`): new `POST seoprostack/v1/link-card-icon` (`upload_files`) reads the page once (core's `rest_url_details_http_request_args` filter and user agent), collects `apple-touch-icon`/`icon` links by `sizes`, `msapplication-TileImage` (WordPress's site icon), the web app manifest, then `/apple-touch-icon.png`; skips SVG/ICO and anything said to be under 128px, tries ≤4 largest first, checks the real size with `wp_getimagesize()`. The editor uses it automatically when a page has no picture; block settings add **Use the site's icon** / **Use the page's picture**. Icons show whole (`contain`) on the card's soft background.
- **External link icon after every card's site name** (user report): External link icons' rule skipped links containing an `img`, and on picture-less cards the link's `::after` became a flex item alone at the bottom left. Link cards mark the site name `sps-external-link-after`; `SEOProStack_External_Links::styles()` puts the icon there and leaves the link's own `::after` off.
- Empty downloads (sites that answer a missing `/apple-touch-icon.png` with an empty 200) are refused before `wp_get_image_mime()`, which logged an `exif_imagetype()` notice. The editor reads the picture with `getEntityRecord('postType', 'attachment')` (`getMedia()` is deprecated in 6.9).
- `sps-no-external-icon` on a container also hides the Link card icon (CodeRabbit), as documented for other links.
- Release 1.3.105 docs (1.3.104 went to #1040): version, `readme.txt`, `changelog.txt`, `README.md` (Link cards, External link icons).

Resolves #1036

## Runtime Testing

`runtime-verified` on `scripts/test-site.sh` (WordPress 7.1.4, PHP 8.3, Kadence), Playwright:

- Cards for bluellama.co.uk, ipopdigital.com, serif.je, wordpress.org (1.91:1 pictures) render 259×136 frames; Wide 260×136, Square 136×136, Fill 233×156 (text height), Left, Above (728×360). Icon cards: 136×136 auto, Fill 233×156, Above 728×136.
- Icon route: ipopdigital.com → 1024×1024 apple-touch-icon; bluellama.co.uk → its declared favicon after an empty `/apple-touch-icon.png`; islandinteractive.co.uk → 404 "no icon big enough" (its certificate fails for www).
- External link icons on: every card has the icon after the site name (`::after` 10.45px), none on the link itself; light, simulated dark and 400px wide.
- Editor: same classes and frame sizes as the front end, no block warnings; **Use the site's icon** → `is-image-icon`, **Use the page's picture** → back. No `getMedia` deprecation.

title: GH#1046: Links skip redirects: internal links to a permanently redirected address point at its target; release 1.3.106
body:
## What

New, on by default: **Links skip redirects** (Links tab). Links in posts, block widgets and menus to an old address that Rank Math permanently redirects to another page of the same site now point straight at that page when it is shown. Saved content is unchanged.

Resolves #1046

## Why

Renamed pages keep their old address through Rank Math → Redirections, but internal links still point at it, so each visit and crawl takes an extra 301. A client site did this with a must-use plugin no update reaches; this is the generic version.

## How

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-redirect-links.php` (`SEOProStack_Redirect_Links`, key `redirect_links`), listed in `SEOProStack_Setup::FEATURES` after Modal links.
- Reads Rank Math's active, exact, 301/308 redirections with a same-site target: one query, at most 500, through `%i`, kept in a 10-minute transient. Only while Rank Math and its Redirections module are loaded; otherwise nothing is skipped and nothing is cached. Forgotten on `rank_math/redirection/post_updated`, `term_updated` and `deleted`.
- Front end: `the_content` and `widget_block_content` (`WP_HTML_Tag_Processor`) and `wp_nav_menu_objects`, priority 20. Follows chains up to five hops and keeps fragments. Links with a query string are skipped, and HTML that mentions no old path is not parsed.
- Left alone: temporary redirects (the old address stays the one to link to) and redirects to other sites (`/go/` affiliate links keep their click path).
- Filter `seoprostack_redirect_links` for other plugins' redirects.
- Docs: README feature section. The default-on reason is recorded in `AGENTS.md`.
- Release 1.3.106 (second commit): version in `seoprostack.php`, `readme.txt` Stable tag, README `Version:` line and badge. The changelog section 1.3.106 also takes #1043's entries, already on `main`. `scripts/preflight-release.sh --no-docker`: 0 errors.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`: all passed.
- On a review-copy site with Rank Math 1.0.280, I loaded the class on its own with `wp eval-file`. The map was injected through reflection, so no transient was written:
  - Redirection `exact:how-it-works` 301 → `/for-my-property/`. `read()` took one query.
  - `/how-it-works/` → `https://…/for-my-property/`; the absolute form with `#part` → `…/for-my-property/#part`.
  - Unchanged: `/how-it-works/?x=1`, `https://example.com/how-it-works/`, `/no-such-old-address/`, `#login-drawer`, `mailto:`.
  - In an HTML fragment, only the old link changed. HTML with no old address came back byte-for-byte identical.
- Across five installs (ten sites), every Rank Math redirection is an active 301, so limiting to permanent redirects loses nothing there.

title: GH#1039: Load plugins only where needed checks each address and skips what it renders the same without; release 1.3.108
body:
Resolves #1039

## What

Load plugins only where needed skips more plugins on each address of the site. Plugins that add something to pages loaded on every page of their kind, even where they added nothing. Each address visitors open is now checked once in the background, and skips only the plugins it renders exactly the same without.

The first approach on this issue, verifying per page kind from sampled pages, failed on a test site: sampled pages had no form, so Fluent Forms was marked safe for every page, and the contact page lost its form (see the issue comment). This PR checks each address by itself instead of generalising from a sample.

## How

- `learn_front()` saves for each page kind the plugins it might also skip (`propose`): plugins that add to pages or extend one that does, but not the kind's needs, plugins that always load or check logins, or **Always load these plugins on the site**.
- `start_front()` keys a cookie-free address by its path plus `cpage`, `p`, `page`, `page_id` and `paged` (search results are not checked). It applies the saved skip set for that address, or queues it after a 200 render (at most 50 queued).
- The scheduled task `seoprostack_front_verify` (`includes/class-seoprostack-front-verify.php`) renders each queued address through a loopback: first as it is served, then without groups of the proposed plugins, halving a group when the page changes.
  - Each render carries a one-time token (`hash_equals`), is kept out of page caches (`DONOTCACHEPAGE` plus a unique argument), never learns or flags the site, and reports which plugin wrote to the database, sent a request or sent mail.
  - Plugins with such effects are never skipped, and a trial that adds effects fails.
  - A match needs the same status, key headers and cookie names, and the same normalised HTML. Up to 50 words that change on every render are tolerated, found by a second base render.
- Results go in `seoprostack_plugin_front_pages`. They hold until the content revision or the plugin set changes, for a week at most, and cover up to 5,000 addresses with shared skip sets. Five loopback failures in a row pause checks for an hour.
- The status panel shows how many addresses were checked, how many skip more plugins and how many wait. Uninstall removes the new options and the hook.

## Verification

On an isolated copy of a production site (45 active plugins, LiteSpeed, SEO Pro Stack 1.3.106 plus these files):

- 17 addresses were queued from visits and all were verified across 4 scheduled runs (about 50 s each). Single pages, the contact page, the home page, archives and pagination were among them.
- Cookie-free HTML compared with and without the saved checks was identical on all 17 addresses, apart from LiteSpeed's timestamp comments.
- Plugins loaded per page:

| Pages | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Single pages | 36 | 20 |
| Contact page (keeps Fluent Forms; form present) | 36 | 22 |
| Archives | 39 | 34 |

- Server time to headers (median of 4 interleaved rounds):

| Page | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Single page | about 620 ms | about 400 ms |
| Home | 531 ms | 441 ms |
| Directory archive | 540 ms | 535 ms |

- A search URL was not queued.
- `scripts/lint.sh`: php, js, shell, workflows, phpcs and phpstan all pass.

title: GH#1061: WebP and AVIF images records a conversion only when the picture is unchanged; release 1.3.115
body:
## Summary

WebP and AVIF images could mark a picture converted while WordPress was still making its sizes, with a record (`_seoprostack_nextgen`) missing the later sizes. Media in cloud storage uploads only listed copies, so those copies stayed on the server, never sent or uploaded, and a storage drain with local removal on could not finish. Release 1.3.115.

Resolves #1061

## Changes

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-nextgen-images.php`
  - `GENERATION` post meta (`_seoprostack_nextgen_generation`), changed by `metadata_updated()` on every metadata save.
  - `convert_attachment()` reads the generation from the database before the sizes, and `unchanged()` compares generation, attached file and file names at the end. A change leaves the picture waiting (`nextgen_changed`); the next conversion keeps the copies made and lists every size.
  - `run_batch()` defers `nextgen_changed` pictures to the next batch; `wp seoprostack convert-images` passes over pictures that stay waiting after an error once per run (it could repeat them before).
  - `record_unlisted()`: converts a converted picture again when up-to-date copies of its files are missing from its record. The skip conditions match `convert_attachment()`'s loop, so a conversion always lists what it flags.
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-media-storage.php`: `upload_attachment()` calls `record_unlisted()` after restoring removed files; when it changed the record, the picture is queued (which clears the retry job) and uploaded with its copies by the next batch.
- README (both features, changelog), `changelog.txt`, `readme.txt`, version 1.3.115.

## Verification

- `php -l`, PHPCS on the changed files, PHPStan: clean.
- `scripts/preflight-release.sh`: 0 errors (1 existing WordPress.org slug warning). `scripts/plugin-check.sh`: no errors.
- Disposable WordPress 7.1.4 / PHP 8.3 (`scripts/test-site.sh`), one race script run on 1.3.114 and on this branch. The script adds a size through the metadata filter while `convert_attachment()` runs:

| Step | 1.3.114 | This branch |
|---|---|---|
| Size added mid-conversion | recorded done, new size not listed | `nextgen_changed`, waiting, record unchanged |
| Converted again | lists new size | lists new size, copy on disk |
| `record_unlisted()` on a stale record | not present | converts, lists the copy, copy not re-encoded |
| `record_unlisted()` again / no record / waiting picture | not present | no / converts (7 names) / no |

- Data repaired on live sites before the fix (four pictures, three installs) matched this pattern: after converting again, audits found no unlisted copies and the bucket served the copies with HTTP 200.

title: GH#1064: Media in cloud storage names uploads from the claim index, not every stored record; release 1.3.117
body:
## Summary

With local copies removed, every `wp_unique_filename()` call read every stored inventory of the site (`stored_records()`) to list the folder's stored names. Production directory stacks paid 0.27s (1,385 stored pictures), 2.92s (15,221) and 7.24s (18,949) per call, several calls per picture, so bulk imports slowed as libraries grew.

WordPress only tests names that begin with the file name's stem (without a trailing `-N`): `_wp_check_existing_file_names()` matches `{name}-(size|scaled|rotated){ext}` case-insensitively, for the name, its numbers and other formats. So:

- `index_claims()` also stores a name claim (`n:{folder}\n{prefix}`) for each stored file under every hyphen-ended prefix of its lower-case name and the whole name (`name_hashes()`), in the existing `seoprostack_media_claims` table. The index is rebuilt for each version already, so no schema change.
- `unique_filename_files()` computes the stem (`numbering_stem()`), reads only the inventories under its claim (`stem_records()`: one primary-key lookup, then `handover_records()`), and returns only names beginning with the stem, local `scandir()` names included.
- Until the index is complete for this version, or when the lookup fails (`claims_failed()`), it streams every inventory as before, still filtered by stem.

Version 1.3.117 (plugin header, constant, readme, README, changelog).

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`: all passed.
- Read-only equivalence check on production inventories (the branch's `numbering_stem()`/`name_hashes()` logic copied into a `wp eval-file` script, index simulated from every inventory): 3 stacks, 34,669 inventories, 846,160 names in this month's folder, 243 sample upload names (stored stems as uploaded, numbered, upper-case, size-like, other formats, new names); every name the full list holds for a stem was found through the index, and 15,480 `_wp_check_existing_file_names()` tests gave the same answer with the full and the index-scoped list.
- Not yet run on a live upload with the built index: after release, on the smallest stack first, time the filter (expected milliseconds) and an import of pictures, and confirm a same-name upload still gets a new number (GH#956).

Resolves #1064

title: GH#1069: Resumable media jobs for watermark refresh, bucket adoption and kept originals; release 1.3.128
body:
## Summary

Resolves #1069.

Implements resumable `media-jobs start|status|stop remark|adopt|originals` on the existing storage lease, hook and uninstall namespace. The runner journals an in-flight attachment before work, persists descending scan cursors, retries refusals at the tail and limits systematic failures across a rolling window. Media jobs wait briefly for the shared lease, skip pictures already drained, and also run in WP-CLI (`media-jobs run <kind>`).

### Files and integration

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-media-jobs.php`: durable job coordinator and CLI.
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-media-storage.php`: worker integration, `lease_wait()`, existing safe adoption/original-upload paths, and interrupted-refresh upload guard.
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-watermark-images.php`: frozen mark context and refresh path using kept originals and format regeneration.
- `README.md`, `readme.txt`, `changelog.txt`: command usage, recovery, limits and safety constraints.

## Runtime Testing

Risk: high (resumable state machines and verified local-file removal). **runtime-verified** at head `8540b60da88429e297c68b00788c93ab687134b0`.

- `scripts/lint.sh`: php, js, shell, workflows, phpcs, phpstan all pass.
- Disposable WordPress (PHP 8.3) from `scripts/test-site.sh`, with an isolated MinIO S3 service: a public `media` bucket and a separate private `originals` bucket. Settings: Watermark pictures (new, keep originals, site-icon mark), Media in cloud storage with local removal, WebP/AVIF copies.
- 16 generated pictures marked, uploaded and verified; local copies and kept originals removed (`media-storage status`: uploaded 18, failed 0, local copies removed 17, originals uploaded 16, originals local removed 16). A bucket address serves `200 image/jpeg`.
- **Re-mark with SIGKILL:** changed the site icon so 14 remote-only pictures held an older mark; ran `media-jobs run remark` with a `--require` hook that `posix_kill(getmypid(), 9)` at the third attachment metadata write (inside each refresh, after clean sizes are made). The job resumed through repeated kills to `done`: 14 done, 2 skipped (icons), 0 failed. Afterwards every picture had the current mark signature, no `remark_pending`, kept originals back in the private bucket, no local files left, and the lease free. Two newer pictures past the cutoff were left alone.
- `media-jobs run originals`: 2 done (the pictures with local kept originals), 14 skipped (already drained), 0 failed.
- `media-jobs run adopt`: 15 skipped (already adopted), 0 failed; no files restored.
- Debug log empty.

### Review fixes (c5978fc3, d6601d73)

- `cli()` releases the lease before `WP_CLI::error()` (which exits, skipping `finally`). Verified: `start remark` with Watermark pictures off errors and leaves no `seoprostack_storage_lock` row.
- A new upload whose mark is queued behind a running media batch sets `_seoprostack_watermark_queued`; storage `waiting()`/`upload_locked()` skip it while a non-remove watermark batch runs; the batch clears it after the picture. Verified with another request holding the lease: flagged and excluded, then marked, unflagged and included.
- `turn()` stops a re-mark job before choosing a picture when the mark changes or is off (`watermark_mark_changed` in the stop list). Verified: icon changed mid-job → failed, 0 refusal rows, lease free.

### Release 1.3.128 (b1b24637)

Version in `seoprostack.php`, `readme.txt`, `README.md` and badges; Unreleased renamed to 1.3.128 (with #1074 and #1102). `scripts/preflight-release.sh --no-docker`: 0 errors, 1 known warning (WordPress.org slug); `readme.txt` 9,635 bytes.

title: GH#1084: Fluent Support email by IMAP saves sent ticket emails to the Sent folder; release 1.3.120
body:
## Summary

With **Fluent Support email by IMAP** on, every email Fluent Support sends a customer from that inbox is now also saved, exactly as sent and marked read, to the mailbox's Sent folder over IMAP. This keeps the support record in the owner's mailbox, as an email app would. Sending is unchanged: it still goes through the site's mail plugin (FluentSMTP through Amazon SES on the owner's site). Release 1.3.120: 1.3.119 was released for #1083 while this PR was open, and main is merged in.

- `includes/class-seoprostack-helpdesk-imap-sent.php` (new, `SEOProStack_Helpdesk_Imap_Sent`):
  - `mark()` at `fluent_support/mail_to_customer_header` (`PHP_INT_MAX`) marks the email when the ticket's `mailbox_id` is the feature's inbox. All five customer emails go through this filter: ticket created, agent reply, closed by agent, created by an agent, created on the customer's behalf.
  - `arm()` at `pre_wp_mail` hands the mark to the next `wp_mail()` only.
  - `sent()` at `wp_mail_succeeded` keeps the global PHPMailer's `getSentMIMEMessage()` when `From` is the inbox's address. The same works with core `wp_mail()` and with FluentSMTP's, which leaves the raw PHPMailer in the global.
  - At `shutdown`, `flush()` appends the copies.
  - A copy that fails waits in `seoprostack_helpdesk_imap_sent`, which is not autoloaded and holds at most 20 copies and 8 MB; extras are counted as not kept. `retry()`, called by the five-minute run, takes copies out of the queue before appending, so none is saved twice.
- `_Connection`: `folders()` and `append()`, with `\Seen`, the sent time as INTERNALDATE, CRLF line endings and modified UTF-7 folder names.
- Feature: settings `helpdesk_imap_sent` (on by default) and `helpdesk_imap_sent_folder` (empty means the first of Sent, Sent Items, Sent Messages, Sent Mail, INBOX.Sent, INBOX/Sent or [Gmail]/Sent Mail; a folder is never created). Also: boot, run (retry), the settings card and the `status` line.
- `uninstall.php` removes the queue option.
- Version 1.3.120.

Agent and admin notifications, FluentCRM and other site email are not copied, because their From address differs or they don't pass the customer filter. The inbox is still only read.

## Verification

- `bash scripts/lint.sh`: all passed, including phpcs and PHPStan level 8.
- `scripts/preflight-release.sh`: 0 errors. The only warning is the known WordPress.org slug note; readme.txt is 10,174 bytes.
- `scripts/plugin-check.sh`: no errors. None of the warnings are in the changed files.
- Live append check on the owner's support mailbox (Cloudron): a message built by PHPMailer the way `sent()` takes it, not sent to anyone, was appended to Sent with `\Seen`. Sent went from 1 to 2 and INBOX stayed at 0. The message had To and Subject even with PHPMailer's `mail` mailer.
- After release: an agent reply on a test ticket should show up in Sent, with nothing new in INBOX.

Resolves #1084

title: GH#1093: support tickets from site email use the Reply-To person; MainWP Contact Support adds the client's Reply-To; release 1.3.125
body:
Resolves #1093

## Why

Sites send email from their own address: FluentSMTP's Force From Email is on, and Amazon SES needs it. The person who wrote in survives only as Reply-To. Tickets that **Fluent Support email by IMAP** made from these emails therefore belonged to the site, and agent replies went to the site instead of the person. This affected problem reports and MainWP Child's Contact Support form. The owner is routing Contact Support for every site to the WPALLSTARS support desk.

## What

- `includes/class-seoprostack-helpdesk-imap-message.php`: new `sender()`. When the raw header has `Reply-To` with exactly one address, and that address is not the inbox's own (the IMAP user or the business inbox's address), the payload's `from` is the Reply-To address. Otherwise it is From, as before.
  - The header itself is checked because `imap_rfc822_parse_headers()` fills `reply_to` from From when there is no Reply-To. I checked this on the production host's PHP.
  - `payload()` takes the MailBox, passed in from `Reader::process()`. The headers map passed to Fluent Support is unchanged and keeps the original From.
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-fixes.php`: `mainwp_support_reply_to()` on MainWP's `mainwp_child_contact_support_mail_headers` filter.
  - It adds `Reply-To:` with the address the client entered, else the logged-in user's email.
  - It skips when a Reply-To is already present, or when the address is the support address itself.
  - MainWP's settings are untouched.
- Docs: README (IMAP feature section, Fixes for other plugins section, changelog), changelog.txt and readme.txt. Version 1.3.125: rebased onto 1.3.123 (#1088) and 1.3.124 (#1095), which merged while this PR was open.

## Verification

- `bash scripts/lint.sh`: all passed, including phpcs and PHPStan.
- `bash scripts/preflight-release.sh --offline --no-docker`: 0 errors; the one warning is the known WordPress.org slug note. readme.txt is 10,224 bytes.

body:
## What

- **Kadence icon picker draws icons as you scroll or search.** It drew all 5,482 icons (over 22,000 elements) each time it opened. New `admin/js/seoprostack-kadence-icon-picker.js` (loaded by `SEOProStack_Kadence_Library`, setting **Faster editor with Kadence Blocks**) adds a last `kadence.icon_options_names` filter (priority 1000). Scrolling near a set's end adds 300 more by switching the picker's set list to that set and straight back, with `wp.element.flushSync` (or microtasks as a fallback). The set's own icons stay in place, and folded sets and the scroll position are put back.
- **Dev tab: no sideways scrollbar under the sidebar tabs.** `underline()` in `admin/js/seoprostack-editor-dev-tab.js` placed the tab line with `offsetLeft`/`offsetWidth`. Both round to whole pixels, so the line could end up to about 1 px past the Dev tab, and the `overflow-x: auto` tab list then scrolled. On the preview site, 0.6 px was enough to make it scroll. The line now uses `getBoundingClientRect()`, never ends past the Dev tab, and a `ResizeObserver` moves it when the tabs change width.

title: GH#1100: Kadence icon picker opens on press and shows at once; hidden Font Awesome animations no longer slow the editor; release 1.3.127
body:
## Summary

Kadence's icon picker still took a noticeable time to appear after 1.3.124. Profiling the preview site's editor (dark mode, every recommended plugin) found two causes.

1. **The page was slow on every frame, whatever was clicked.** Lasso Lite (Simple URLs 161) loads Font Awesome 5's SVG script on post editor screens. EventON Lite 2.5.10's tooltips (`<em class="evotooltip ajdeToolTip L fa">`) have Font Awesome's `fa` class but no icon, so Font Awesome turns each into its "missing icon", which has four `repeatCount="indefinite"` SVG animations. That makes 550 icons and 2,200 animations, all hidden in EventON's shortcode window. Chrome still ran them on every frame: a trace showed 2,200 `repeatEvent`s and 15,700 style recalculations in 2 s, with idle frames of 40-80 ms. Kadence's 100 ms debounce fired 265 ms late, and React's render waited one more frame.
2. **The picker itself.** It opened on the click (when the button is let go), then waited Kadence's 100 ms debounce, drew 150 icons per set and faded in.

## Changes

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-fixes.php` (Fixes for other plugins, on by default): where `surl-lasso-icons` is enqueued, an inline script after it removes the `animate` elements of Font Awesome SVGs (`svg[data-fa-i2svg] animate`) whenever Font Awesome adds `fontawesome-i2svg-complete` to the html element. The icons stay, still. Font Awesome's own icons have no SVG animations. Its `showMissingIcons` option would not help: an element without an icon name gets the missing icon whatever it says, and for named icons it rejects the whole batch of replacements.
- `admin/js/seoprostack-kadence-icon-picker.js`: opens the picker on mouse `pointerdown` (the trusted click that follows is dropped so it does not close it again). Keys and touch still open it through the click, and a touch can still start a scroll. `FIRST` is now 50 (about a view's worth).
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-kadence-library.php`: `.components-popover.kadence-icon-picker-pop-selection{opacity:1!important}`, so the picker shows at once. WordPress's slide, which carries its position, stays. No frame showed it away from its final place.
- `admin/js/seoprostack-admin-menu.js`: menu fitting's `flush()` walks changed subtrees with a TreeWalker that skips the insides of script-placed elements (inline left/right/inset/transform), instead of checking each of a popover's thousands of elements.
- Release 1.3.127: version, readme, changelogs and README.

## Verification

All on the preview site in dark mode, Kadence Blocks 3.8.0.2 / Pro 2.8.20.1. Press to picker visible in place, measured per frame from the trusted `pointerdown`, eight opens per fresh editor page:

| Variant | Median (range) |
|---|---|
| 1.3.126 | 1,254 ms (1,096-1,328) |
| Hidden animations paused only | 531 ms |
| Picker changes only | 369 ms (204-696) |
| Both | 207 ms (200-211) |

- Enter and Space on the toggle open the picker. A mouse press opens it with 151 icons; scrolling loads more (750); searching "arrow" shows 35; choosing an icon sets the block's `icon` and closes the picker, and it reopens.
- `scripts/lint.sh`: all passed (php js shell workflows phpcs phpstan build).
- `scripts/preflight-release.sh`: see the comment below.

Resolves #1100

title: GH#1129: Dark mode: Kadence typography and colour popovers in the Customizer
body:
Resolves #1129

## What

In Dark mode, the Kadence theme's typography popover in the Customizer (Font, Style and Size of each font setting) and its colour and background pickers opened with a white background.

## Why

Kadence 1.5.2's `inc/customizer/react/build/controls.css` paints `.components-popover.kadence-popover-color .components-popover__content { background: rgb(255, 255, 255) }` at specificity (0,3,0). The typography popover carries that class too. The WordPress components popover rule in `admin/css/seoprostack-whole-theme.css` is (0,2,1), so it lost, and the popovers were dark only where `SEOProStack_Dark_Fallback` had already written its copy of `controls.css` to `uploads/seoprostack-dark/`.

## Change

- `admin/css/seoprostack-whole-theme.css` (Customizer → Kadence's controls): `html.sps-dark .wp-customizer .components-popover.kadence-popover-color .components-popover__content` gets the dark surface and text, plus the same edge and shadow as the WordPress components popover rule.

title: GH#1131: Site templates: split the feature into focused classes
body:
Resolves #1131

## What

Splits the Site templates feature (#1127) into focused classes, with no change in behaviour, so PHP Mess Detector (`phpmd.xml.dist`, which Codacy reads) reports nothing for it. Before: `SEOProStack_Site_Templates` had class complexity 382 with 32 methods, several methods over the cyclomatic and NPath limits, and the WP-CLI class was over them too.

## Change

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-site-templates.php`: keeps settings, scheduling, cron, the public `run()`/`undo()`/`manifests()`/`manifest()` API and constants, and one `locked()` helper for the MySQL advisory lock shared by apply and undo. It loads `includes/site-templates/` only when a template is listed, compared, applied or undone.
- `includes/site-templates/`, one job per class:
  - `manifest`: read, header/section/CSS checks, resources in write order (protected option names still fail at run time, as before).
  - `schema`: keyed items (pages, elements, images, parts) and menus.
  - `run`: site record, batches, cursor, journal (`journal()` then `amend()`, still saved before each write), `finish()`.
  - `parts`, `posts`, `media`, `menus`, `values`: one applier per resource kind, called in the same order as before.
  - `journal`: reads and restores the storage behind each journal entry type.
  - `undo`: identity recovery, preflight of every write before any change, ordered restore with per-write `undone` checkpoints.
- `includes/class-seoprostack-site-templates-cli.php`: the multisite loop (`all_sites`, `visit`, still `restore_current_blog()` in `finally`) is separate from each site's work (`list_templates`, `show_status`, `undo_site`, `run`).
- `changelog.txt`, `README.md`: Developers lines under Unreleased (`changelog.txt` also names the two fixes below).

Two fixes to #1127's unreleased code, from CodeRabbit's review (89e879f5):

- `values`: `apply_css()` checks the owned prefix with `strncmp()`. On PHP 7.4, `strpos()` with an empty needle warns and returns `false`, so a site's first apply reported its empty custom CSS as `edited-on-site` and never wrote the template's CSS.
- `menus`: a menu item's hash is taken from what WordPress stored, not what was written, so a title kses filtered on save (cron and WP-CLI have no user) is not taken for a site edit on the next run.

Otherwise unchanged: the record's layout and hashes on live sites, journal-before-write order, the advisory lock name, undo's preflight, report rows and their order, CLI output and error messages.

## Verification

- PHPMD 3.0.0, `phpmd.xml.dist`, on the feature, the CLI and `includes/site-templates/`: no findings (with a fresh PDepend cache).
- Codacy reports a value equal to the limit, which PHPMD 3 does not, so its first run found three classes at complexity 50 and `merge_leaf()` at 10. Fixed in f721c783: `owned_path()` became `SEOProStack_Site_Template_Run::owns()` (it reads only the run's record), image validation moved to `SEOProStack_Site_Template_Media::item_error()`, the menu item read to the journal, and `merge_leaf()`'s keep-the-site's-value branch to its own helper. PHPMD with thresholds one lower (Codacy-equivalent) reports nothing; the largest class, Run, is at 49. Codacy now passes.
- `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`: all passed.
- Behaviour equivalence on a disposable `scripts/test-site.sh` site, plugin built from each ref by `build-release.sh` (so the new folder ships). The same scenario was run on `main` at 6a4a6e1c and on this branch, starting from the same database snapshot. It covered: ship v1, list, diff, apply, status, record dump, site edits (part, title, menu item, option leaf, theme mod, removed page and option), ship v2 with the version bump through cron batches, status, dump, diff, undo, dump, second undo, invalid slug and other-template errors, `--all-sites` on single site, and the debug log. The outputs are identical except the commit ref and random UUIDs written by an unrelated feature (`_seoprostack_nextgen_generation`), with the part hashes of the markup that holds them; the same lines differ between two runs of `main`. Rerun on f721c783 and 89e879f5, each ref on a fresh site: same result.
- PHP 7.4, same scenario: `main` logs `strpos(): Empty needle` three times and reports `custom_css edited-on-site` throughout; 89e879f5 matches its PHP 8.3 output (`custom_css updated`, empty debug log).
- Multisite (main site plus two subsites), same scenario on both refs: `list`, `status`, `diff` with and without a slug, `apply` and `undo` with `--all-sites`, a second undo stopping at the first failure, and subsites without a record left untouched. Outputs identical apart from the ref, also on f721c783.

title: GH#1135: Dark mode: Kadence typography preview in the Customizer; release 1.3.136
body:
Resolves #1135

## What

In Dark mode, the Kadence theme's typography preview in the Customizer (the arrow beside each font setting, showing "Design is not just what it looks like…") was a harsh checkerboard with the site's text hard to read. This PR fixes it and releases 1.3.136.

## Why

Kadence 1.5.2's `.kadence-preview-font` (`inc/customizer/react/build/controls.css`) draws `#ddd` squares over clear ones, meant for the light Customizer panel. In Dark mode:

- Without the Dark mode fallback's copy of `controls.css`, the clear squares show the near-black panel: a light-and-black grid (the reported screenshot).
- With the copy (the preview site), the `#ddd` squares are darkened to `rgb(44, 51, 56)`: a near-black box.

Either way, the sample uses the site's own text colour (`var(--global-palette3/4/5)`, dark, for light pages), and settings with no colour (Heading Font Family, H1 Title, Breadcrumbs) inherited the panel's light text `rgb(240, 240, 241)`.

## Change

- `admin/css/seoprostack-whole-theme.css` (Customizer → Kadence's controls, after the colour swatch rule): `html.sps-dark .wp-customizer .kadence-preview-font` draws Kadence's own `#ddd` checkerboard on `#fff`, with `color: #1d2327` for settings without a colour. Kadence's inline colour still wins when set. The preview looks as it does in light mode. Specificity (0,3,1) beats Kadence's (0,1,0) and the fallback copy's rule.
- Release 1.3.136: `seoprostack.php` (`Version:`, `SEOPROSTACK_VERSION`), `readme.txt` (`Stable tag:`, changelog), `README.md` (`Version:`, badge via `scripts/readme-badges.sh`, changelog), `changelog.txt`.

## Verification

Preview site (WordPress 7.1, Kadence 1.5.2), Dark mode, signed in with `scripts/preview-browser.sh`, Customizer → Typography, all 10 previews opened, this branch's stylesheet served by Playwright:

- Before: every box had `background-color: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)` and squares `rgb(44, 51, 56)`; 3 had text `rgb(240, 240, 241)`.
- After: every box has `background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255)` with `rgb(221, 221, 221)` squares; the 7 with a palette colour keep it (for example Base Font `rgb(45, 55, 72)` from `var(--global-palette4)`); the 3 without show `rgb(29, 35, 39)`. title: GH#1145: Retry transient cloud storage errors
body:
## Summary

Resolves #1145.

- Retry transient HTTP/S3 failures up to three attempts with jittered backoff inside the batch budget.
- Preserve successful concurrent PUT/HEAD peers, checked payload bytes and existing size/digest removal checks.
- Keep an isolated removal failure local to its attachment; retain the site-wide pause for repeated service errors or configuration/credential failures.
- Document retries and recovery in README.md, readme.txt and changelog.txt.

## Files and reference pattern

Changes are confined to includes/class-seoprostack-s3-client.php, includes/features/class-seoprostack-media-storage.php and the three user docs. Uses the existing byte/concurrency caps and removal deadline handling.

## Runtime Testing

Risk: critical (local file removal). Testing level: runtime-verified.
Final head: ca7df534276ee17b1b79e68f0d3e09f85d3af698.

- `bash scripts/lint.sh`: all passed on final head (PHP/JS syntax, ShellCheck, actionlint, PHPCS, PHPStan; no JS build).
- Disposable WordPress 6.2/PHP 7.4 multisite, temporary subsite, with a localhost-only mock S3 endpoint: imported 120 PNG pictures (360 local files) through WordPress's media APIs, then drained the normal storage batch path in 13 turns. Result: uploaded 120, waiting 0, failed 0, local copies removed 120; every recorded local path absent, storage error empty, no site-wide wait. Rechecked the subsite's normal CLI status after installing final head.
- Single and concurrent PUT/HEAD transient 500s recover. Exact endpoint counters confirm two attempts for recovered failures, one request for healthy peers, three attempts for persistent 503, and one for 403. S3 SlowDown with HTTP 400 recovers too.
- Final-head proxy fallback runtime checks recover from HTTP 429/500/502/503/504 in two attempts each.
- Final-head deadline checks: backoff refuses a sleep with only 0.2 seconds remaining; a 503 followed by a deadline-cut retry retains the original safe HTTP error and healthy peer; a first-attempt-only timeout still yields storage_budget. title: GH#1146: Media in cloud storage remove_local_now(); release 1.3.141
body:
## Summary

Adds public SEOProStack_Media_Storage::remove_local_now($id, $deadline): removes one uploaded attachment's local copies at once with every batch check (removal_record, size/SHA-256, HEAD, public address, generation, changed_meanwhile), under the shared storage lease taken without waiting. Refuses (false, no change) when removal is off/paused, the attachment is not uploaded on this connection, its WebP/AVIF copies are pending (new per-attachment SEOProStack_Nextgen_Images::is_waiting() instead of the library-wide gate), the lease is busy, the deadline passed, or its files were kept. Errors are recorded through local_result(), extracted unchanged from local_step(). README documents the method; keeps the site-wide lease because uploads, watermark jobs and the batch hold only that lease for the same attachment, so a per-attachment lease would not exclude them; removals therefore stay serial site-wide. Also bumps to 1.3.141 (includes #1137, #1140, #1164).



## Files Changed

README.md, changelog.txt, includes/features/class-seoprostack-media-storage.php, includes/features/class-seoprostack-nextgen-images.php, readme.txt, seoprostack.php

## Decisions

Kept the site-wide lease (documented: throughput stays serial for removals, but each import slot removes its own pictures immediately instead of waiting for the newest-first batch). Retryable error marks only this picture kept, as the batch does for an isolated failure.

## Runtime Testing

body:
## Summary

Resolves #1184. Resolves #1187. Supersedes #1185 (its three removal-batching commits are included). #1183: upload_locked() is split into prepare/stage/settle/finish driven by upload_many(): up to seoprostack_media_storage_parallel_pictures (default 5) pictures prepare and claim keys alone, then each round sends a group from every picture that fits seoprostack_media_storage_batch_requests (default min(64, 4x concurrency)) and the group byte cap; each picture settles with its own results. Kept originals go up in one PUT phase and are read back in one GET phase (new SEOProStack_S3_Client::confirm_files()); finish_original() skips its second read-back when the bytes were confirmed in this request under the same lock. Remove local copies runs shared HEAD phases bounded by the same request count, repeating within its half budget. Retry jobs and WP-CLI --retry-failed use the same path. #1184: request_multiple_once() uses the client's own curl multi loop with curl_multi_select() (10 ms pause on -1), kept open per client for connection reuse, empty Expect header; same signing, CA bundle, no redirects, http(s) only, timeouts and 16 MiB + 1 limit; Requests remains the fallback, proxies keep the WordPress HTTP API. #1187: the six functions SonarCloud flagged (php:S3776) are split into private helpers with no change in behaviour: curl_multiple() into curl_wait() and curl_read_done(); remove_locals() into removal_phase() and removal_result(); upload_originals() into original_sort() and original_sent(); upload_many() into upload_prepare_many(), upload_round(), upload_join() and upload_end(); upload_prepare() into upload_visit_handover() and upload_original_only(); upload_settle() takes group_error(). title: GH#1193: Keep recommended settings
body:
## What

**Keep recommended settings**: a child of Plugin presets (Plugins tab), off by default, so a site (or every site of a network, from Network Admin) keeps SEO Pro Stack's plugin presets and its own on-by-default features without anyone applying them by hand, and picks up later releases' changes to them. Settings someone changes by hand stay as they set them.

Resolves #1193

## How

- `includes/class-seoprostack-presets-keep.php` (new): WP-Cron `seoprostack_keep_settings` a minute after the switch goes on (`seoprostack_settings_changed`), after `seoprostack_page_cache_purge` (each SEO Pro Stack update) and after `activated_plugin` for a plugin with a preset, plus `seoprostack_keep_settings_daily`. A run on a request where Load plugins only where needed skipped plugins waits for the next. For each active plugin with a preset (here or network-wide), the differing paths go through `SEOProStack_Presets::write($slug, 'options', $paths)`, so the plugin's save code, the undo copy and `seoprostack_plugin_preset_changed` all run. The value written to each path is remembered in `seoprostack_presets_kept` (not autoloaded); a path whose stored value no longer matches was changed by hand and is left alone.
- Presets take a `manual` list (setting paths or option names; a path covers its children) that waits for Apply preset. Marked at the owner's choice: AI Engine's chatbot, Turnstile on Fluent Forms, Readabler's button and popup, Tutor LMS course rules (not `enable_gutenberg_course_edit`), Rank Math page schema, WooCommerce Order attribution. `scripts/preflight-plugin.sh` fails on a `manual` entry the preset does not set.
- `includes/class-seoprostack-defaults-keep.php` (new): remembers each own setting's default in `seoprostack_defaults_kept`. When a default changes, a setting still at the old one gets the new one. The first run switches on bool settings that default to on but are off (features made on by default after the site was set up). Network-enforced settings are skipped.
- `SEOProStack_Presets::paths()` (every path a preset sets, stored and wanted) and a public `same()`. WP-CLI: `wp seoprostack presets keep [--dry-run]`. Plugin deactivation clears both hooks; uninstall removes both options and hooks.

title: GH#1194: Load the CSS each page uses first; release 1.3.145
body:
## What

**Load the CSS each page uses first** (Speed tab, off by default) works only with the Kadence theme, Kadence Blocks (Pro), Kadence Pro, Fluent Forms (Pro) and WordPress's block library. For those, each page gets the CSS rules it uses inline, where each stylesheet link was. The full stylesheet then loads without holding up the first paint. The site's own server does all the work, with no cloud service or licence. FlyingPress 5 and LiteSpeed's UCSS both need one. This is a narrow exception, approved by the owner, to the no-CSS-optimisation rule in `AGENTS.md`.

This PR also releases **1.3.145**: the version bump, with #1192 (Keep pages cached, PR #1195), #1193 (Keep recommended settings, PR #1198), #1197 (network cache fills, PR #1200) and #1194.

Resolves #1194

## How

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-used-css.php`:
  - Settings: `used_css`, plus two troubleshooting lists, `used_css_exclude` and `used_css_keep`.
  - When it runs: GET requests to front-end pages from people who are not logged in. It skips previews, the Customizer, feeds, embeds, robots.txt, AJAX, REST, JSON, AMP and any listed pages.
  - An output buffer on `template_redirect` at priority `PHP_INT_MAX`.
  - It steps aside where LiteSpeed Cache combines CSS or makes UCSS or critical CSS.
  - Changing any of its settings calls the new `SEOProStack_Page_Cache::purge_all()`, and turning it off removes its cache.
  - It provides the Recommended speed settings entry (`plan()`).
- `includes/class-seoprostack-used-css-page.php`: rewrites one page. Each handled `<link>` becomes a `<style id="{id}-used">` with the used rules, in the link's place so the cascade is unchanged. After it come the link, with `media="print"` switched back on load, and a `<noscript>` copy.
- `includes/class-seoprostack-used-css-links.php`: chooses the links to handle. Each must be plain, render-blocking, local and inside a supported folder (filter `seoprostack_used_css_sources`, unsupported), and not on the keep list.
- `includes/class-seoprostack-used-css-match.php`: counts a rule as used when the page has every class, ID and element named in one of its selectors. This is an allowlist of selectors, not a list of whole stylesheets to leave out:
  - Classes that the Kadence, Kadence Blocks, Kadence Pro and Fluent Forms scripts add after load count as present. So do those from intl-tel-input, Choices and flatpickr.
  - The list is in `CLASSES`; filter `seoprostack_used_css_classes` adds to it.
- `includes/class-seoprostack-used-css-parser.php`, `-selector.php` and `-sheet.php`: parse each stylesheet once for each path, size, modified time and folder. The limit is 1 MB per stylesheet.
  - Each result is saved to `uploads/seoprostack-used-css/*.json` through a temporary file that is then renamed.
  - Rules inside `@media`, `@supports`, `@container`, `@layer` and `@scope` are filtered too.
  - Other at-rules are kept, except `@charset`, and relative `url()`s are made absolute.
- Uninstall and deactivation remove the folder. Docs: `README.md`, `readme.txt`, `changelog.txt`, `AGENTS.md`.
- Release 1.3.145:
  - `seoprostack.php` (`Version:` and `SEOPROSTACK_VERSION`), `readme.txt` (`Stable tag:` and the changelog) and `README.md` (`Version:`, the badges and the changelog).
  - In `changelog.txt`, the Unreleased section is now 1.3.145.
  - `readme.txt` is 10,179 bytes, under the 10 KB limit. Its 1.3.145 notes are short; `changelog.txt` and `README.md` have them in full.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh`: everything passed (php, js, shell, workflows, phpcs, phpstan).
- PHPMD (`phpmd.xml.dist`) is clean on all seven Used CSS files. `class-seoprostack-speed-plan.php` changes by one line, and its existing PHPMD findings are the same as on `main`.
- Disposable site (`scripts/test-site.sh`): PHP 8.3, Kadence, Kadence Blocks, Fluent Forms and WP-Optimize's page cache. The test page has Kadence's header, Kadence Blocks rows, tabs and an accordion, and a Fluent Forms form.
  - Render-blocking stylesheets: 11 before, none after. 41.0 KB of their 187.7 KB is inlined.
  - Median first paint under mobile throttling: 1,048 ms before, 824 ms after.
  - Parsing all 11 stylesheets the first time took 10.1 ms. With the cache files, each page after that took 5.4 ms.
  - Playwright screenshots of 9 states, on desktop and mobile: the top of the page, tabs, the accordion, form errors, the submenu and the mobile drawer. All 18 shots match the reference with the feature off. Some runs blocked the full stylesheets, so only the inlined CSS applied, and they matched too.
  - Splitting the classes for PHPMD left the rendered page the same, byte for byte, apart from a script version timestamp. The test used a fresh cache and a purged page cache. 11 cache files were written, no temporary files were left over, and the debug log is empty.
- The 10 CodeRabbit findings fixed in `1be93572` and `83d0ed30` were checked against 281 stylesheets and 52 link tags. The reply explains the 2 findings left as they are: https://github.com/wpallstars/seoprostack/pull/1199#issuecomment-6623255274

title: GH#1202: Keep pages cached gets past LiteSpeed's bot protection and delivers waiting purges; release 1.3.146
body:
## Summary

Keep pages cached (#1192) on LiteSpeed servers with the host's bot protection on, and release 1.3.146.

- **Fill requests as LiteSpeed Cache's crawler.** On a LiteSpeed page cache, `SEOProStack_Keep_Cached_Requests::open()` puts `lscache_runner ` (`SEOProStack_Litespeed::CRAWLER_AGENT`, as `\LiteSpeed\Crawler::FAST_USER_AGENT`) before its desktop and phone user agents. LiteSpeed's reCAPTCHA protection lets it through, and LiteSpeed Cache leaves the vary alone for it (`\LiteSpeed\Vary::can_change_vary()`). LiteSpeed answers `201` without a body for pages it holds (shown as `201 hit`); on `428` (crawler turned off by the host) the plain agent is used for the rest of the run.
- **Deliver waiting purges.** New `SEOProStack_Litespeed::deliver_purge()`: from the command line (WP-CLI, or a host cron job running `wp-cron.php`), when `litespeed.purge.queue`/`queue2` still holds a purge (read with `$wpdb`: autoloaded, changed by another process), it opens `admin-ajax.php` as the crawler, through Server IP when set. LiteSpeed Cache's own `kick_purge_queue()` uses WordPress's user agent and counts a 403 as delivered. Runs at shutdown (priority 20, after LiteSpeed Cache's at 0), before each batch on a LiteSpeed page cache, and before `wp seoprostack keep-cached`.
- **Back off when refused.** A batch stops at the first page answered 403, 429 or 503, or before opening any while a purge still waits. The refused page goes to the end of the queue, the next batch waits a minute longer for each stop in a row, and after 5 the queue is cleared (`…_last` records `stopped`) and LiteSpeed Cache's crawler is started where it is on.
- Changelog also lists #1188 (merged in #1190 after 1.3.145).

Not changed, unlike the issue's list: `SEOProStack_Litespeed_Crawler::reaches_server()`. It already counts any 2xx–4xx answer from LiteSpeed as reaching the server, so a challenge (403) does not fail it.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh`: all passed (php, js, shell, workflows, phpcs, phpstan, build).
- `scripts/preflight-release.sh --offline`: 0 errors, 1 warning (the usual WordPress.org slug note).
- On the pilot Hostinger site (LiteSpeed Enterprise, Cloudflare in front), with these files in place of 1.3.145's:
  - Stored a purge with both shutdown deliveries removed, then called `deliver_purge()`: delivered in 1.05 s, queue `-1`; the home page then answered `200` (rebuilt), then `201`.
  - `wp seoprostack keep-cached` after a purge: `200 miss | 200 miss` for each page (desktop | phone), `301` for redirects; a second run `201 | 201`. Then a desktop and a phone visitor both got `x-litespeed-cache: hit`, so the crawler's copies serve visitors.
  - WP-Cron path: `litespeed_purge_all` from WP-CLI, then `wp cron event run --due-now` after 90 s: the batch ran 21 s, the next host cron batch finished the fill: `{"opened":20,"stopped":false}`.
  - Backoff on an idle queue with `wp eval-file`: stops 1–5 rescheduled at 60, 120, 180, 240 and 300 s with the refused page moved last; the 6th cleared the queue with `"stopped":true`; a stopped batch that opened a page counts as stop 1.

Resolves #1202

title: GH#1207: deliver a LiteSpeed purge a timed-out request took
body:
## Summary

On a busy LiteSpeed server, a purge made from WP-CLI or a host's cron job could be lost. LiteSpeed Cache delivers it with a request to `admin-ajax.php` that gives up after WordPress's 5 seconds. The page load takes the purge from the queue (sets it to `-1`) before it answers. So when the client gives up, the server never applies the purge, and the queue is also empty for SEO Pro Stack's 1.3.146 fallback.

In `includes/class-seoprostack-litespeed.php` (command line only):

- `delivery_args()` (`http_request_args`) handles a request to `admin-ajax.php` that sets out while a purge waits. It records the queue values the request carries in the request's `seoprostack_delivers_purge` argument, holds each one as an `[option, value]` pair, and raises the request's timeout to `DELIVER_TIMEOUT` (30 s). This covers LiteSpeed Cache's own `kick_purge_queue()`.
- `delivery_answered()` (`http_api_debug`): an answer below 500 clears only the pairs that request carried, so a purge an earlier request lost stays held. No answer, a 5xx, or a pair still held marks the site failed. A request that set out with no purge does not count (after a lost purge, LiteSpeed Cache sends a second request, which answers `400` without it).
- `deliver_purge()`: when the queue is empty but a purge is still held, `store_again()` writes it back, then delivers it as the crawler. The write is a compare-and-swap `UPDATE` that only succeeds while the row is still `''` or `-1`, followed by clearing the option's and `alloptions`' caches. If the crawler request answers but carried only a newer purge, it sends once more straight away. If a request gets no answer, the purge is stored again for the next request.
- `queued()` replaces the old `purge_waiting()` query and returns the waiting values.

Docs: README (Keep pages cached, Unreleased changelog), changelog.txt (Unreleased).

### Review fixes (CodeRabbit)

1. A newer purge in the other queue option, carried alone by the next request, cleared the lost purge too (f19a7515). Fixed with the per-request carried values and the `[option, value]` pairs, which also cover a newer purge in the same option.
2. `store_again()` read the queue and then wrote it with `update_option()`, so a purge stored in between could be overwritten (563c2ec5). Fixed with the compare-and-swap write.

## Evidence (Hostinger, LiteSpeed Cache 7.9.2, load average 16 to 18)

Before (1.3.146): `wp litespeed-purge all` said "Could not notify the web server to purge." in 3 runs of 4, and the home page stayed `x-litespeed-cache: hit` with old content. In a probe, LiteSpeed's own delivery timed out at 5.02 s with the queue emptied and the page still cached. With a 30 s timeout it answered `400` after 5.59 s and the page was purged.

After (this branch on the same Hostinger site):

| Run | LiteSpeed's request | SEO Pro Stack | Page after |
|---|---|---|---|
| plain `wp litespeed-purge all` (x4) | answered, "Purge all sent" | nothing extra | `miss` |
| probe: LiteSpeed's request cut to 1 s | timed out, queue `-1`; then a second request with no purge (`400`) | stored again, crawler request `400` | `miss` |
| race probe: 1 s timeout, then a harmless purge stored in `queue2` | timed out; its second request carried only `queue2` (`400`) | purge-all stored again, crawler request `400` | `miss` (before the review fix: `hit`) |

No PHP messages in the site's `error_log`.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh`: all passed (php, js, shell, workflows, phpcs, phpstan), after each commit.
- Runtime: as in the table above.

Resolves #1207

title: GH#1204: Kadence Blocks hero backgrounds load first, as AVIF or WebP; release 1.3.147
body:
## Summary

Kadence Blocks hero backgrounds load with the page, as their AVIF or WebP copy, and release 1.3.147. The release also includes #1207 (merged in #1209) and #1201 (merged in #1213 while this PR was open; merged in from `main` here).

- **Preload** (`includes/features/class-seoprostack-image-loading.php`, `kadence_preload()` at `wp_head` priority -10, so it comes before other plugins' inline styles and scripts). This applies when a singular post or page's content opens with a `kadence/rowlayout` block (kbVersion 2) with a background picture (normal tab, not parallax) or a background slider (its first slide). It prints `<link rel="preload" as="image" … fetchpriority="high">`, naming the AVIF copy (else WebP) with its `type` when pages name copies. That picture takes the page's one high fetch priority, so core no longer gives it to the header logo. It also counts as the first picture of **Load straight away**. Rows hidden on a device, with a tablet or phone background, or with a dynamic background are left alone, so no device fetches a picture it does not show. Posts whose featured image the theme shows are left alone too (`feature_shown()`), as that picture comes before the content and keeps core's high priority.
- **`image-set()`** (`includes/features/class-seoprostack-nextgen-images.php`, with **Copies at their own addresses** on). After each `background-image: url(…)` of an uploads picture that has a copy, a second `background-image: image-set(url(….avif) type('image/avif'), url(….webp) type('image/webp'), url(…))` follows, keeping `!important`. Browsers without `image-set()` or `type()` drop that declaration and keep the `url()`. This covers Kadence Blocks' slider slides and inline row styles (`kadence_blocks_row_slider_attrs`, `kadence_blocks_row_wrapper_args`), the CSS Kadence prints before a row or column (`render_block_kadence/rowlayout`, `render_block_kadence/column`), and its head block CSS (`kadence_blocks_css` inline data, at `wp_print_styles`). Addresses with quotes, brackets, spaces or backslashes are skipped; a second run changes nothing. `copy_url()` is split out of the `<source>` builder and shared.
- Version 1.3.147 in `seoprostack.php`, `readme.txt`, `README.md` (and badges); the changelogs' Unreleased section renamed, with #1204 added.

Not done, from the issue's optional item: a smaller picture for phones. `image-set()` picks by resolution, not width. At Lighthouse's 1.75 DPR it would still take the large copy, and for 3x phones a smaller copy risks a blurred hero, so it is not cheap or safe.

## Evidence (pilot site: Kadence, Kadence Blocks, Fluent Forms, LiteSpeed; PageSpeed mobile)

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Slider picture | 565 KB JPEG at High priority, found after the CSS (~670 ms), plus its 235 KB AVIF from a cover block | 235 KB AVIF, fetched once at High priority (~300–420 ms); no JPEG |
| LCP (Lighthouse) | 8.7–8.9 s | 5.8–6.5 s |
| Score | 74–75 | 77–78 |
| CLS | 0 | 0 |

The first-screen screenshots before and after are identical. The observed LCP is about 1.0–1.2 s in both. Lighthouse's simulated LCP also charges bytes that start before it. Most of what is left is two Cloudflare Turnstile challenges (about 213 KB each) from the two Fluent Forms lower down: filed as #1210. The rest is lazy pictures within Chrome's loading distance, which the browser fetches anyway.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh`: all passed (php, js, shell, workflows, phpcs, phpstan), after each commit and after the merge from `main`.
- `scripts/preflight-release.sh --no-docker`: 0 errors, 2 warnings. Both warnings were already on `main`: the WordPress.org slug note, and two core files (`scripts/lib/docker-wordpress.sh`, `scripts/replaced-plugins.php`) that differ from the starter. This PR does not touch those files. Both zips build with one `seoprostack/` folder and pass PHP and JS syntax checks.
- Live HTML on the pilot: the slide's `style` has the `image-set()` declaration after the `url()`; there is one `<link rel="preload" as="image" … type="image/avif" fetchpriority="high">` before the other head output; the first two content pictures are eager and the third is `loading="lazy"`.
- `scripts/plugin-check.sh` (on `feb64ea9`): no errors in either zip. The GitHub zip's updater findings are expected; the warnings are in files this PR does not touch.
- Second commit (`23fed878`), for SonarCloud's three findings on the new code. These were the cognitive complexity of `kadence_background()` (26) and `image_set()` (17), and the regex complexity of the `css_image_sets()` pattern (29). Behaviour is the same:
  - `kadence_row_everywhere()` and `kadence_row_picture()` split the row check from its picture.
  - `first_copy()` and `image_set()` share `css_copies()`.
  - The pattern's two lookaheads are checked at the match's offset (`PREG_OFFSET_CAPTURE`, PHP 7.4+): the declaration must end there, with no `image-set()` after it already.
  - A throwaway PHP probe loaded the old (`b51c360a`) and new code side by side and found no differences. It covered 54 CSS cases (quotes, `!important`, `}` or the end of the text, lists, values after the picture, no copy, a WebP-only copy, unusable addresses, an existing `image-set()`; each with Copies at their own addresses on and off, and run twice), 14 `first_copy()` cases and 34 row shapes (hidden or per-device backgrounds, dynamic, parallax, slider counts, other tabs, bad or relative addresses). `scripts/lint.sh` passed again.
- Third commit (`feb64ea9`), for CodeRabbit's review (replies: https://github.com/wpallstars/seoprostack/pull/1212#issuecomment-6628434060). `feature_shown()` checks `has_post_thumbnail()` and, with the Kadence theme, `\Kadence\kadence()->show_feature()`, the setting Kadence 1.5.2's `single-entry.php` uses. Run inside a real singular query on the pilot, the front page (thumbnail set, but hidden by Kadence) keeps the preload, and the newest post (featured image shown) skips it. The docs now say "AVIF, else WebP", and that a header picture with its own `fetchpriority="high"` keeps it.
- Merge from `main` (`787349c3`): #1201's Unreleased changelog entries go into 1.3.147 in `README.md` and `changelog.txt`. `readme.txt` gets a #1201 line, and its #1204 line is shortened so the file stays under 10 KB.

Resolves #1204
