title: GH#1210: load Fluent Forms' Turnstile when a form comes near; release 1.3.148
body:
## Summary

New Speed setting, on by default: **Load Fluent Forms' Turnstile when a form comes near** (`includes/features/class-seoprostack-fluentforms-turnstile.php`, registered in `SEOProStack_Setup`). `script_loader_tag` replaces Fluent Forms' own `turnstile` tag (Turnstile's explicit-render `/turnstile/v0/api.js`, registered with `FLUENTFORM_VERSION`, Fluent Forms 6.2.17 or later; the address is printed unchanged, so the match uses path, handle and version, not the host, which Plugin Check's `OffloadedContent` flags as a literal) with an inline script that adds the same `api.js` once a `.ff-el-turnstile` widget comes within 600 px of the viewport (`IntersectionObserver`, which also covers modals and hidden steps) or a field in a form with a widget gets focus. Without widgets or `IntersectionObserver` it loads at once. Fluent Forms 6.2.17's `form-submission.js` waits for a late `turnstile.render`, so it renders the widgets itself. Conversational forms (`turnstile_conv`), older versions and other plugins' Turnstile are left alone. Recommended speed settings lists it where Fluent Forms is active.

**Release 1.3.148** (second commit): version in `seoprostack.php`, `readme.txt` and `README.md`, badges, and the changelogs. The release also includes two worker fixes already on `main` that had no changelog entries: #1208 (merged in #1214) and #1211 (merged in #1215).

## Files Changed

`README.md`, `changelog.txt`, `readme.txt`, `seoprostack.php`, `includes/class-seoprostack-setup.php`, `includes/features/class-seoprostack-fluentforms-turnstile.php`, `includes/features/class-seoprostack-speed-plan.php`

## Decisions

Default on: it only changes when a third-party challenge loads, and Fluent Forms' own retry covers an early submit. The 600 px margin starts the load about a screen ahead, so the token is usually ready when the visitor reaches the form. Scoped to Fluent Forms' standard handle and version so no other plugin's Turnstile is touched, per the owner's low-support rule.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium
- **Verification:** runtime-verified on a disposable site (WordPress 7.1.4, PHP 8.3, Kadence 1.5.2, Fluent Forms 6.2.17, Cloudflare's always-pass test keys, two forms with Turnstile auto-included).

  - Playwright: scrolling to the form loaded `api.js` within 20 ms and gave a token in about 1.9 s; a form in the first screen loaded at about 90 ms; a closed modal loaded nothing until opened; Tab into a form far down loaded on focus; every form submitted successfully; submitting before a token got Fluent Forms' own "Turnstile verification failed, please try again." and the next submit succeeded.
  - Speed plan: `on` when on, `recommended` when off, rendered by name on the Speed tab.

title: GH#1220: claim new uploads from insertion until their mark
body:
## Summary

**Mark new uploads** now claims a new upload as soon as it is inserted, not only once its sizes are made, so a storage (or WebP/AVIF) batch in another process cannot copy its files while they are being written and marked.

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-watermark-images.php`
  - `claim_upload()` on `add_attachment`: claims the upload (`_seoprostack_watermark_claim`, the per-picture claim from #1196) before `wp_create_image_subsizes()` runs. WordPress saves the attachment's metadata after each size it makes, so before this a storage batch could reach the upload before `wp_generate_attachment_metadata` fired.
  - `after_generate()` wraps the old body (now `generated()`) and ends that claim in `finally`, marked, left alone or failed. The inline mark takes its own claim first, then drops the insertion claim, so the picture is never unclaimed in between. The claim also ends when the same request inserts another upload, or at `shutdown`; one left by a PHP that stopped expires (600 s).
  - `claim_next()` / `part_step()`: a running batch that reaches a picture claimed by its own upload request takes it with no claim token and counts it as left alone, instead of failing it with `watermark_busy`.
  - Not for uploads the browser processes (WordPress 7.1, marked at finalize), sizes this class regenerates itself, or files that cannot be marked.
- `changelog.txt`, `readme.txt`, `README.md`: 1.3.149 entries.

This follows option 2's goal from the issue (the barrier holds with no job open) by using the claim that #1196 added instead of the queued meta, and with no wait on the lease.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium (media pipeline concurrency)
- **Verification:** runtime-verified on a disposable site: WordPress 7.1.4, PHP 8.3, Imagick, a MinIO bucket on the site's Docker network, WP cron off, Watermark pictures (image mark), Mark new uploads, Media in cloud storage and WebP/AVIF on.
  - 50 generated 2400×1600 JPEGs imported with `media_handle_sideload()` (what `wp media import` uses) while another process ran `SEOProStack_Media_Storage::run_batch(25)` back to back, no watermark batch open.
  - `origin/main` (1.3.149 before this change): **366 upload attempts** for the 50 pictures: batches took each upload while its sizes and mark were still being written, then again after each change.
  - This branch: **52 and 56 attempts** in two runs.
  - Every run: all 50 pictures `uploaded` and marked, no failure or `storage_changed`, and each recorded file digest matches the marked file on disk. Locally the copy takes milliseconds, so main's extra attempts converge; across a WAN to R2 the same overlap gave the `storage_changed` failures in the issue.
  - With a Mark every picture batch open (60 unmarked pictures) while 30 more were imported with Mark new uploads on and storage batches ran back to back: the batch reached one of the new uploads while its own request held it and counted it left alone (`skipped` 2: that one and the watermark picture itself); `failed` 0, no `watermark_busy`. All 90 ended uploaded and marked, digests matching.
  - A test must-use plugin logged every `_seoprostack_storage_state = uploaded` write with whether the picture had its watermark record at that moment: across all runs, no import picture was uploaded before its mark (the only unmarked one was the watermark picture itself, which is never marked).
- `scripts/lint.sh`: all passed (php, js, shell, workflows, phpcs, phpstan), again after merging `main` (#1218's changelog entries; `readme.txt`'s three 1.3.149 lines shortened to stay under 10 KB: 10230 bytes).

## Release gates (1.3.149, this branch at `f618538c`)

This is the last change for 1.3.149 (#1196, #1218, #1220); the version is already 1.3.149 on `main`.

- `scripts/preflight-release.sh`: 0 errors, 2 warnings, both already there in 1.3.148 (the WordPress.org slug from the plugin name; two core files that differ from the starter).
- `scripts/plugin-check.sh`: no errors in either zip; only the updater items expected in the GitHub zip and the existing warnings.

title: GH#1223: remove many pictures' local copies in one pass
body:
## Summary

Plugins that import pictures with WP-Cron off (SEO Pro Directory's import pump) can now remove many uploaded pictures' local copies in one call, instead of one `remove_local_now()` call per picture, each with its own bucket round trip and page purge.

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-media-storage.php`
  - New public `SEOProStack_Media_Storage::remove_local_many(array $ids, float $deadline): array`. It takes the storage lease once and runs `remove_local_now()`'s checks on each picture (`remove_now_ready()`: uploaded, removal record, not waiting for WebP/AVIF, `kept:`). It then checks whole pictures' files in shared HEAD phases (`remove_now_phases()` → `removal_phase()` / `removal_result()`, the same helpers the batch's `remove_locals()` uses), confirms and removes each picture whole, and purges pages once in `finally`.
  - Returns `ID => true|false|WP_Error` with `remove_local_now()`'s meaning. A picture it does not reach (lease busy, deadline, a retryable service error in a phase, removal paused for an hour after another service error) answers `false`.
  - `remove_local_now($id, $deadline)` is now `remove_local_many(array($id), $deadline)[$id]`.
  - `head_requests()`: removal HEAD phases (the batch's included) send up to twice `seoprostack_media_storage_batch_requests` (default 64), at most 128, because a HEAD carries no body. This doubled the far-bucket gain in testing (below).
- `includes/class-seoprostack-s3-client.php` `heads()`: as `put_files()` already does, a HEAD still running when a group given less than 20 s reaches the caller's deadline answers `storage_budget` (try next turn), not `storage_transport`. A long call's last phase then does not count as a service failure.
- `README.md` (Media in cloud storage developer notes, Unreleased changelog), `changelog.txt`, `readme.txt`: Unreleased entries.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium (deletes local media files; safety checks unchanged)
- **Verification:** runtime-verified on a disposable site: WordPress latest, PHP 8.3, a MinIO bucket on the site's Docker network, WP-Cron off, two sets of 300 uploaded pictures (14.8 files each), Remove local copies on. Latency was added to MinIO with `tc netem`.
  - **Issue acceptance (≥5×), 1.2 s added per round trip, 60 s each:** `origin/main`'s `remove_local_now()` back to back removed **22** pictures (0.37/s, 22 purges). One `remove_local_many()` call removed **152** (2.53/s, **6.9×**, **1 purge**), and the other 148 answered `false` at the deadline.
  - With 150 ms added: 155 against all 300 in 41 s (2.8×). Here the local work dominates (each file's SHA-256 checked twice and its removal recorded before it goes), and that work is unchanged on purpose. HEAD phases of 128 took the same ~160 ms as phases of 15 (probe of `heads()` at 15/32/64/128 keys).
  - **Mismatch safety:** five pictures (two untouched, one local file changed, one bucket copy replaced, one bucket copy deleted) got identical answers from `origin/main`'s `remove_local_now()` loop and from one `remove_local_many()` call: `true`, `true`, `storage_kept` (kept), `storage_kept` (kept), `storage_http` 404 (not kept, removal paused for an hour). Every file of the last three was left in place. Purge actions: 2 on main, 1 on this branch.
  - The delegating `remove_local_now()` on this branch: three fresh pictures removed, `true` each in about 60 ms, one purge per call; an already-removed picture answers `true`; a past deadline gives `false`.
  - After review (831a1a44): every given ID answers, an invalid one `false` (`remove_local_many(array(0, -3, 'x', 603, 604))` gave `0`/`-3` `false`, both pictures `true`); the readiness loop stops at the deadline; docs give the real HEAD group size. Main (GH#1224) merged in; the Unreleased entries keep both.
- `php -l` and `vendor/bin/phpcs` on both changed files: clean. `scripts/lint.sh phpstan`: passed.

Release: this goes out with #1221 as 1.3.150 (authorised in the session); no version change in this PR.

Resolves #1223

title: GH#1224: Keep pages cached fills header, footer, home page links, then the rest
body:
## Summary

**Keep pages cached** now fills the page cache in the order visitors reach pages, which is the owner's order: header menu, footer menu, home page links, then the rest of the site. Where no crawler covers the rest, it opens the rest itself.

- `includes/class-seoprostack-keep-cached-pages.php`
  - `of_site()` order: home page; the header's menu locations, then the links inside the site's header; the footer's menu locations, then the links inside its footer; the home page's other links, in document order; the posts page; then the rest.
  - `menu_urls()` splits locations by slug (contains `footer` → footer) and orders them as the theme registers them (Kadence: primary, secondary, mobile, footer), not as `get_nav_menu_locations()` stores them.
  - `page_links()` reads the home page once per fill and walks it with `WP_HTML_Tag_Processor`. The site's header and footer are a header/footer element with `id="masthead"` / `"colophon"`, or the class `site-header` / `site-footer` / `wp-block-template-part` (block themes). Links are made absolute; `clean()` still keeps only this site's cacheable pages.
  - `rest_urls()` / `permalinks()`: published pages, then posts, then other viewable public types, newest first. These read only the columns permalinks use, so up to 1,000 posts' content is not loaded (0.9 MB against 64.5 MB in the test below).
  - `MAIN_MAX` 20 → 50. `MORE_MAX` (50) is gone: without a crawler the fill goes up to the queue's `MAX` (1,000). A network fill keeps 10/25 per site and does not read home pages.
- `includes/class-seoprostack-keep-cached-requests.php` `page_html()`: fetches a page the way `open()` does. On LiteSpeed it sends LiteSpeed Cache's crawler user agent first, then asks again as a visitor when LiteSpeed answers 201. Responses are capped at 4 MB. `request()` is shared with `get()`.
- `includes/class-seoprostack-keep-cached-queue.php`, `includes/features/class-seoprostack-keep-pages-cached.php`: WP-Optimize's preload (`wpo_page_cache_run_preload`) is no longer scheduled 30 s after its purge, where it competed with the fill. `fill_later()` marks the queue, and `done()` schedules the preload when the fill ends, as it starts LiteSpeed Cache's crawler. The setting description is updated.
- `includes/class-seoprostack-keep-cached-cli.php`: `--dry-run` notes that it opens only the home page, to read its links.
- `README.md` (Keep pages cached section, Unreleased changelog), `changelog.txt`, `readme.txt`.

Two differences from the issue's proposal:
- The posts page comes after the home page's links, to keep the owner's order strictly.
- With a crawler or preload on, the list still fills up to 50 with the newest pages and posts, as before, rather than stopping after the home page's links; the crawler or preload follows.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Low-medium (background WP-Cron requests to the site's own pages; no content changes)
- **Verification:** runtime-verified on a disposable site: WordPress 7.1.4, PHP 8.3, Kadence 1.5.2, WP-Optimize 4.7.0 page cache, WP-Cron off. Setup:
  - header menu in `primary` and footer menu in `footer`, stored footer first;
  - a Kadence header HTML item and footer HTML, each linking to a page in no menu;
  - home page links to a page, a post, a page already in the menu, `#top`, another host, a search, `/wp-login.php` and a relative address.

  A test must-use plugin pointed the site's published port at its web container.
  - `wp seoprostack keep-cached --dry-run`: `/`, the three header menu pages, the header's link, the two footer menu pages, the footer's link, the home page's three new links, `/blog/`, then the other pages and posts newest first. Each appeared once, with no query string, login page, fragment-only link or other host.
  - Preload off: a WP-Optimize purge, then one batch, opened all 19 pages in that order, and the cache folder held them (38 files). Preload on: `wpo_page_cache_run_preload` was not scheduled at the purge and was scheduled when the batch emptied the queue.
  - With 1,100 more posts of about 30 KB: the list without preload held 1,000 addresses, worked out in 61 ms and +0.9 MB (`get_posts()` whole for `get_permalink()`: +64.5 MB). With preload on: 50.
  - Twenty Twenty-Five (block theme): header and footer template parts were read as header and footer.
  - Debug log: no messages.
- `php -l` and `vendor/bin/phpcs` on all changed files: clean. `scripts/lint.sh phpstan`: passed.

Resolves #1224

title: GH#1221: Kadence hero background at the size each screen needs; release 1.3.150
body:
## What and why

A Kadence Blocks row names one background picture, often the full upload, so phones fetched it too, and on a hero row that is the page's first paint (LCP). Image loading now gives the background picture of the row a page opens with at the size each screen needs, never less sharp than before (owner's rule).

- `includes/class-seoprostack-kadence-hero.php` (`SEOProStack_Kadence_Hero`), started from `SEOProStack_Image_Loading::kadence_preload()` for the row it already picks. `includes/class-seoprostack-hero-picture.php` (`SEOProStack_Hero_Picture`) lists the picture's files: its WordPress sizes of the same proportions whose file is here, or in cloud storage when Media in cloud storage serves it, then the row's own picture; only when the row's address is in that attachment's folder.
- The head gets a style hiding only that row's background while the page loads, the old preload inside `<noscript>`, and the files. A script right after the row measures it, picks the smallest copy at least as wide as the pixels painted (cover: max of width and height × proportions; contain: min; × devicePixelRatio × 1.1), else the row's own picture, preloads it at high priority (its AVIF or WebP copy with Copies at their own addresses, via new `SEOProStack_Nextgen_Images::background_set()`), and swaps in a larger copy when the row grows or the screen gets denser, never a smaller one.
- Left as before: other background sizes, block themes, pictures without smaller copies, and a slider whose first slide has none. Filter: `seoprostack_kadence_hero_sizes`.
- Release: version 1.3.150, with GH#1223 and GH#1224.

Review: CodeRabbit's folder, denser-screen and no-JavaScript findings are fixed; the per-slide size and later-slide findings are answered in their threads. Codacy's complexity findings are fixed by splitting the class (local PHPMD with `phpmd.xml.dist`: none).

Resolves #1221

## How it was tested

Disposable site: WordPress 7.1.4, PHP 8.3, Kadence 1.5.2, Kadence Blocks 3.8.1.1; Playwright Chromium; pages opening with a two-slide background slider, a cover background and an auto background, 2048×1536 uploads with 300, 768, 1024 and 1536 sizes (one picture without its 1536 file).

- PageSpeed's phone (412×823, DPR 1.75, 964 px painted) and desktop (1350, DPR 1) got the 1536 copy; iPhone 15 (393, DPR 3, 1,652 px) and tablet (768, DPR 2, 1,536 px plus 10%) kept the full picture. One file of the picture fetched each time, never the full one alongside a copy, no console errors. AVIF copy preloaded with `type="image/avif"` and `fetchpriority="high"`.
- Widening 412 to 1600 and going from DPR 1 to 2 at 1350 replaced the 1536 copy with the full picture; the resolution listener then waited on `(resolution: 2dppx)`.
- JavaScript off: the `<noscript>` preload and the full picture, as before. `background-size: auto`: the head's preload, unchanged.
- Folder check through `SEOProStack_Hero_Picture::get()`: the row's own address and a CDN host with the same folder got the copies; the same file name in `2020/01` or `2025/11` got none.
- Media in cloud storage (MinIO) with local files removed, earlier in the PR: every copy and the row's picture at bucket addresses answering 200.
- Local: `scripts/preflight-release.sh` (exit 0), `scripts/plugin-check.sh` (no errors, before the review fixes); CI's Release build, preflight and Plugin Check passed.

title: GH#1229: Keep pages cached fills a LiteSpeed cache emptied from outside the site; release 1.3.151
body:
## Summary

**Keep pages cached** now fills LiteSpeed's page cache again when it is emptied from outside the site. That covers another site on the same hosting account sending Empty Entire Cache (`wp litespeed-purge all` on a network), the host's panel, or the server. None of these run the site's WordPress, so `litespeed_purged_all` never fired and pages stayed uncached until each was visited.

This PR also makes release 1.3.151 (version, Stable tag, badges, changelogs).

Resolves #1229

## Changes

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-keep-pages-cached.php`
  - New WP-Cron event `seoprostack_keep_pages_cached_check`. It runs every 300 s on its own `cron_schedules` interval (`check_schedule()`).
  - It runs only where `checks()` holds: the feature is on, the page cache is LiteSpeed's, and the site is a single site or a network's main site.
  - `sync_check()` schedules or clears the event at `wp_loaded` in the admin (not AJAX), in cron runs and in WP-CLI. Sites whose cron the host runs, and that a deploy script updates, get the event without an admin visit. It also runs on `seoprostack_setting_saved` for `keep_pages_cached`.
  - `check()` skips while a fill is queued. Otherwise it opens the home page once with `SEOProStack_Keep_Cached_Requests::open()`, as LiteSpeed Cache's crawler, which LiteSpeed answers `201` without running PHP while it holds the page.
  - `held()` reads `200`/`201` with a hit as held and `200` without one as missing. Anything else (a redirect, `403`, `429`, `503`, an error) changes nothing.
  - When the page was held at one check and is missing at the next, `fill_later(is_multisite())` fills the cache as `litespeed_purged()` does.
  - The setting's description and the file header describe the check.
  - `deactivate()` clears the event and the new option.
- `uninstall.php`: removes `seoprostack_keep_pages_cached_held` and the check's event.
- `README.md`, `readme.txt`, `changelog.txt`: feature docs and the 1.3.151 entries.

New option `seoprostack_keep_pages_cached_held` (`held`, `since`). It is not autoloaded and is written only when the answer changes.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan` passed.
- `scripts/preflight-release.sh` was run on the branch.

title: GH#1232: scheduled tasks keep other requests' changes, no piled-up copies, AI Engine runner not rescheduled from page loads; release 1.3.153
body:
## What

Fixes for other plugins (`plugin_fixes`, on by default) stops WordPress's scheduled tasks list from losing changes and piling up copies of recurring tasks, and stops AI Engine rescheduling its task runner from page loads. Includes release 1.3.153 (version, readmes, changelog), as GH#1229 did. 1.3.152 was released from `main` while this PR was open, so `main` is merged in and this PR's entry moves to 1.3.153.

- New `includes/class-seoprostack-cron-list.php` (`SEOProStack_Cron_List`, loaded from `SEOProStack_Plugin_Fixes::boot()` when the fix is on):
  - `write()` on `pre_update_option_cron` (`PHP_INT_MAX`): when the stored list (one `$wpdb` read past the caches) differs from the request's copy, only what the request added, changed or removed is applied to the stored list. Otherwise `$value` is written unchanged.
  - `dedupe()` at `wp_loaded` (priority 0) in cron runs and WP-CLI requests (`wp cron event run`), before due tasks are read: extra copies of a recurring task (same hook, args key and schedule) are removed in one write, **keeping the latest**.
- `SEOProStack_Plugin_Fixes::mwai_runner_check()` (init 14) swaps AI Engine's `ensure_cron_scheduled()` (init 15) for `mwai_runner()`: the same, without the "more than 300 s late → clear and reschedule" branch.

## Changes from the brief (#1232), and why

- **No `pre_schedule_event` guard** (brief item 2). `wp_reschedule_event()` calls `wp_schedule_event()` for the next time *while the copy that ran is still in the list*, then `wp-cron.php` unschedules that copy. A guard that refuses a second copy at another time would refuse every cron reschedule, and the task would be removed for good. Code that moves a task by adding before removing would lose it the same way. With writes merged, copies come only from races (requests that cannot see each other's copy, which a guard cannot stop) and are removed at the next cron run.
- **Keep the latest copy, not the earliest.** Between `wp-cron.php`'s reschedule write and its unschedule write, the copy about to go is the earlier one. If an overlapping cron run's dedupe kept that one, the task would then be removed entirely.
- **AI Engine: callback swap instead of `pre_clear_scheduled_hook` returning 0.** Blocking the clear would have left its `wp_schedule_event()` adding a copy on every late page load (the guard is gone). Replacing the init callback keeps AI Engine's own behaviour (schedule when missing, clear the other dev-mode hook). It works in every context: Reset (REST) and dev mode still clear and schedule themselves. It does not depend on `DISABLE_WP_CRON`, because the same reset also delays the runner on WP-Cron sites after 5 idle minutes.
- **Kept under `plugin_fixes`, no new setting.** STANDARDS → Code rules: a new setting must earn its place; this is a bug fix, and the bypass is to switch the fix off.

Remaining "could not be saved" case: a request that removes a task another request already removed now finds nothing to write, and `wp-cron.php` still logs that. Before, it wrote its old copy back over the other request's changes. The read and core's UPDATE are not locked, so two writes in the same instant can still race; the window is one query, not a whole request (review thread).

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh` (php, js, shell, workflows, phpcs, phpstan, build): all passed.
- `scripts/preflight-release.sh --offline`: 0 errors. 2 warnings existed before this PR (WordPress.org slug note; `RELEASING.md` and `scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh` behind the starter).
- `scripts/plugin-check.sh`: no errors. Only the existing expected updater findings and warnings, none in changed files.
- `scripts/test-site.sh` (WordPress 7.1.4, PHP 8.3, `DISABLE_WP_CRON`, a must-use copy of AI Engine 3.9.0's scheduling code):
  - **Overlap:** this request held an old copy while "another request" (a direct DB write) removed Y and added X, then this request scheduled Z. Stored list: `spsx_x,spsx_z`. With SEO Pro Stack deactivated: `spsx_y,spsx_z` (Y back, X lost).
  - **Late runner:** a front-end load left a 6-minute-late `mwai_tasks_internal_run` in place. Without the fix, it was rescheduled to +57 s.
  - **One `wp-cron.php` run:** the runner ran once (ticks 0 → 1) and one copy remains at +60 s. Two hourly copies 10 s apart became one (the later). A daily copy of the same hook and two single events of one hook were kept.
  - **Dev mode:** switching it on scheduled `mwai_tasks_internal_dev_run` (5 s) and removed the minute runner; switching it off did the reverse.
  - **WP-CLI:** in a WP-CLI request, two hourly copies became one, and the late runner was left in place.
  - `debug.log` empty.

Resolves #1232

title: GH#1233: Keep pages cached checks a page only it opens and counts it held after a fill; release 1.3.152
body:
## What

Keep pages cached's check for a LiteSpeed cache emptied from outside the site
(#1229, 1.3.151) missed two cases seen on Hostinger after the 1.3.151 deploy:

1. **First check after an update**: a fill left nothing stored, so a cache
   emptied between the fill and the first check was only recorded as
   "missing", and nothing filled it again.
2. **Home page re-cached by a visitor first**: the check opened the home
   page, which visitors and bots rebuild, so after the whole cache was
   emptied the check could find it held and leave every other page uncached.

## How

- `look()` opens the home page at its own address, `/?seoprostack-held=1`
  (`CHECK_ARG`), which LiteSpeed caches apart from the home page and nobody
  else opens. Where it does not answer 200 or 201 (redirected, refused), the
  home page itself, as before.
- New private `hold()`, called at the end of `run()` when a batch opened
  pages, nothing was refused and the queue is empty: opens the check's page
  (a second time if that request built it) and stores it as held only when
  LiteSpeed answered from its cache. A page LiteSpeed never caches is never
  stored as held, so it still never starts fills.
- README, readme.txt, changelog.txt: 1.3.152. README also corrects LiteSpeed
  Cache's Default Front Page TTL default to a week (604800 s in its
  `data/const.default.json`), not a day.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh php phpstan`: all passed; `vendor/bin/phpcs` on the
  changed PHP files: no findings.
- On a Hostinger LiteSpeed dev site with this file: the queued fill ran
  through the queue's own hook (2 batches, 50 pages), then `hold()` stored
  `held: true`; `/?seoprostack-held=1` answered miss, then hit, apart from the
  home page.
- Controlled outside purge (site only) and the next check queuing a full fill:
  results in the comment below.

title: GH#1238: Keep pages cached's network fill plans every site, not only the first; release 1.3.154
body:
## Summary

Keep pages cached's network fill planned only the network's first site. `SEOProStack_Keep_Cached_Pages::next_site()` narrowed a one-site `get_sites()` query with a `sites_clauses` filter. `WP_Site_Query` caches by query vars and applies that filter only on a cache miss, so every later call in the request got site 1. `network()` planned site 1 until `MAX`, left the queue at `site: 1` and `full`, and each batch reopened the main site's pages, while subsites waited for their own purges.

`next_site()` now takes the network's active site IDs from one `get_sites()` query (`number => 0`, `network_id`, ordered by ID), which is cached correctly, and returns the first at or after `$after`. `SEOProStack_Security_Headers::cleanup_sites()` had the same cursor (a problem with a persistent object cache) and now picks its 50 IDs the same way.

Version 1.3.154, with changelog entries in `README.md`, `readme.txt` and `changelog.txt`.

## Files Changed

- `includes/class-seoprostack-keep-cached-pages.php`: `next_site()`
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-security-headers.php`: `cleanup_sites()`
- `seoprostack.php`, `readme.txt`, `README.md`, `changelog.txt`: 1.3.154

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Low. Two private site-walk helpers; the query is core's `get_sites()`.
- Live, on an 11-site network (Hostinger LiteSpeed, 1.3.152): the old `next_site()` returned 1 for 1, 2, 5, 19 and 23. `plan_network(true, 1, ...)` returned 1,000 addresses, only 25 distinct, all site 1's, with `done: false, site: 1`.
- The new query, inline on the same network: 0→1, 1→1, 2→2, 3→5, 6→7, 19→19, 20→20, 22→22, 23→0.
- The fixed class file, loaded under another class name with `wp eval-file` (opens no pages, writes nothing): `plan_network(true, 0, ...)` returned `done: true, site: 0`, 191 distinct addresses across all 11 sites, in 4.4 s.

title: GH#1240: Keep pages cached keeps a fill when the cache is emptied during a batch; 20 s batches on network subsites; release 1.3.155
body:
Resolves #1240

## What

- `includes/class-seoprostack-keep-cached-queue.php`: `get()` calls the new private `forget()` first, which removes the queue option from the `options` cache group and from `notoptions`. `plan()` and `done()` now really see a purge (`fill_later()`) or a saved post (`add()`) made by another request while the batch ran, and `update_option()` compares with the stored value. Same idea as `SEOProStack_Cron_List::stored()` (#1232).
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-keep-pages-cached.php`: `run()` uses `CLI_BUDGET` (90 s) from the command line only when `is_main_site()` (a single site, or a network's main site, where the network fill and the check run). Other network sites keep `BUDGET` (20 s), because networks' cron runs one site after another.
- Release 1.3.155: `seoprostack.php`, `readme.txt`, `README.md` (feature text and changelog), `changelog.txt`.

## Why

After the 1.3.154 deploy, an 11-site network's main site stayed uncached. The deploy purged site 1 while the cron runner's 90-second batch ran (05:06:26 to 05:07:56). `done()` at 05:07:53 used the batch's own copy of the queue and deleted the new fill, then `hold()` counted the check page held again. At 05:39, 24 of its 25 first pages were misses taking 1 to 5 s.

On the same network, the runner (stops starting sites after 240 s) processed 5 sites in 353 s and skipped the next cycle, so each site got a turn every 20 to 30 minutes.

## Verification

- `php -l` on both files; `vendor/bin/phpcs -q --standard=phpcs.xml.dist` on both files: clean; `scripts/lint.sh phpstan`: passed.
- Mechanism, on two live sites (no persistent object cache): a request read a throwaway option, its row was changed in the database as another request would, and `get_option()` again returned the old value (`read_again=before`); after `wp_cache_delete()` it returned the new one (`after_forget=after`).
- End to end on a single test site, purge (`fill_later()`) 12 s into a batch:
  - 1.3.154: the batch ended with `full=0`, the purge lost.

title: GH#1242: page checks wait for Keep pages cached, 15 s network turns, refused checks retried; release 1.3.156
body:
Resolves #1242

## What

Load plugins only where needed's page checks (`seoprostack_front_verify`) no longer use up a network site's cron turn after an update, and no longer save an address as needing every plugin when the server refused the check. Release 1.3.156.

- `includes/class-seoprostack-front-verify.php`
  - `run()` returns, keeping its queue and schedule, while `filling()` finds a Keep pages cached batch scheduled with URLs queued or a full fill pending. Visitors' cached pages come first.
  - On a network run from the command line (`'cli' === PHP_SAPI && is_multisite()`), checks start for `NETWORK_RUN_BUDGET` (15 s) instead of `RUN_BUDGET` (50 s). A check already started still runs to its end.
  - `render()`: answers in `SEOProStack_Keep_Cached_Requests::REFUSED` (403, 429, 503) return `retry` and `refused`. A refused first render, or a refused trial (which `check()` treated as a difference, halving the group and rendering on), ends the check as failed with retry. The address waits for its next visitor, and five refusals in a row pause checks for an hour (`FAILURES`).
  - `render()` sends its request through `SEOProStack_Keep_Cached_Requests::resolver()` (LiteSpeed Cache's Server IP when set), as Keep pages cached and `SEOProStack_Litespeed::deliver_purge()` already do.
- README.md (the page checks; Hosting needs → Server IP; changelog), readme.txt, changelog.txt, version 1.3.156.

## Why (evidence)

- On an 11-site network run by a sequential cron runner that starts no site after 240 s, `seoprostack_front_verify` took 89.8 of a subsite's 113 s of due events (Keep pages cached 22.9 s, the other nine under 1 s). A cycle reached 3 sites in 243 s, so subsites' purged pages waited 20 minutes or more for their turn.
- Behind Cloudflare on Hostinger, the origin's LiteSpeed refused the server's own requests through Cloudflare most of the time (21 of 30 samples in six minutes): `403 Access to this resource on the server is denied!`, `x-turbo-charged-by: LiteSpeed`, on every site and user agent. The same request straight to the server was answered every time. The last check on four network sites had failed with 403, and all 10 addresses queued for a test were saved as needing every plugin.

## Verification

- `php -l`, `vendor/bin/phpcs` (clean), `scripts/lint.sh phpstan` (no errors).
- `scripts/preflight-release.sh --offline` on the branch head: 0 errors, 3 standing warnings (slug, core-file drift in `scripts/`, README badges), none in files this PR changes.

title: GH#1245: Server IP read as LiteSpeed Cache applies it on primary-settings networks; release 1.3.157
body:
## What

`SEOProStack_Litespeed::server_ip()` reads LiteSpeed Cache's Server IP as LiteSpeed Cache applies it. `SEOProStack_Keep_Cached_Requests::resolver()` (Keep pages cached, Load plugins only where needed's page checks, `deliver_purge()`) and `SEOProStack_Litespeed_Crawler::origin()` (Hosting needs) use it instead of `SEOProStack_Litespeed::conf('server_ip')`.

## Why

On a network with LiteSpeed Cache's **Use Primary Site Configuration** on, LiteSpeed Cache loads the main site's options over a subsite's (`Conf::_try_load_site_options()`; `server_ip` is not in `Base::$single_site_options`), so the subsite's own option is ignored and is usually empty. `conf()` read that own option, so with Server IP set on the main site, other sites' checks and fills still went through the CDN and its origin refusals (#1242).

- While LiteSpeed Cache is loaded and the request has not switched site: `apply_filters('litespeed_conf', 'server_ip')`, its API (`src/api.cls.php`), with its constant, primary-site and network rules.
- After `switch_to_blog()` (the network fill), LiteSpeed Cache still holds the first site's settings, so the main site's option when the network uses primary settings and the site is not the main site; else `conf()`.

## Evidence

Probe with the same logic on the 11-site production network (LiteSpeed Cache 7.9.3, `use_primary_settings` = `1`, Server IP set on the main site), printing only direct/DNS:

- `--url` per site: old read direct on 2 of 11 sites, new read direct on 11 of 11.
- From the main site through `switch_to_blog()` for each site: old 2 of 11, new 11 of 11.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`: all passed.
- `scripts/preflight-release.sh` on the branch (below).
- After deploy: `resolver()` non-null on subsites; page checks stop failing with 403; the network cron cycle reaches every site.

## Release

Version 1.3.157 (`seoprostack.php`, `readme.txt`, `README.md`, `changelog.txt`). 1.3.156 is released and update-tested but not deployed; 1.3.157 is deployed once, so sites are purged once.

Resolves #1245

title: GH#1243: Keep pages cached and page checks go straight to this server behind a CDN when Server IP is empty; release 1.3.159
body:
## What

Behind a CDN, with LiteSpeed Cache's **Server IP** empty, Keep pages cached, purge delivery and the page checks of Load plugins only where needed now go straight to this server instead of through the CDN. SEO Pro Stack learns the server's address from the site's own web requests and keeps it in its own option. LiteSpeed Cache's settings are never written. Release 1.3.159.

Resolves #1243

## How

- `includes/class-seoprostack-litespeed-crawler.php`
  - `learn()` runs at shutdown on web requests to a LiteSpeed server. It writes `SERVER_ADDR` to the autoloaded option `seoprostack_origin_ip`, only when the address changes. It looks nothing up and sends no request, so a visitor's request never waits.
  - `learned()` checks a newly noted address the first time `resolver()` needs it, which happens from WP-Cron or WP-CLI. The address is used only when the host name resolves elsewhere and `reaches_server()` gets an answer from LiteSpeed itself with no `cf-ray` header. An address that fails is checked again after an hour.
  - `reaches_server()` uses the home URL's own port. It fails when the pin was not applied (no cURL transport), which also affects the existing Hosting needs fix.
- `includes/class-seoprostack-keep-cached-requests.php`
  - `resolver()` uses Server IP when it is set, else the learned address.
  - `settle()` forgets the learned address only when cURL could not connect (error 7, or error 28 before connecting) or when a CDN answered (`cf-ray`). A slow page that timed out after connecting keeps it.
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-hosting-needs.php` hooks `learn()` whether Hosting needs is on or not. `uninstall.php` deletes the option.
- `README.md` (Keep pages cached; Hosting needs → Server IP), `readme.txt` and `changelog.txt` describe the change. The version is now 1.3.159.

This takes over the worker's first version. The worker's `learn()` sent the DNS lookup and a HEAD request at the end of a visitor's uncached request. It then repeated that every hour on sites where the check failed, on any server, not only LiteSpeed. It also forgot the address on any `WP_Error`, so one slow page made the whole batch fall back to Cloudflare.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`: all passed.
- Tested on a Hostinger LiteSpeed site behind Cloudflare, with the patched files and Server IP empty for the WP-CLI run only (`LITESPEED_CONF` and `LITESPEED_CONF__SERVER_IP=''`):
  - One web request (`admin-ajax.php`) stored `{"seen": <server IPv4>}`, autoloaded.
  - From WP-CLI, `resolver()` checked the address and pinned it, and `open()` got `201 hit` for `/` and `/contact/`, straight from LiteSpeed.
  - With the learned address set to the site's Cloudflare address, the first answer had `cf-ray`, so the address was forgotten and the option deleted. The next web request noted the address again, and the next CLI run checked and pinned it.
  - `settle()` forgot on cURL 7, on 28 "Connection timed out" and on 28 "Failed to connect … Timeout was reached". It kept the address on 28 "Operation timed out … 0 bytes received" and on 35.
  - With Server IP set (the normal state), Server IP was used and Keep pages cached's check ran cleanly.

title: GH#1251: Media in cloud storage URL index in its own table; GH#1250 starter sync; release 1.3.160
body:
## Summary

Resolves #1250. Media in cloud storage kept its URL index as one wp_options row per stored file (107,444 rows on the East Sussex stack). It now lives in {prefix}seoprostack_media_urls (binary(32) SHA-256 primary key, post_id indexed): url_store() writes it (INSERT ... ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE), url_lookup() reads it by primary key and falls back to the option until this version has moved them. run_batch() calls build_urls() for up to 5 s a batch (index_due() keeps batches coming): creates the table, moves the options 500 at a time (INSERT, then one DELETE plus cache deletes), then once per table creation adds every inventory's files with INSERT IGNORE, which refills a dropped table. A failed write or lookup sends reads and writes back to options and retries in 10 minutes. Deleting an attachment deletes its rows. New WP-CLI action: wp seoprostack media-storage url-index (takes the batch lease per 20 s step); status reports table rows and options left. Uninstall drops the table. Also syncs the 4 starter core files that were behind (deploy-sites cron run and home retry, update-test release wait) to starter 1.0.52, and releases 1.3.160 (version, readme.txt, README.md, changelog.txt, badges). Follow-up for the per-picture seoprostack_storage_job_original_* rows: #1252.



## Files Changed

README.md, RELEASING.md, changelog.txt, includes/features/class-seoprostack-media-storage.php, readme.txt, scripts/deploy-sites.sh, scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh, scripts/update-test.sh, seoprostack.php, uninstall.php

## Decisions

Options are moved and deleted, not copied, as the issue asks; a downgrade to 1.3.159 after the move would lose bucket-address lookups for content images without wp-image-{id} until uploads rewrite them. The per-picture kept-original inventories (seoprostack_storage_job_original_*, 9,522 rows / 10 MB on East Sussex) stay for now: they rely on insert-only and tombstone semantics, filed as #1252.

## Runtime Testing

body:
## What

New Speed feature **Lighter Tutor LMS pages** (`SEOProStack_Tutor_Light`, setting `tutor_light`, on by default): Tutor LMS's styles and scripts, the Kadence theme's `kadence-tutorlms` stylesheet and, through them, React, ReactDOM and moment load only on pages that use Tutor.

## Why

Tutor LMS 4.2.0 (`TUTOR\Assets`) enqueues its files on every page. PageSpeed on 5 November showed them holding up the first paint on 11 of 15 measured home pages, none of which has Tutor content. Details and the Load plugins only where needed analysis: #1258.

## How

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-tutor-light.php`, modelled on `SEOProStack_Woo_Light`: at `wp_enqueue_scripts` `PHP_INT_MAX`, queued styles and scripts whose file is in `plugins/tutor/` or `plugins/tutor-pro/`, and `kadence-tutorlms`, are dequeued unless `is_tutor_page()`:
  - a query var Tutor registers (dashboard, profile, course subpages);
  - a single page, archive or taxonomy of the post types `tutor()` names (read with `Config::all()`, so no `__get()` log entries);

  - filter `seoprostack_tutor_light_page`.
- A Tutor shortcode or block that renders anyway puts the files back for the footer (`pre_do_shortcode_tag`, `pre_render_block`).
- Logged-in people are left alone (Tutor's toolbar items, Tutor Pro's push notification prompt on the front page, `Utils::handle_flash_message()`). This differs from the issue text, which said "while the admin bar shows": students usually have no admin bar.
- Registered after Woo light in `SEOProStack_Setup::FEATURES`. Added to the Recommended speed settings while Tutor is active. Docs: README (Features, a section, the filter), readme.txt, changelog.txt. PHPStan: `tutor()`/`tutor_utils()` added to the "not installed here" ignore.

title: GH#1260: Used CSS covers every recommended plugin and theme, and the classes their scripts add
body:
## What

**Load the CSS each page uses first** (Used CSS) now:

- handles the stylesheets of every recommended theme and plugin (Free Plugins and Pro Plugins) that prints its own front-end CSS, and the Kadence child theme, not only the Kadence theme, Kadence Blocks, Kadence Pro, Fluent Forms and the block library (`SEOProStack_Used_Css_Links::PLUGINS`);
- counts the class names the page's scripts may add after it loads as present (new `SEOProStack_Used_Css_Scripts`), so sliders, galleries and animations look right before the full stylesheets arrive;
- is recommended by the speed plan wherever the Kadence theme or one of those plugins is active.

Only scripts that run without the visitor doing anything count: no type, a JavaScript type (Rocket Loader's too) or `module`. Scripts held until a click, a key or consent (`seoprostack/delayed`, `litespeed/javascript`, `text/plain`) run after the full stylesheets, so they are left out. Each script file is read once per version into a cache file next to the stylesheets'.

## Evidence

Read-only probe on two live Kadence sites (the branch's classes, renamed, run on each home page's HTML; no site changed), with Tutor's files taken out as Lighter Tutor LMS pages (#1258) leaves these pages:

| Home page | Before (live) | After |
|---|---|---|
| Site A | 21 stylesheets handled, 72 KB in the page; Readabler, WooCommerce styles and others still held up the page | 22 handled, none left holding up the page, 140 KB in the page (113 KB without the scripts' classes) |
| Site B | 26 handled, 112 KB | 29 handled, 192 KB (153 KB without the scripts' classes) |

Rewriting takes 46 to 242 ms the first time (scripts and stylesheets read and cached), 24 to 78 ms after.

What the scripts add is almost all their sliders', galleries' and lightboxes' first-paint classes: `kb-splide-init` +12.7 KB, the gallery lightbox init +17.8 KB, Splide +3 to 4 KB. Before skipping delayed scripts, the accessibility toolbar's delayed script added 41 KB of rules for a panel that only opens on a click.

Screenshot pilot on both home pages (Playwright; desktop, mobile and both in dark mode; top of page, header submenu, mobile menu drawer, form and footer). The reference is the page's own render without Used CSS; it is compared, pixel by pixel, with this branch's rewrite of the same render, once with the full stylesheets loading later and once with them blocked, so only the used CSS in the page applies (what the first paint shows):

| Home page | Shots | Stylesheets blocked | Pixels different |
|---|---|---|---|
| Site A | 16 | 22 | 0 in every shot |
| Site B | 24 | 28 | 0 in every shot |

A control run, the page without its used CSS with the same stylesheets blocked, differs by 338,717 pixels on Site B's mobile top, so the check sees missing CSS. On the old code, an earlier run of this pilot showed Site A's hero slider as a bulleted list with a grey gutter (its script adds `kb-splide`, which had no rules); the scripts' classes fix that.

Test site (WordPress 7.1, PHP 8.3, Kadence, Kadence Blocks, Fluent Forms, Tutor LMS): a page with a form and a Tutor shortcode renders 11 stylesheets' used CSS; no PHP notices in the debug log.

title: GH#1261: Load AI Engine's chatbot on first use, not in every page's head
body:
## What

New Speed feature, on by default: **Load AI Engine's chatbot on first use** (`SEOProStack_Ai_Engine_Later`, setting `ai_engine_later`).

With a site-wide chatbot, AI Engine enqueues `mwai_chatbot` (`app/chatbot.js`, about 350 KB, in the head, with React, ReactDOM and wp-element) and the chatbot's theme stylesheet on every page. This takes them out of the queue (at `wp_enqueue_scripts`, and at `wp_footer` 19 for a chatbot a shortcode or block enqueued). After the footer's scripts it prints their tags, exactly as WordPress would (`do_items()`, so dependencies not yet printed, inline scripts and translations come too), as escaped JSON. A small loader adds them on the first pointer, mouse move, touch, key, wheel or scroll, or when an inline (non-popup) chatbot comes within 600 px of the screen, then calls AI Engine's own `window.mwaiInitialize()`.

- If another script needs the chatbot's, it loads as before and nothing is printed.
- Not in the admin, feeds, embeds, the Customizer, AJAX, REST or AMP requests. Filter `seoprostack_ai_engine_later`.
- In Recommended speed settings while AI Engine or AI Engine Pro is active.
- README.md (Features, a section, filter), readme.txt, changelog.txt.

## Evidence

On two Kadence sites with AI Engine Pro 3.9.0's site-wide chatbot, AI Engine's files led Lighthouse's render-blocking requests (mobile 60 and 69, LCP 7.2 s and 7.5 s, estimated saving 3 to 5 s). Their HTML has `mwai_chatbot_theme_chatgpt-css`, `react-js`, `react-dom-js`, `wp-element-js` and `mwai_chatbot-js` in the head.

|---|---|---|
| AI Engine / React files before any interaction | 6 requests, 4 in the head | 0 |
| After a mouse move or tap | | the same 6 files load; the chatbot mounts and its launcher shows |
| Console errors | none | none |

With the feature on, a page with an inline `[mwai_chatbot]` mounts it without interaction (in the first screen). The popup opens after a mouse move; `start_session` and `chats/submit` return 200 (REST nonce works). The reply is AI Engine's "something went wrong" because the test site has no AI provider ("The environment is required" in the log, the same with the feature off).

title: GH#1264: Load plugins only where needed skips Tutor LMS on pages without Tutor content
body:
## Summary

Load plugins only where needed kept Tutor LMS (and Tutor LMS Pro) on every page, including home pages without Tutor content. There were two causes. This fixes both.

1. **Always-load notes.** Tutor's `determine_current_user` callback (`TUTOR\RestAuth::api_auth`) and its and Tutor LMS Pro's login and registration callbacks are on hooks that make a plugin always load. `front_propose()` never offered such a plugin for skipping. Those callbacks do nothing on the requests that skip plugins (GET page views, not the REST API): `api_auth` changes the user only on Tutor REST routes, and the login and registration callbacks only run on login and registration POSTs, which load every plugin anyway. New `FRONT_INERT_CALLBACKS` lists them, and `front_notes()` no longer counts them. Any other callback on those hooks counts as before. New `callback_id()` is shared with `woo_can_skip()`.
2. **Pages still differed without Tutor.** Once proposed, `verify_front()` reported "differs", so Tutor stayed. With Lighter Tutor LMS pages on (#1258), a page that is not Tutor's, viewed logged out, now also leaves out what Tutor adds beyond its own files:
   - the Kadence theme's Tutor rules in `kadence-global` inline CSS (`kadence_dynamic_css` callbacks of `Kadence\TutorLMS\Component`, which only style course and course-archive headers);
   - `jquery-ui-sortable` and `jquery-touch-punch`, which `TUTOR\Assets::frontend_scripts()` queues (they bring jQuery into the head, plus jQuery UI core and mouse). They are removed only if nothing queued them before Tutor's turn, and put back with Tutor's files when a Tutor shortcode or block renders;
   - the `tutor-lms` body class.

Resolves #1264

## Files

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-loading.php`: `FRONT_INERT_CALLBACKS`, `callback_id()`, `front_notes()`, `woo_can_skip()`.
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-tutor-light.php`: `light()`, `kadence_css()`, `core_before()`, `core_after()`, `body_class()`, `dequeue()`.
- `README.md`, `changelog.txt`.

## Evidence

Test site (WordPress 7.1.4, PHP 8.3, Kadence, Kadence Blocks, Fluent Forms, Tutor LMS 4.2.0), logged out:

- Learned map: `tutor/tutor.php` noted `content,pages,bar` (before: `always,content,pages,login,bar`).
- Home page HTML with Tutor active and inactive: identical except an asset version string that changed with the reinstall.
- `SEOProStack_Plugin_Loading::verify_front()`: `result: verified`, `skip: 1`, set `["tutor/tutor.php"]` for the front page and a plain page (before the second fix: `differs`).
- Per page, with a test-only marker reporting whether Tutor loaded:
  - `/` and `/plain/`: Tutor not loaded, 0 Tutor files, no jQuery, no `tutor-lms` class.
  - A course, the courses archive, the dashboard and the registration page: Tutor loaded with its files.
- No SEO Pro Stack messages in the debug log.
- `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`: all passed.

Not yet checked: Tutor LMS Pro on the test site (live sites have it; its callbacks are in `FRONT_INERT_CALLBACKS`).

title: GH#1268: AI Engine chatbot on first use: stylesheet first, printed when loaded anyway, older AI Engine left alone
body:
## What

Fixes from the review of #1261 (Load AI Engine's chatbot on first use, `SEOProStack_Ai_Engine_Later`):

1. **The stylesheet loads before the scripts.** The loader appended the held `<link rel=stylesheet>` and moved on at once, so `chatbot.js` could mount the chatbot before its theme stylesheet loaded (a moment unstyled). It now waits for each held stylesheet's `load` or `error` event, or at most 3 s (`STYLE_WAIT`), before the next tag.
2. **The stylesheet prints when the chatbot loaded anyway.** When another script depended on `mwai_chatbot`, WordPress printed `chatbot.js` as usual, but `print_loader()` returned early and the held `mwai_chatbot_theme_*` stylesheets never printed. They now print at `wp_footer` 21 in that case.
3. **Older AI Engine is left alone.** The loader calls `window.mwaiInitialize()`; without it, a chatbot added after `DOMContentLoaded` never mounts. The feature now runs only when the active AI Engine's `app/chatbot.js` (`MWAI_PATH`) defines `mwaiInitialize`. The answer is kept per `MWAI_VERSION` in the autoloaded option `seoprostack_ai_engine_later_support` (removed on uninstall), so the file is read once per AI Engine version.

Docs: README.md (the feature's section), changelog.txt.

## Evidence

Test site (WordPress 7.1.4, PHP 8.3, AI Engine 3.9.1, Default chatbot site-wide), Playwright:

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| Feature on, first mouse move | `chatgpt.css` finished at 1638 ms, `chatbot.js` requested at 1661 ms; chatbot mounted (`data-mwai-initialized`); no console errors; 0 AI Engine requests before the move |
| Support option set to `ok: false` | AI Engine's `<link>` and `<script src=…chatbot.js>` print as before; no loader |
| Support option for another `MWAI_VERSION` | read again from `chatbot.js`: `{"version":"3.9.1","ok":true}` |
| A must-use script depending on `mwai_chatbot` | `chatbot.js` and `chatgpt.css` both print; chatbot mounted; no console errors (before: no stylesheet) |

AI Engine Pro 3.9.0, as used in production, defines `window.mwaiInitialize=initializeMwai` in `app/chatbot.js` (checked read-only), so the feature stays on there. The test site's log had only AI Engine's own gateway messages, none from SEO Pro Stack.

## Checks

- `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`: all passed.

Resolves #1268

title: GH#1307: Speed: load jQuery at the end of the page
body:
## Summary

New Speed feature, on by default: **Load jQuery at the end of the page** (`SEOProStack_Jquery_Footer`, setting `jquery_footer`).

WordPress registers `jquery-core` and `jquery-migrate` in the head. A footer script's dependencies keep their own group, so one footer script that needs jQuery prints jQuery in the head as a synchronous, render-blocking script. The Kadence theme's `kadence-shop-spinner` does this with WooCommerce active, and PropertyHive's search scripts do the same. On one Kadence shop with Used CSS on, `jquery.min.js` was the largest render-blocking request left (601 ms on mobile, 1.3.163).

How it works:

- `wp_head` priority 8 (after styles, before head scripts): when the queue already needs WordPress's own `jquery-core`, `jquery`, `jquery-core` and `jquery-migrate` get group 1 and a marker is printed. WordPress's dependency order still prints jQuery in the head when a head script needs it, and otherwise just before the first footer script that does.
- An output buffer moves jQuery's tags (with their inline scripts) back to the marker, with an HTML comment saying why, when anything between the marker and jQuery's new place might use jQuery: inline code naming `jQuery`, Google Tag Manager, a same-site script outside WordPress, SEO Pro Stack, the Kadence theme and the recommended plugins, or a script from another site without `async`/`defer`.
- Not for logged-in users, cart/checkout/account, previews, feeds, embeds, Customizer, AJAX, REST or AMP. Filter `seoprostack_jquery_footer`. Toggling it empties the page cache.

Not in scope: deferring jQuery or its dependents.

Resolves #1307

## Files

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-jquery-footer.php` (new).
- `includes/class-seoprostack-used-css-links.php`: `on_site()` (shared same-site check).
- `includes/class-seoprostack-setup.php`: feature registered after Delay scripts.
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-speed-plan.php`: in Recommended speed settings.
- `README.md` (On by default, Speed plan, feature section, filter), `changelog.txt` (Unreleased).

## Evidence

Disposable test site (`scripts/test-site.sh up`; WordPress 7.1.4, PHP 8.3, Kadence, WooCommerce 11.2.2, Fluent Forms, this branch's build). A test-only must-use file adds a footer script that needs jQuery (like Kadence's shop spinner) and sets a flag when its jQuery code runs, plus query switches for each blocker. Playwright, logged out unless stated:

| Page | jQuery | Comment printed | jQuery code ran | Console errors |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Home | end of page | none | yes | none |
| Fluent Forms page | end of page | none | yes | none |
| Home, setting off | head | none | yes | none |
| Home, logged in | head | none | n/a (curl) | n/a |
| Shop (WooCommerce's deferred head scripts need jQuery) | head | none | yes | none |
| Single product | head | none | yes | none |
| Head script declares `jquery` | head | none | yes | none |
| Inline `jQuery(...)` in the body | head | "an inline script uses it" | yes | none |
| Synchronous script from another site | head | "a script from another site comes before it" | yes | none |
| Same, `async` | end of page | none | yes | none |
| Unsupported same-site script in the head | head | "a script outside WordPress, the Kadence theme and the recommended plugins comes before it" | yes | none |
| Google Tag Manager snippet | head | "Google Tag Manager may use it" | yes | none |

`scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`: all passed.

title: GH#1312: Image loading: Kadence Advanced Slider loads only the shown slides' pictures, first slide preloaded
body:
## What

**Image loading** with a Kadence Blocks Pro **Advanced Slider** (`kadence/slider`):

- When a post or page opens with the slider, its first slide's picture is preloaded at high priority from the head, as a Kadence row's background is (`SEOProStack_Image_Loading::kadence_preload()`), and counts as the page's one high-priority picture and the first of **Load straight away**.
- New `SEOProStack_Kadence_Slider` (`render_block_kadence/slider`): before each slider, a style and a small script. The script adds `sps-slides` to `<html>`; under it every slide's picture except the first slide's waits until Splide shows the slide (`is-active`, `is-visible`). Once the first slide's picture is in (or the page has loaded), `sps-slides-near` lets the next slides fetch theirs (`is-next`, `is-prev`, the slide after each shown one). A slider with no `is-active` slide a second after load gets `sps-slides-all` and every picture, as before. No JavaScript, or a browser without `:not()` selector lists: nothing waits. Filter `seoprostack_kadence_slider_wait`.
- Rows and sliders hidden by WordPress 6.9's Block visibility (`metadata.blockVisibility`) or shown on a Kadence Blocks Pro condition (`kadenceConditional`) are no longer preloaded.
- With **Copies at their own addresses**, Kadence Blocks Pro's head CSS (`kadence_blocks_pro_css`) names the AVIF and WebP copies with `image-set()`, as Kadence Blocks' does, so the slide's CSS and the preload name the same file.

## Why

A Kadence home page opening with a 17-slide fade slider (Kadence Blocks Pro 2.9.0): every slide's picture was fetched with the page at low priority, competing with the first: 28 pictures, 4.9 MB of the page's 5.4 MB; PageSpeed mobile 75, LCP 15.3 s on the first slide.

## Verification

- `bash scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`: all passed.
- Live page, with what the class prints (generated from the class) and the preload injected, throttled phone (Playwright, 1.6 Mbps, 150 ms, 4x CPU):

  | | first slide's picture | LCP | load | slide pictures with the page |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | before | 0.48 s, with 16 others | not the slide | 29.7 s | 17 |
  | after | 0.26 s (preload) | 4.9 s, first slide | 17.9 s | 1; slide 2 at 4.9 s, then the others about 3 s apart, with the autoplay |
  | classes renamed (fail-safe) | 0.23 s | 4.9 s | 17.9 s | the rest at load + 1 s |

  Every slide shown had its picture; no console errors.
- Test site (WordPress 7.1.4, PHP 8.3, Kadence 1.6.0, Kadence Blocks 3.9.0, Kadence Blocks Pro 2.9.0, that page's content): preload first in the head; style and script just before the slider; first slide's picture at 0.18 s and the LCP; the second slide's requested at 3.7 s and shown at 5.2 s, then each next slide's one ahead; no PHP messages from SEO Pro Stack. With Copies at their own addresses and a WebP copy: the preload and the slide's `image-set()` name the same `.jpg.webp`, requested once.
- After release: PageSpeed mobile on the two affected home pages, before and after.

Resolves #1312

title: GH#1313: Hreflang codes with the site's country (1.3.167)
body:
## Summary

New off-by-default Content feature SEOProStack_Hreflang_Country (settings hreflang_country, hreflang_country_code). With TranslatePress and a two-letter ISO country, a trp_hreflang filter at priority 20 replaces the country part of each locale-derived hreflang code with the site's (en_GB en-GB to en-JE, es_MX es-MX to es-US), in the head and in TranslatePress SEO Pack's sitemap (same filter). Language-only codes and locales without a country stay; formality suffixes are handled as TranslatePress does; where two languages with different codes would collide (en_GB + en_US, fr_FR + fr_BE on a BE site) both keep TranslatePress's. Codes are computed once per request from trp_settings and recomputed after either plugin's settings save. Release PR for 1.3.167 (1.3.166, GH#1312, was released on main meanwhile).

README.md, changelog.txt, includes/class-seoprostack-setup.php, includes/features/class-seoprostack-hreflang-country.php, readme.txt, seoprostack.php

## Decisions

Off by default because it needs a per-site choice. Collision guard rather than overwriting, so no two URLs ever share an hreflang code. x-default is left to TranslatePress's own Advanced setting rather than duplicated here.

title: GH#1324: Keep pages cached fills the WebP copy of each page that browsers get
body:
## What

Keep pages cached asked for each page with `Accept: text/html,application/xhtml+xml`.
With LiteSpeed Cache's WebP replacement or WP-Optimize's WebP images on, those caches keep
a separate copy of each page for browsers whose `Accept` holds `image/webp`, which every
current browser sends. So Keep pages cached filled a copy no desktop browser gets (and on
WP-Optimize, no phone either), and visitors still waited for an uncached page.

## Change

- `includes/class-seoprostack-keep-cached-requests.php`: new constant `ACCEPT`, Chrome's
  `Accept` for a page; `request()` sends it for every request (desktop, phone and
  `page_html()`). This is what LiteSpeed Cache's own crawler does with WebP on
  (`Accept: image/webp,*/*`, skipping the plain copy). Where no WebP copy is kept, the
  cache ignores `Accept`, so nothing else changes.
- Changelog: `changelog.txt`, `readme.txt`, `README.md` (Unreleased).

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`: all passed.
- Live, straight to the origin on a multisite network with LiteSpeed Cache 7.9.1 and
  WebP replacement on (1.3.166, after Keep pages cached had filled the site):
  - Before: 10 of 11 linked pages `miss` for desktop Chrome's `Accept`, `hit` for the
    warmer's old `Accept`.
  - The new request (Keep pages cached's desktop user agent with the new `Accept`) on
    four pages not opened since the purge: `miss`, then desktop Chrome `hit` on all four.

Resolves #1324

title: GH#1326: Image loading: preload names LiteSpeed Cache's WebP copy when it rewrites the slide or row CSS
body:
## What

With LiteSpeed Cache's WebP replacement on, Image loading preloaded a Kadence Advanced
Slider's first slide picture (GH#1312), or a hero row's picture without smaller copies
(GH#1204), as the JPEG, while LiteSpeed rewrote the slide's or row's CSS to its `.jpg.webp`
at the end of the page. Browsers fetched the picture twice at high priority, and the copy
they show (the LCP) only after the CSS.

PageSpeed mobile on a Kadence home page opening with a 17-slide Advanced Slider (1.3.166):
the same 214 KiB picture at 256 ms (`.jpg`, the preload) and 353 ms (`.jpg.webp`, the LCP),
with 303 ms of resource load delay.

## Change

`includes/features/class-seoprostack-image-loading.php`:

- `preload()` prints its tag through the new `preload_tag()`, and when no SEO Pro Stack copy
  is named and LiteSpeed Cache is loaded, keeps the address and tag and adds
  `litespeed_next_gen()` at `litespeed_buffer_after` 5.
- `litespeed_next_gen()` swaps the tag's address for `<address>.avif` or `<address>.webp`
  (named as LiteSpeed's `Media::replace_webp()` names it) when the page names that copy,
  so the preload follows what LiteSpeed did on that request. Logged-in visitors, pages
  LiteSpeed does not cache and browsers without WebP keep the picture's own address.
- Changelog: `changelog.txt`, `readme.txt`, `README.md` (Unreleased).

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`: all passed.
- `litespeed_next_gen()` run on the live home page's two cached copies (fetched from the
  site, with the preload as 1.3.166 printed it):
  - WebP copy: preload `…Wooden-Bridge.jpg.webp`, slide CSS `…Wooden-Bridge.jpg.webp`.
  - JPEG copy: preload and slide CSS both `…Wooden-Bridge.jpg`, page unchanged.
- After release: live preload and CSS name the same address in each copy, and PageSpeed
  shows one request for the first slide's picture.

Resolves #1326

title: GH#1329: Kadence rows further down load their background pictures as visitors scroll near; fixes GH#1331
body:
## What

**Image loading** with Kadence Blocks: background pictures of rows further down a page now load as the visitor scrolls near them (#1329). This also fixes the Advanced Slider script from 1.3.166, which stopped WordPress's curly quotes in the rest of the post content (#1331).

Resolves #1329
Resolves #1331

## Why

Kadence Blocks writes a row's background picture into the page's CSS, so browsers fetched every row's picture with the page, wherever the row was. Backgrounds have no lazy loading of their own. On one Kadence home page (PageSpeed mobile, 1.3.166), a call-to-action row about 30,000 px down on a phone fetched a 566 KiB WebP with the page.

## How

- New `includes/class-seoprostack-kadence-rows.php` (`SEOProStack_Kadence_Rows`), loaded by Image loading when Kadence Blocks is active, front end only. It filters `render_block_kadence/rowlayout` at priority 30, the same as the hero.
- A row qualifies when it has `kbVersion` 2, the normal background tab, and a picture that is not parallax (its own, its overlay's, a tablet or phone one, or a dynamic one). It must also have a safe `uniqueID`, carry no `data-kadence-lazy-` attribute (Kadence's own optimizer), and not be the row the post opens with (that row is preloaded or sized by the hero code).
- Before such a row: a style that sets `background-image:none!important` under `html.sps-rows`, until the row has `sps-near`. After it: a one-line script that has the row watched.
- Once a page, before the first such row, a script adds `sps-rows` to `<html>`. It does so only while the document is loading and only if IntersectionObserver exists. It then gives each row `sps-near` within 1,250 px of the window, Chrome's own lazy-loading distance on a fast connection. At load, rows whose own script did not run are watched too.
- Without JavaScript, in an old browser, or when an optimiser runs the script late, nothing waits. Filter: `seoprostack_kadence_row_wait`.
- **#1331:** `wptexturize()` runs on the content after blocks are rendered and treats a `<` in an inline script as the start of a tag. It escapes `&` up to the next `>` (the first draft of this script failed with a SyntaxError) and leaves the rest of the content without curly quotes. Scripts printed in post content (the slider's and this one) now have no `<`: loops use `Array.prototype.forEach.call()`. The docblocks say why.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`: all passed. `scripts/preflight-plugin.sh`: passed.
- Test site (WordPress 7.1.4, PHP 8.3, Kadence 1.6.0, Kadence Blocks 3.9.0), Chromium at 412×823, DPR 1.75:
  - The opening row's picture was preloaded and fetched at once, and so was the second row's (just below the first screen).
  - A row 5,000 px down was fetched only when scrolled within reach, then shown with its overlay (screenshot checked).
  - A parallax row behaved as before.
  - With JavaScript off, every picture loaded with the page.
  - No console errors, and the debug log was empty.
- `wptexturize()` check (`wp eval-file`): each script, between two quoted paragraphs, came out unchanged, and the paragraph after it got curly quotes. A page paragraph with straight quotes after the rows now renders curly ones.
- Live home page (`<site>`) with the style and script injected before the row, on a throttled phone (Playwright, 1.6 Mbps, 150 ms, 4x CPU, one run each):

  | | Pictures by load | Load |
  |---|---|---|
  | Before | 12 (2,318 KiB) | 14.3 s |
  | After | 10 (1,398 KiB) | 10.0 s |

  The 566 KiB picture was fetched only after scrolling to the row, which then showed it. No console errors.

title: GH#1333: Image loading: Advanced Slider slides at the size each screen needs
body:
## What

Resolves #1333.

Kadence Blocks Pro Advanced Slider slides named the picture's full upload, so phones got it too. Each slide's picture now comes at the size the screen needs, as #1221 does for the row a page opens with, and is never less sharp than before.

## How

- `includes/class-seoprostack-kadence-slider.php` (`SEOProStack_Kadence_Slider`):
  - For each `kadence/slide` with a normal background, no gradient, and `cover`, `contain` or unset size, `SEOProStack_Hero_Picture::get()` finds the same-proportion copies (uploads folder or Media in cloud storage). One `_prime_post_caches()` call loads the attachments.
  - Before the slider: a style hides its slide pictures under `html.sps-sizing` until the slider has `sps-sized`, plus a once-per-page script. After the slider: a one-line call with the pictures.
  - The call measures the slide box and reads each slide's computed `background-size`. It picks the narrowest file ≥ painted px × DPR × 1.1, else the slide's own.
  - It writes one `!important` rule per slide class into a head `<style>`, so Splide's loop clones get it. #1312's wait rules are more specific and still win.
  - ResizeObserver and a `matchMedia` resolution watch only ever grow the file.
  - New filter: `seoprostack_kadence_slider_sizes`. Block themes are skipped.
- `SEOProStack_Image_Loading::kadence_preload()`: when a page opens with the slider and `SEOProStack_Kadence_Slider::opens()` says it is sized, the head's preload of the slide's own picture goes only in `<noscript>`. The call then preloads the chosen copy at high priority. If the slider is not sized after all, that preload is printed before it. Both come from the new `preload_html()`, so #1326's `litespeed_next_gen()` names LiteSpeed's WebP copy in each (now replacing every copy of the tag).
- Growth re-reads each slide's `background-size`, in case the theme switches contain to cover at another width (review).
- `SEOProStack_Hero_Picture::for_script()` (new; used by both the slider and the `SEOProStack_Kadence_Hero` script) passes each file as `url(…)`. LiteSpeed Cache's WebP replacement rewrites every `url()` in the page, so the scripts and their preloads now get LiteSpeed's `.webp` copy, as the block CSS does (#1326). This also fixes the hero row fetching the JPEG on LiteSpeed's WebP pages.
- None of the new scripts or the style contain `<`, so wptexturize leaves them alone (#1331).

## Verification

Test site: WordPress 7.1.4, PHP 8.3, Kadence 1.6.0, Kadence Blocks 3.9.0, Kadence Blocks Pro 2.9.0. A 16:9 fade slider of 2048×1536 uploads with 768/1024/1536 copies, one 2500×2500, gradient/contain/auto slides, and a carousel lower down. Chromium:

| Screen | First slide file | Painted px |
|---|---|---|
| 412×823 DPR 1.75 | 1024 copy | 721 |
| 393×852 DPR 3 | 1536 copy | 1,179 |
| 768×1024 DPR 2 | full upload | 1,536 |
| 1350×940 DPR 1 | 1536 copy | 1,350 |

- The preload named the same file the slide showed. One file per picture, never the full one as well. Gradient and `auto` slides were unchanged. No console errors, and no PHP messages from SEO Pro Stack.
- JavaScript off: every slide's own picture, as before. With the LiteSpeed rewrite, the `<noscript>` preload names `slide1.jpg.webp`, and only that file is fetched for the first slide.
- A contain slide that a test style makes cover from 900px: loaded at 412 (768 copy) and widened to 1000, it took the 1536 copy. Without the style it stayed contain and took the 1024.
- Copies at their own addresses: slides use an `image-set()` of the chosen copy, and the preload names its `.jpg.webp`.
- A buffer filter repeating LiteSpeed Cache 7.9.3's `url()` rewrite: the slides, the hero row and both preloads named the `.jpg.webp`. No JPEG was fetched.
- Hero row regression (#1221): phone and desktop both take the 1536 copy and preload it.
- Filter off: the old head preload, no sizing tags.
- wptexturize: the slider, rows, size script, size call and size style all come out unchanged, with curly quotes after them.
- `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`: all passed.

title: GH#1339: Kadence row background slider's first slide at full width before Splide mounts
body:
## What

Image loading with Kadence Blocks: a row background slider's first slide now paints at its full width from the first paint, not only after the slider's script has run.

## Why

Kadence Blocks resets the slider list's margin and padding only under `.kb-splide` (`.kb-splide .splide__list{…;margin:0!important;padding:0!important}`, `kadence-splide.min.css`), a class `kb-splide-init` adds when Splide mounts. Until then the `<ul class="splide__list">` keeps the browser's or theme's padding, so the first slide is about 40 px narrower. When the script runs, the slide widens, and Chrome records a new, larger LCP for the same picture. LCP then waits for the slider's footer scripts, or with Cloudflare Rocket Loader for the page's `load`.

Three Kadence home pages opening with a row background slider (keyed PageSpeed mobile on 1.3.169): scores 85, 88 and 81; LCP 4.4, 3.9 and 5.0 s; observed element render delay 494, 429 and 400 ms. Details in #1339.

## How

`SEOProStack_Kadence_Rows::around_row()` (`includes/class-seoprostack-kadence-rows.php`) calls the new `slider_style()`. Before the page's first row whose `backgroundSettingTab` is `slider` and whose markup has `kb-blocks-bg-slider`, it prints once per page:

```html
<style class="seoprostack-bg-slider" data-no-optimize="1">.kb-blocks-bg-slider .splide__list{margin:0!important;padding:0!important}</style>
```

These are Kadence's own values once the slider has started, so nothing changes then. The style has no `<` or `&` (#1331). Filter `seoprostack_kadence_bg_slider_width` (default true, the parsed row block). The issue suggested `…_fix`; the name follows the other Kadence filters' "what it keeps" wording. Docs: README Image loading and filter list; `changelog.txt`, `readme.txt` and `README.md` under Unreleased.

## Verification

Test site: WordPress 7.1.4, PHP 8.3, Kadence 1.6.0, Kadence Blocks 3.9.0, Kadence Blocks Pro 2.9.0. Two pages: one opening with a 2-slide fade row background slider, one with it as the second row. Playwright phone 412×823 @1.75, throttled (1.6 Mbps, 150 ms, 4× CPU).

| Check | Before (`?nofix` via the filter) | After |
|---|---|---|
| First slide width before Splide mounts / after (row 348 px) | 314 / 348 | 348 / 348 (both pages) |
| Splide's scripts held 4 s (as Rocket Loader): LCP entries for the picture | 1,912 ms (125,600 px²), then 4,656 ms (139,200 px²) | 1,864 ms (139,200 px²) only |
| JavaScript off: slide width | 314 | 348 |

- The style is printed once per page; the fade still runs after mount.
- `wptexturize()` leaves the style unchanged; the content around the row still gets curly quotes.
- No PHP messages from the plugin.
- `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan` passes.

Live check after release: keyed PageSpeed mobile on the three home pages.

Resolves #1339
