title: GH#1337: preload the first Kadence picture from the head when its block sets its height
body:
## What

Image loading: when a post or page opens with a full-width Kadence Blocks row or Advanced Slider that sets its height for the screen size, the copy of its first picture that the screen needs is preloaded from the head, before any stylesheet, instead of from the script after the block.

Resolves #1337

## Why

The scripts that choose the copy (`SEOProStack_Kadence_Hero`, #1221; `SEOProStack_Kadence_Slider`, #1333) run after the block, where they can measure it. Their preload goes in only once the parser has read the header and the block, after every stylesheet in the head, and the picture then shares the connection with them (#1337: resource load delay 349 ms on a Kadence home page opening with a slider).

## How

- New `includes/class-seoprostack-kadence-early.php` (`SEOProStack_Kadence_Early`): a head script, printed only under the Kadence theme (or a child theme of it) on a page without a sidebar (`kadence()->has_sidebar()`: with one, `.has-sidebar .wp-site-blocks .content-container .alignfull` keeps full-width blocks in the content column), for a block with `align` full (a slider: `sliderType` slider and no left or right padding on any screen size), a picture `SEOProStack_Hero_Picture::get()` finds smaller copies of, and a height for at least one Kadence screen size:
  - slider: `sliderRatio` (default `12-5`, tablet and phone inherit), or `minHeight` in `heightUnit` with `heightType` fixed;
  - row: `minHeight`, `minHeightTablet`, `minHeightMobile` in `minHeightUnit` (px, vh, vw; em, rem and % left alone).
  While the document loads, it picks the height for the screen size (767 / 1024 px), measures `100vh` on an empty element (phones' address bar), works out the fewest device pixels the picture can paint (cover: max of width and height × proportions; contain: min; × DPR × 1.1), preloads the narrowest copy at least that wide at high priority, and records it in `window.seoprostackEarly`.
- `SEOProStack_Kadence_Hero::start()` prints it for a row. `SEOProStack_Image_Loading::kadence_preload()` prints it for a slider, after the `<noscript>` preload, through the new `SEOProStack_Kadence_Slider::early()`.
- The scripts after the block take the head's copy when it is at least their own choice and then skip their preload; otherwise they take and preload their own, as before. The head's copy is never smaller than theirs, because a block's content can only make it taller.
- Files go to the script as `url(…)` (`for_script()`), so LiteSpeed Cache's WebP replacement names its copy in the head's preload too.
- Same `SCRIPT_ATTRS` as the other scripts (`data-no-optimize`, `data-no-defer`, `data-cfasync="false"`).
- Filter `seoprostack_kadence_head_preload` (default true; the block's attributes).

### Why a script, not `imagesrcset`/`imagesizes`

The issue proposed a `<link imagesrcset imagesizes>`. Instead, the script reuses the after-block scripts' exact choice rule, so they know which copy the head fetched. With `imagesrcset` the browser may pick on its own (cache, network, DPR rounding), and the after-block script would have to guess from Resource Timing. LiteSpeed's WebP replacement also rewrites `url()`, not `imagesrcset`.

## Verification

Test site: WordPress 7.1.4, PHP 8.3, Kadence 1.6.0, Kadence Blocks 3.9.0, Kadence Blocks Pro 2.9.0. Chromium at 412×823 @1.75, 393×852 @3, 768×1024 @2 and 1350×940 @1, with the head script and without it (filter off).

- Full-width 16:9 Advanced Slider, and full-width rows of 500 px, 80 vh (90 vh on phones), and 400 px with a background slider: on every screen the shown copy is the same as before, fetched once. The head's choice equals the measuring script's.
- A row with no minimum height, and a row that is not full width: no head script; unchanged.
- The 500 px row's page with `_kad_post_layout` right (body class `has-sidebar`): no head script, the script after the row still prints; without the sidebar, both (f806fa0f, after CodeRabbit's review).
- JavaScript off: the head script is in the HTML but does nothing; the `<noscript>` preload of the block's own picture and the requests are unchanged.
- LiteSpeed WebP simulation (`url()` rewrite plus `litespeed_buffer_after`): the head's preload names the `.jpg.webp` the CSS shows, fetched once, with no JPEG.
- Copies at their own addresses on: the head's preload names the copy each block shows, fetched once (phone and desktop).
- Phone, network (150 ms, 1.6 Mbps) and CPU (4×) slowed, final build, three loads each, same copy in both variants:

  | Page | Picture requested, head / off | Last LCP (median), head / off |
  |---|---|---|
  | 16:9 Advanced Slider | 350–408 / 684–708 ms | 1,596 / 1,872 ms |
  | Row, 500 px | 183–184 / 513–515 ms | 1,596 / 1,760 ms |
  | Row, 400 px, background slider | 181–190 / 627–643 ms | 2,124 / 2,696 ms |
  | Row, 80 vh (90 vh phones) | 180–193 / 515–519 ms | 2,676 / 2,832 ms |
- The head script is printed in `wp_head`, not in post content, so `wptexturize()` (#1331) does not apply.
- `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`: all passed.
- No PHP messages in `debug.log` from page loads.

Live (point-in-time, 7 November 2026): all 11 Kadence home pages checked open with an `alignfull` row or slider. Four set a height (two 16:9 Advanced Sliders, rows of 400 and 975 px) and get the head preload. The rest are as tall as their content and are unchanged. Keyed PageSpeed before and after follows the release deploy.

title: GH#1341: every Kadence row and column background at the size the screen needs
body: ## What Image loading: every Kadence Blocks row and column background picture now comes at the size the screen needs, not only the row a page opens with (#1221) and Advanced Slider slides (#1333). Column pictures also wait until the visitor scrolls near them, as rows' do (#1329). Resolves #1341 ## Why Kadence Blocks writes the picture a row or column names, usually the full upload, into the page's CSS. Phones fetch the whole file even where it paints a small box. On one Kadence home page (1.3.169, keyed PageSpeed mobile 83, LCP 4.8 s), the LCP element was a column's background: a 1365×1024 upload of 293 KiB painting 126×189. Two more columns had 134 and 85 KiB pictures for boxes about 150 and 114 px wide. ## How All in `includes/class-seoprostack-kadence-rows.php` (`SEOProStack_Kadence_Rows`), extending #1329's wait: - New `render_block_kadence/column` filter (`around_column()`, priority 30). For a column with Kadence's normal background type and a picture: - before the column, a style (`class="seoprostack-rows" data-column`) hides `.kadence-column:not(.sps-near) > .kt-inside-inner-col`'s picture under `html.sps-rows`; - inside the column, before its last ``, the one-line call `seoprostackRows(document.currentScript, '', , 1)`. Inside rather than after, because Kadence places a row's columns with `:nth-child(… of *:not(style))`: a style beside them does not shift that count, but a script would. - Rows (#1329) and columns pass their picture's files to the call when `SEOProStack_Hero_Picture::get()` finds smaller copies. Each file is written as `url(…)` (`for_script()`, #1333) so LiteSpeed Cache's WebP replacement rewrites it. The JSON uses `JSON_HEX_TAG | JSON_HEX_AMP`. - Sized only when the picture is `cover`, `contain` or unset, not fixed or parallax, and has no dynamic background. Rows must also have no tablet or phone background of their own. Columns must have nothing on hover that changes the picture: Kadence's hover colour sets `background-image: none` on `:hover`, and a hover picture or gradient replaces it, but the copy is set with `!important` and would win. Those columns still wait. - Script: - when the call runs, a block already within 1,250 px of the window is handled at once (`getBoundingClientRect`); others when the IntersectionObserver finds them near, as before; - it reads the box's computed `background-size` and sets, with `!important`, the narrowest file at least the painted pixels × DPR × 1.1 (then its AVIF/WebP `image-set()` with Copies at their own addresses), and only then adds `sps-near`, so only that file is fetched; - a ResizeObserver and a resolution `matchMedia` swap in a larger copy, never a smaller one; - the load-time pass now covers columns too; - no `<` in the script (#1331). - New filters: `seoprostack_kadence_column_wait` (parsed column block) and `seoprostack_kadence_bg_sizes` (parsed row or column block), both default true. ## Verification Test site: WordPress 7.1.4, PHP 8.3, Kadence 1.6.0, Kadence Blocks 3.9.0, Kadence Blocks Pro 2.9.0. The test page opens with a two-column row whose first column has a 2048×1536 picture (cover). Then come a 400 px row 1,500 px down, and three columns 2,500 px further: cover; cover with a hover colour; contain with a 2500×2500 picture. | Screen | First column | Row | Cover column | Contain column | |---|---|---|---|---| | 412×823 @1.75 | 348×359 → 1024 | 348×400 → 1536 | 1024 | 768 | | 393×852 @3 | full (≈1,580 px needed) | full | full | 1536 | | 768×1024 @2 | 1536 | 656×400 → 1536 | 197×359 → 1536 | 768 | | 1350×940 @1 | 573×359 → 768 | 1178×400 → 1536 | 768 | 768 | - Every choice is at least painted × DPR × 1.1. Each picture was fetched once, never the full one alongside a copy. Before scrolling, only the first row's column loaded (on the tablet also the row within 1,250 px). - Hover colour column: its own picture; on hover `background-image: none` and its colour, as before. - JavaScript off: every row and column showed its own picture. - `wptexturize()`: the calls keep `&&`, and text after them still gets curly quotes. - No console errors. No PHP messages in `debug.log` from page loads. - Throttled phone (150 ms, 1.6 Mbps, CPU 4×), three loads each: - first column's copy requested at 519–601 ms, against 479–875 ms for its full picture with the column wait off; - last LCP 1,196–1,272 ms against 9,104–9,516 ms. With the wait off, the columns further down fetched their full uploads during the load and shared the slowed line. - `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`: all passed. title: GH#1347: size Kadence background pictures that have no attachment ID
body:
## What

Image loading: Kadence Blocks row, column, hero row and Advanced Slider slide background pictures saved without their Media Library ID now come at the size the screen needs too, as those with an ID have since #1221, #1333 and #1341.

Resolves #1347

## Why

`SEOProStack_Hero_Picture::get($id, $url)` returned null when `$id` was 0, because `meta()` needs an ID above 0. Kadence rows saved with `bgImg` but no `bgImgID` (blocks from imported templates, or a picture given by address) kept the full upload. After the 1.3.171 rollout, a phone survey of the Kadence home pages with row pictures found none sized on four of them (2, 1, 1 and 1 rows): each row has `bgImg` only. `attachment_url_to_postid()` finds the attachment for each, with 3 to 5 smaller copies.

## How

All in `includes/class-seoprostack-hero-picture.php`:

- `get()` uses the saved ID when it is above 0, else new `url_id($url)`.
- `url_id()`: when the address can go in CSS (`css_url()`), `attachment_url_to_postid()`, kept per address for a day in the object cache (group `seoprostack`, key `hero_url_id_` plus 32 hex of the address's SHA-256, 0 cached too), so each picture is looked up once while the cache holds it. Without a persistent object cache it is one query per picture per page view, on uncached views only (the page cache holds the result).
- `attachment_url_to_postid()` matches only this site's uploads address of an attachment's own file (or its `-scaled` one), so a CDN's, a size copy's or a theme's address stays 0 and the picture stays as the block names it. `meta()` still checks the address is in the attachment's folder.
- Callers (`kadence-rows.php`, `kadence-hero.php`, `kadence-slider.php`, and the head script through them) are unchanged. The slider's `_prime_post_caches()` skips slides without an ID; they are looked up one by one.

## Verification

Test site: WordPress 7.1.4, PHP 8.3, Kadence 1.6.0, Kadence Blocks 3.9.0, Kadence Blocks Pro 2.9.0.

- `get()` direct: attachment 8 with ID and with ID 0 (and `""`) give the same copies (300, 768, 1024, 1536, 2048); the theme's `screenshot.png` and the attachment's `medium` copy give null.
- Test page made from the #1337 hero page's first block and the #1341 page's rows and columns with every `bgImgID` removed, plus a row with the theme's picture:
  - head script (`seoprostack-early`) and hero script byte-identical to the page with IDs;
  - `seoprostackRows` calls: first column, row and cover column with 2048×1536 copies, contain column with 2500×2500 copies, hover-colour column 0 (waits, unsized), as with IDs; the theme picture row waits unsized.
- No PHP messages in `debug.log` from page loads.
- `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`: all passed.

title: GH#1351: fix: deploy gives extracted files the current time; only a newer version purges the page cache
body:
## What

Stops a multisite network from purging its whole page cache on every request after a rollout, and makes the deploy load new code at once.

- `scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh` (`swap_plugin_folder()`): after `unzip` into the staging folder, `find … -exec touch -c {} +` gives the files the current time before the swap; a failure there falls back to `wp plugin install --force` as any other swap failure does. The release zip's fixed 2020-01-01 times (reproducible builds) made OPcache keep the previous version's compiled code, and kept `filemtime()` asset versions at `1577836800` across releases.
- `SEOProStack_Page_Cache::after_update()`: returns without purging or storing when the stored version is newer than the running one (`version_compare`), so a request still on older compiled code can no longer alternate full purges with the new code.
- README.md (page cache after updates; changelog), changelog.txt, readme.txt.

## Why

Evidence in #1351: on an 11-site network after the 1.3.172 rollout, web requests linked assets with `ver=1.3.171` while WP-CLI ran 1.3.172; `seoprostack_page_cache_purged` flipped between the two versions, and each flip purged everything (backtrace: `after_update` → `litespeed_purge_all`). Touching the plugin's files had web requests on 1.3.172 within 2 s and the stored version held.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`: all passed. `shellcheck -x scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh scripts/deploy-sites.sh`, `bash -n`: clean.
- Rollout of 1.3.172 to the remaining single sites with this branch's deploy script: results in the comment below (file times, asset `ver=`, stored version).

title: GH#1355: fix: Used CSS keeps rules for elements scripts create with an ID
body:
Resolves #1355

## What

`SEOProStack_Used_Css_Match::added()` (`includes/class-seoprostack-used-css-match.php`) now counts an `#id` the page's HTML lacks as present when it is a word in the page's running scripts, as it already did for classes and elements (#1260). Before, it returned `false` for every ID, so ID rules were kept only when the served HTML had the ID.

Readabler's `readabler.min.js` (runs as the page loads) builds its voice navigation panel with `t.id = e` (`e = "mdp-readabler-voice-navigation"`); only `#mdp-readabler-voice-navigation{position:fixed;…}` and `#mdp-readabler-voice-navigation[aria-hidden=true]{display:none}` place and hide it. With Used CSS on and the full stylesheets blocked, the panel sat below the footer, 23,801 px tall at 1280 px wide.

Docblocks of `SEOProStack_Used_Css_Match` and `SEOProStack_Used_Css_Scripts`, README.md (Load the CSS each page uses first), changelog.txt and readme.txt (`= Unreleased =`) updated.

## Cost

Measured on the affected page: at most 70 more rules, 11.9 KB before compression, from Readabler's 93.7 KB stylesheet. Scripts that wait for the visitor are still not read. No cache version change: the stylesheet cache holds parsed rules only; matching runs per page, and the update purges the page cache.

## Checks

- `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`: all passed.
- After release, on that page: the used CSS includes `#mdp-readabler-voice-navigation[aria-hidden=true]{display:none}`, and the screenshot comparison's blocked desktop footer shot matches the reference.

title: GH#1349: fix: deploy cron race check matches WordPress's full log line
body:
## What

Network deploys kept ending `FAIL` with `new_log_lines=2` (1.3.169, 1.3.171 and 1.3.173 on one 11-site network) on core's cron race for `seoprostack_front_verify`. #1300 was meant to show those as `WARN cron race HOOK`, but `classify_log()` (`scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh`) required nothing after `Error code: could_not_set`. WordPress 6.1 and later's `wp-cron.php` goes on with `, Error message: The cron event list could not be saved., Data: {...}`, so no real race line was ever let through.

The pattern now also accepts that tail. Everything else still fails the install, as before: another hook, another error code, text before the message, or anything after the code that is not core's `Error message` and `Data` tail.

## Evidence

- Old vs new classifier on the real line from the 1.3.173 deploy plus near misses (`classify-test.sh`, a local helper that feeds lines to `classify_log()` from a given file):
  - old: real `reschedule` and `unschedule` lines → `line`, `line` (counted, so FAIL)
  - new: → one `race seoprostack_front_verify`; other hook, `invalid_schedule`, prefixed text, unrelated warning, trailing junk → `line` each; the bare form still → `race`.
- A temporary must-use trace on the network during the 1.3.174 deploy (logging only, removed afterwards) logged every run, reschedule and unschedule of `seoprostack_front_verify` with PID, SAPI, `DOING_CRON`, `WP_CLI` and the command. Two processes run the event on the same sites: the host's network runner (`wp-cron.php` per site, with core's lock) and the deploy's `wp cron event run seoprostack_front_verify`, which takes no lock. So the race is between the deploy and the site's own runner, the case #1300 is for. No third runner showed.
- `shellcheck -x scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh scripts/deploy-sites.sh`: no findings.

## Files

- `scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh`: `classify_log()` pattern and comment.
- `RELEASING.md`: the race's cause and the full message.

Core file: the starter port is wpallstars/wp-plugin-starter-template-for-ai-coding#646 (the #1300 port); it needs this pattern too.

## Not in this PR

Step 4 of #1349 (`seoprostack_keep_pages_cached` unschedule-only errors outside deploys) is a separate plugin question and moves to its own issue.

title: GH#1363: Keep pages cached opens every header, footer and home page link first, also on networks
body:
## Summary

**Keep pages cached** now opens every link in the header, the footer and the home page before the rest of the site, also on a network (Resolves #1363).

- `includes/class-seoprostack-keep-cached-pages.php`
  - `MAIN_MAX` 50 → 150. New `COVERED_MAX` (50): where LiteSpeed Cache's crawler or WP-Optimize's preload covers the rest, the newest pages and posts still fill only up to 50 in all, so a small site opens no more than before ahead of the crawler.
  - `network()` plans in two rounds: round 1 every site's home page and first header links (`of_site(NETWORK_MAIN_MAX, NETWORK_MAIN_MAX, false)`, so every site still gets them in one round, #1240); round 2 each site's other main pages with its home page read (`of_site(MAIN_MAX, NETWORK_MORE_MAX, true)` less round 1's). Room is checked for a site's whole list in the round, so the queue's `MAX` never cuts one. `network_end()` moves round 1 to round 2 at the first site, and round 2 to done.
  - `to_open(true)` (`wp seoprostack keep-cached --network`) lists both rounds.
- `includes/class-seoprostack-keep-cached-queue.php`: the queue keeps `round` (1 or 2); `fill_later()` resets it to 1 with `site` for a network purge; `plan()` passes it and stores the next one.
- Docs: README.md (Keep pages cached, Changelog), readme.txt, changelog.txt, the feature's file header.

## Evidence

Live sites, logged out, about 45 minutes after the 1.3.174 deploy's purge:

- Single site with LiteSpeed Cache's crawler on: 49 of the 53 pages its home page links to answered from LiteSpeed's cache (0.08 to 0.44 s); 4 home-page links were uncached (1.3 to 2.3 s). `to_open(false)` planned 50 (`covered()` yes) and none of the 4; LiteSpeed's crawler had 1,034 sitemap addresses at about 41 minutes a pass.
- The branch's planner loaded on that site from a renamed copy (`wp eval-file`, read-only): 56 pages planned, the same first 50 in the same order, the 4 at positions 51 to 54.
- On an 11-site network, the same check: round 1 plans 86 (10 a site, 4 on sites with fewer), round 2 138 more, none in both rounds. Per site, round 1 + round 2 equals that site's main pages after `clean()` (16, 37 and 41 on three sites, read with `of_site(150, 1, true)`), or 25 where it has fewer. Before, the site with 37 main pages got 10 of them and 15 newest posts. `page_html()` reads each site's home page from the main site's context (`switch_to_blog()`): 470 to 840 KB in 0.15 to 0.38 s.

## How to check

1. `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`: passed locally.
2. On a single site with the crawler on: `wp seoprostack keep-cached --dry-run` lists every header, footer and home page link (above 50 where there are more), in that order.
3. On a network: `wp seoprostack keep-cached --network --dry-run` lists every site's first pages, then each site's other main pages.

title: GH#1367: fix: Load plugins only where needed keeps what it learned when plugins refresh update caches
body:
## Summary

Load plugins only where needed stops forgetting what the site's pages learned when other plugins refresh update caches and bookkeeping options from wp-admin, AJAX or WP-CLI.

- `record_write()` (`includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-loading.php`): an option named only by an MD5 counts as a record when its value is EDD Software Licensing's update cache shape, exactly `timeout` and `value`. New `update_cache()` reads the value from the hook (`add_option` passes the new value, `update_option` the stored one; both now registered with two arguments) or, for `delete_option`, matches the stored row as a string without unserializing it.

title: GH#1369: fix: deploy check notes a cron event the site's cron ran meanwhile
body:
## What

`run_site_cron()` (`scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh`) lists the plugin's scheduled events, then runs each with `wp cron event run`. A single event the site's own cron runs in between (here `seoprostack_keep_settings`, scheduled once after an update) makes WP-CLI exit 1 with `Invalid cron event '<hook>'`, and the 1.3.175 network deploy reported a FAIL for a site whose plugin updated and loaded fine.

## Change

- Exit non-zero with `Invalid cron event '<hook>'` for that hook, and no fatal or database error in the output: a note, `cron <hook> ran meanwhile`, in the site's warnings. It is not counted as run here (`cron=4/5`) and not added to `CRON_HOOKS_RUN`, since it did not run in the deploy's process.
- Every other non-zero exit, and any fatal or database error, is still a failure.
- `CRON_WARNED` now carries the warning text, so a single site shows the actual note instead of always "cron timed out".

Deploy tooling only, so no changelog entry (`STANDARDS.md` docs rule).

## Verification

- `shellcheck -x scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh scripts/deploy-sites.sh`: clean.
- The branch order, checked on sample outputs: this hook gone → note; another hook's message → failure; fatal plus the message → failure; other exit 1 → failure; exit 0 → ran; exit 0 with fatal text → failure.
- Read-only, on the affected network site: `wp cron event list` shows only `seoprostack_keep_settings_daily`. The single event is gone, consistent with the site's cron having run it.

title: GH#1372: feat: keep text still while web fonts load (metric-matched fallback fonts)
body:
## What

New Speed feature, on by default: **Keep text still while web fonts load** (`SEOProStack_Font_Fallbacks`, settings `font_fallbacks` and `font_fallbacks_skip`).

While a page's web fonts load (`font-display: swap`, as the Kadence theme's Google Fonts), text shows in the browser's default font, then moves when the web font arrives. For each web font the page declares that the bundled measurements know, this adds `"<Family> Fallback"` faces (local Arial / Liberation Sans / Arimo, or Times New Roman / Liberation Serif / Tinos for serif fonts) and `"<Family> Fallback 2"` faces (Roboto / Noto Serif, for Android), sized with `size-adjust` and ascent/descent/line-gap overrides, regular and bold separately. Capitals (`U+41-5A`) and spaces (`U+20,U+A0`) get faces of their own when their ratio differs from the small letters' by 1% or more. A small inline script starts loading them as the head is read. Each `font-family` and `--*font-family` declaration in the page's own `<style>` elements gets them after the web font.

## Files

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-font-fallbacks.php`: the feature (page buffer, font detection, faces, stack rewrite). `face()` sizes small letters, capitals and spaces; `PARTS`/`REST` hold the `unicode-range`s.
- `includes/class-seoprostack-setup.php`: registered after Used CSS, so its buffer runs first and leaves Used CSS's stylesheet copies alone.
- `includes/class-seoprostack-used-css-links.php`: `stylesheet_file()` (shared `site_file()` with `script_file()`), to read same-site font stylesheets.
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-speed-plan.php`: listed with the other on-by-default features.
- `assets/font-metrics/metrics.json` (116 KB, 1,873 families, 758 with bold) and `LICENSE.txt`: heights from `@capsizecss/metrics` 4.4.0 (MIT, SEEK); widths of a–z, A–Z and space (letters weighted by English frequency) measured from the fonts Google Fonts serves at 400 and 700 (`text=` subsets, `hmtx`/`cmap` read, no file kept). 23 fonts Google Fonts does not serve at 400 (Arial, Segoe UI, -apple-system, …) are left out.
- `scripts/update-font-metrics.sh` + `.js`: refresh (pattern: `scripts/update-brand-icons.sh`).
- `README.md`, `changelog.txt`, `readme.txt`: feature section, lists, filter, credit, changelogs.

## Why three sizes, not one

A single `size-adjust` (Capsize's `xWidthAvg`, the first version of this PR) is right for average text only. Poppins Bold against Arial Bold: capitals 0.97, small letters 1.11, space 0.76, so "USED CAR OF THE WEEK" came out 19% wider sized by the small letters, 1.6% with the three sizes.

Layout check (`wrap-eval.mjs`, kept out of the repo): load the page, wait for its fonts, record every element's box, switch each known web font to the fallback faces, record again; CLS for the first screen from the moved boxes. It reproduces the throttled loads exactly (0.1121/0.12, 0.0513/0.0513, 0.03/0.0299, 0.0141/0.0141). 78 pages on 13 sites (home + up to 5 linked pages):

| | 412 px: CLS sum | blocks changed | pages > 0.01 | 1,350 px: CLS sum | blocks changed | pages > 0.01 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| one size (`xWidthAvg`) | 0.30 | 231 | 8 | 0.23 | 107 | 3 |
| small letters only | 0.93 | 340 | 19 | 2.70 | 197 | 31 |
| three sizes (this PR) | 0.32 | 201 | 8 | 0.20 | 85 | 3 |

Widths of 878 texts from those pages (advances from the font files): mean error 1.56% against 2.22%, 90th percentile 2.96% against 4.22%, texts ≥ 300 px p90 16 px against 30.5 px.

The 412 px sum for three sizes is held up by one heading: a 44 px h1 365 px wide in its web font, 363 px in the fallback, in a 364 px box (0.11). Any width match has such knife edges; three sizes have fewer of them.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`: all pass.
- `scripts/test-site.sh` (Docker, WordPress latest, PHP 8.3) with the Kadence theme, Lexend body and Poppins 700 headings: feature off CLS 0.001; on CLS 0 (2 loads, three-size faces; `U+20,U+A0` and `U+41-5A` faces in the head). Google Fonts link and Load Google Fonts locally both detected; Kadence's `--global-body-font-family` and `--global-heading-font-family` rewritten once each; feature off leaves no trace; debug.log empty.
- Prototype (same faces added in the browser) on 12 Kadence home pages, PageSpeed phone throttling (1 load with, 3 without): CLS fell on 7 (0.1896 → 0.0007, 0.266 → 0.1211, 0.1654 → 0.0002, 0.0619 → 0.0002, 0.0449 → 0.0001, 0.0187 → 0.0003, 0.0014 → 0.0003), within 0.002 on 3, rose on 2 (0.0212 → 0.0299, 0.0051 → 0.0141; both under 0.1).
- Not measured: Android phones (the Roboto/Noto Serif set) and PageSpeed's own Linux fonts; to check with PageSpeed Insights after the deploy.

Resolves #1372

title: GH#1383: feat: redirect to the main address before WordPress loads
body:
## What

New Speed feature, on by default: **Redirect to the main address before WordPress loads** (`SEOProStack_Host_Redirect`, setting `host_redirect`).

A request for a site's other address (`www.` added or taken away) reached WordPress, whose 301 (`redirect_canonical()` or a domain mapping plugin) no page cache keeps: `x-redirect-by: WordPress`, `x-litespeed-cache: miss`. First byte took 0.6 to 5.0 s on five Hostinger sites behind Cloudflare (7 November 2026). The server now answers with the same redirect from a marked block at the top of the root `.htaccess`, before PHP starts.

## How

- **Only redirects the site already makes.** Each site address's `www.` twin (that is not itself a site's address) is opened from the server with `wp_remote_get` (no redirects followed, `?seoprostack-host-check=<random>`, sent straight to this server through `SEOProStack_Keep_Cached_Requests::resolver()`, as Keep pages cached does since #1242). A rule is added only for a 301 or 308 to that host's home page.
- **Rules:** that host, GET or HEAD only, not `/.well-known/` on the request line (`THE_REQUEST`: WordPress's own rules send a missing file to `index.php` and the rules run again with that URI), not the check's query string; `R=301` to the same path, keeping the query string.
- **Schedule:** WP-Cron `seoprostack_host_redirect_check` daily, plus a single `soon` event a minute after the home option, a site's address or the network's sites change. Rules whose main host is no longer a site's address go at once.
- **Loop guard:** a `wp_redirect` filter drops a rule when WordPress sends a visitor to the address that rule redirects from (an address changed outside WordPress's hooks).
- **Server detection:** WP-CLI cannot tell `$is_apache` or the root folder, so both are noted from the main site's admin and WP-Cron web requests (`seoprostack_host_redirect_server`). `get_home_path()` is used only when it holds `ABSPATH` and an `index.php`. Nothing is written until then, or on servers that do not read `.htaccess`.
- **Writes** go through `SEOProStack_Hardening::files_write()` (now public). The block is rewritten when an update changes its rules (hash in `seoprostack_host_redirect`), retried from admin and cron while unwritable, and removed when switched off, on deactivation (network-wide or from the main site) and on uninstall.
- **Multisite:** one block, written by the main site, for every site's address.
- **Panel:** lists the addresses redirected, or why nothing is written (waiting for a web request, a server that does not read `.htaccess`, an unwritable file with the lines to add).

## Files

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-host-redirect.php` (new)
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-hardening.php`: `files_write()` public
- `includes/class-seoprostack-setup.php`: FEATURES list
- `uninstall.php`: block and both options removed
- `README.md`, `readme.txt`, `changelog.txt`: Unreleased entries and the feature section

## Verification

Docker test site (Apache, WordPress 7.1.4, PHP 8.3), `scripts/test-site.sh`:

- Single site: `GET http://<other>/sample-page/?a=1&b=two` answered 301 to the main host with the same path and query, without `X-Redirect-By` (before PHP). `/.well-known/acme-challenge/abc` and `?seoprostack-host-check=x2` reach WordPress (`X-Redirect-By: WordPress`). POST is not redirected (200).
- Home address changed to another host: the rule dropped at once, `soon` event scheduled, block restored after the check. Home changed to the bare host (WordPress then 301s www to bare): `loop_guard` removed the stale rule and the block served www to bare.
- Setting switched off: block, state, daily and `soon` events cleared. Deactivation removes the block, state and schedule; reactivation plus cron rewrites it.
- Multisite (subdirectory network moved to `www.<net>`, sites at a bare host, a `www.` host and a bare+`www.` pair): only `www.<bare-site>` got a rule (WordPress's `get_site_by_path()` drops `www.`, then 301s); the unknown bare network host's 302 was not copied; a `www.` host that is its own site is untouched. Network deactivation removed block, state and events; network reactivation plus cron restored the block. PHP log empty.
- `bash scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan` passed; `scripts/preflight-release.sh`: 0 errors (readme.txt size warning clears at release, when the 1.3.177 section is replaced).

Not yet run: LiteSpeed (Hostinger) and Nginx; checked after release on the deploy.

Resolves #1383

title: GH#1383: fix: note the server when WP-Cron runs only from the command line
body:
## What

Redirect to the main address (#1384, not yet released) wrote nothing on sites whose WP-Cron runs only from the command line. With `DISABLE_WP_CRON` and a server cron job running PHP (every Hostinger site in the fleet, checked with `wp config get DISABLE_WP_CRON`), no web request ran WP-Cron, so the server and root folder were noted only when someone opened the main site's admin screens. On sites nobody signs in to, the block stayed `waiting`.

## How

- `ask_server()`: when a check runs from the command line with nothing noted, it sends one GET to the main site's `admin-ajax.php?action=seoprostack_host_note`. Nothing handles that action, so `admin-ajax.php` answers 400 and does nothing else. It is still an admin request, so `boot()` notes the server from it through the existing `remember()`. The check then drops its cached copies of `seoprostack_host_redirect_server` (options or site-options caches) and reads the note again.
- `get_here()`: the request to this server (resolver to the server's own address, #1242; no redirects followed; core's `https_local_ssl_verify`), now shared by `verify()` and `ask_server()`.
- No new endpoint, and no input is read from the request: the note comes from the server's own `$is_apache` and `get_home_path()`, as before.

## Files

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-host-redirect.php`: `NOTE_ACTION`, `ask_server()`, `get_here()`; `check()` calls `ask_server()`.
- `README.md`: feature section bullet on how the server is noted; Unreleased line.
- `changelog.txt`: Unreleased entry. `readme.txt` unchanged (its one line for the feature still holds).

## Verification

Docker test site (Apache, WordPress 7.1.4, PHP 8.3), `DISABLE_WP_CRON` true, home `http://www.sps-redirect.test`, neither option present:

- `wp cron event run seoprostack_host_redirect_check` (WP-CLI only): note saved as `{"reads":"yes","root":"/var/www/html/"}`, status `written`, rule `sps-redirect.test` to `http://www.sps-redirect.test`.
- `GET http://sps-redirect.test/sample-page/?a=1`: 301 to `http://www.sps-redirect.test/sample-page/?a=1` with no `X-Redirect-By` (before PHP).

title: GH#1396: restart WebP and AVIF conversion when pictures wait with no batch
body:
## What

**WebP and AVIF images** now starts its background conversion again when pictures wait and no batch is scheduled. Once a day, on a WP-Cron, WP-CLI or admin request (after `wp_loaded`, so image editors are registered), `SEOProStack_Nextgen_Images::maybe_restart()`:

1. reads an autoloaded option (`seoprostack_nextgen_restart`) and returns if it was set within the last day;
2. sets it;
3. calls `schedule()` when `wp_next_scheduled(self::HOOK)` is false and `waiting(1)` finds a picture.

The hook is added only after the `enabled()` return, so a disabled feature does nothing. Deactivation and `uninstall.php` remove the option. `run_batch()` is unchanged. Failed pictures are marked done before conversion (`convert_claimed()`), so a broken file cannot make the daily restart loop.

## Why

Batches started only on a settings save, an upload or edit, the bulk action, a rules sync or opening the settings panel. A change to `signature()` (the server learning AVIF, or a new default reaching the site) marked every picture as waiting but scheduled nothing. On one 11-site network, ten sites had 326 pictures waiting with no batch, so browsers got WebP instead of AVIF (82 KB vs 57 KB for one slider picture).

## Verification

- `bash scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`: all passed.
- Test site (`scripts/test-site.sh`, WordPress 7.1.4, PHP 8.3):
  - Picture uploaded, feature switched on through `SEOProStack_Settings::set()` (no batch scheduled: the stalled state). The next WP-CLI request set the mark and scheduled `seoprostack_nextgen_batch`; the batch made `avif:70s,webp:90s`, and the hook cleared.
  - `_seoprostack_nextgen_done` set to `webp:90` and the hook cleared (a format change). Same day: no batch (the gate held). Mark aged past a day: the next request scheduled the batch, which made the AVIF copy again; `waiting` 0, hook cleared.
- Live, before the fix: ten stalled network sites started converting when `schedule()` was called by hand.

Resolves #1396

title: GH#1399: Keep pages cached refills the site after LiteSpeed's Pages purge rule empties it
body:
Resolves #1399

## What

On a LiteSpeed site, Keep pages cached now fills the whole site after a post save that LiteSpeed Cache's purge rule **Pages** (on by default) or **All pages** uses to empty every page. Before, only the saved post, the home page and the posts page were opened again.

## How

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-keep-pages-cached.php`: new `litespeed_post_purged()` on LiteSpeed's `litespeed_purged_post` action. LiteSpeed fires it from `\LiteSpeed\Purge::_purge_post()` after adding the purge tags. The handler returns early unless the page cache is LiteSpeed, `purge-post_p` or `purge-post_all` is on, the post type is built-in or viewable (or LiteSpeed's `litespeed_purge_post_skip_non_viewable` filter says not to skip, as `_get_purge_tags_by_post()` decides), and `WP_IMPORTING` is not set. Then it calls `SEOProStack_Keep_Cached_Queue::fill_later(false)`, as `litespeed_purged()` does after Purge All for a single site. Saves one after another move the fill back for up to 10 minutes, through the queue's existing coalescing. `post_changed()` is unchanged, so the post itself is still reopened first.
- Docs: class docblock, README.md → Keep pages cached, changelog.txt, readme.txt (Unreleased).

## Evidence

One Kadence site on Hostinger (1.3.180, LiteSpeed Cache with its default purge rules), 7 November 2026. An automatic page update at 20:14 UTC left 18 of the first 20 Pages as `x-litespeed-cache: miss` for phones at 20:28 (0.64–1.24 s). The only `post` in the list was a hit, which matches the `PGS` tag being on Pages only. LiteSpeed Cache's source on that host: `purge.cls.php` L1468–1470 (`O_PURGE_POST_PAGES` → `Tag::TYPE_PAGES`); `tag.cls.php` L281–284 (`is_page()` → `PGS`); `_purge_post()` → `do_action('litespeed_purged_post', $pid)` L1122.

- After release, live on a wpallstars network test site: update a page with `wp_update_post()`, check the queue is marked `full` with a batch scheduled, then check other Pages answer `hit` as a phone once the batch has run.

title: GH#1402: Image loading: the hero row after a short text-only Kadence row gets the opening row's preload
body:
## Summary

Image loading treats the Kadence Blocks row after a short row of text alone (a heading band) as the row a post or page opens with. Its background picture then gets the head preload at high priority, the size the screen needs (`SEOProStack_Kadence_Hero`, `SEOProStack_Kadence_Early`), and counts as the first picture that loads straight away; `SEOProStack_Kadence_Rows` leaves it alone.

## Why

On one Kadence home page (PageSpeed mobile 84, LCP 4.6 s simulated, 1.3.180) a heading band comes first, so `kadence_preload()` (which read only `$blocks[0]`) did nothing for the hero row below it, the page's LCP. Phones fetched the 2560 px upload (182 KB AVIF) once the parser reached it, and two listing photos far below loaded with it. Local Lighthouse with those listing photos blocked: score 74–80 → 83–85, LCP 5.4–5.7 s → 4.3–4.4 s.

## Changes

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-image-loading.php`: new `opening_block()` (memoised per post), `band()`, `band_text()`; `kadence_preload()` uses `opening_block()`.
- `includes/class-seoprostack-kadence-rows.php`: `first_row()` uses `opening_block()` (still no parse unless the content opens with `kadence/rowlayout`).
- `README.md`, `readme.txt`, `changelog.txt`: Unreleased entries; README Image loading paragraph.

A band: `kadence/rowlayout`, normal, gradient or slider tab, no minimum height, no media file, picture attribute or `kadenceDynamic` in its JSON, only columns, headings, paragraphs, lists and buttons, at most 300 characters of text.

## Verification

- `bash scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`: all passed.
- Test site (WordPress 7.1.4, PHP 8.3, Kadence 1.6.0, Kadence Blocks 3.9.0), six pages, Playwright:

title: GH#1406: Image loading makes the missing 1536 and 2048 copies of Kadence row and slide pictures
body:
## Summary

Image loading's sizing scripts take the smallest copy of a Kadence row, column or slide picture that is at least as wide as the pixels it paints, else the picture itself. Many uploads lack WordPress's 1536 and 2048 copies (made before WordPress 5.3, or while a plugin removed them), so a box needing 1,025–2,000 px got the full upload. On one Kadence home page (1.3.182) phones needed 1,460 px and fetched the 2,560 px hero upload.

Now, when `SEOProStack_Hero_Picture::get()` reads a picture for a page that lacks any of WordPress's uncropped sizes (medium, medium_large, large, 1536x1536, 2048x2048) it is larger than, the picture is queued and WordPress's own `wp_update_image_subsizes()` makes only those sizes in a background cron batch (3 pictures a run, 20 s budget, each tried at most weekly). Only the page it was seen on is purged (LiteSpeed post tag, not its Purge Rules) and re-opened through Keep pages cached. WebP and AVIF images makes the new files' copies as for any upload.

Never less sharp: more copies only let the browser take a smaller file that is still enough.

## Files

- `includes/class-seoprostack-picture-sizes.php` (new): `want()`, `missing()`, `run()`, `make()`, filters `only_these()` and `source()` (original gone → attached file), `refresh()`.
- `includes/class-seoprostack-hero-picture.php`: `get()` calls `want()`.
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-image-loading.php`: boots the batch hook.
- `includes/class-seoprostack-page-cache.php`: `purge_posts($ids, $only = false)`; `$only` purges LiteSpeed's `Po.<id>` tag only.
- `uninstall.php`: unschedules the hook, deletes the option and `_seoprostack_sizes_tried` meta.
- `README.md`, `readme.txt`, `changelog.txt`: Unreleased entries.

Skipped: watermarked pictures (files marked in place), non-images, sizes a site removed, admin requests.

## Verification

Test site (WordPress 7.1.4, PHP 8.3, Kadence 1.6.0, Kadence Blocks 3.9.0), 2560×1920 upload with 1536/2048 removed from metadata and disk; two pages from the #1402 fixtures (hero first; heading band then background-slider hero). Chromium, 412×823 DPR 1.75 and 1350×940:

- Before the batch: both pages fetched `hero.jpg` (2560) on both screens.
- One visit queued the picture with its page; `wp cron event run --due-now` ran `seoprostack_picture_sizes`, made `hero-1536x1152.jpg` and `hero-2048x1536.jpg`, emptied the queue option.
- After: hero data offers 300, 768, 1024, 1536, 2048, 2560; both pages fetch only `hero-1536x1152.jpg` (need 1,283–1,485 px). Head keeps only the no-JS preload; no double fetch.
- A registered cropped 900×900 size was not made; with `original_image` naming a missing file, sizes were made from the attached file.
- `bash scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`: all passed.

Resolves #1406

title: GH#1409: Image loading's new picture sizes get their WebP and AVIF copies in the same run
body:
## Summary

Image loading's new picture sizes (#1406, 1.3.183) waited for WebP and AVIF images' next batch. On a host whose cron runs every few minutes, that batch came minutes after the page was purged and reopened. Meanwhile, on one Kadence site, the home page hero's new 1536 copy went out as a 278,691-byte JPEG, where the 2560 upload it replaced was a 185,835-byte AVIF. With **Copies at their own addresses**, a page rendered in that gap could stay cached without the copies' `image-set()`.

Now `SEOProStack_Picture_Sizes::make()` calls new `SEOProStack_Nextgen_Images::convert_now()` once the sizes are added, before `run()` purges and reopens the page. `convert_now()` takes the picture's claim and calls `convert_claimed()`, as each picture of a batch does. It does nothing when the feature is off or another batch holds the claim.

## Files

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-nextgen-images.php`: `convert_now($attachment_id)`.
- `includes/class-seoprostack-picture-sizes.php`: `make()` calls it; header comment.
- `README.md`, `readme.txt`, `changelog.txt`: Unreleased entries; README feature line updated.

title: GH#1414: Bookly's booking form files load at the end of the page
body:
## Summary

With **Load plugins only where needed** on, Bookly's booking form stylesheets and scripts print at the end of the page instead of in the head.

- New `includes/class-seoprostack-bookly-assets.php` (`SEOProStack_Bookly_Assets`), booted from `SEOProStack_Plugin_Loading::boot()` on the site's pages.
- On `wp_enqueue_scripts` at `PHP_INT_MAX` (after Bookly's own callbacks), handles starting `bookly-` or served from a `plugins/bookly*` folder (add-ons included) get script group 1. Their queued styles are dequeued and enqueued again on `wp_footer` priority 1, so `print_late_styles()` prints them just before the footer scripts.
- Only where every Bookly shortcode in the queried posts is `[bookly-form]` and the content has no `<!-- wp:bookly/` block. Bookly's other shortcodes (appointment lists, customer cabinet) render markup on the server and keep their head placement.

On one Kadence site's home page (Bookly 28.7), the only Bookly shortcode was a booking form inside a Kadence modal, yet about twenty Bookly files were render-blocking in the head (`bookly.min.js` 67 KB, `tailwind.css`, `intlTelInput`, and others). PageSpeed mobile scored 88, with first paint at 3.1 s. The form markup is an empty container that `bookly.min.js` fills once `document.readyState` is `complete` (Bookly `frontend/modules/booking/templates/short_code.php`), so nothing needs these files before the first paint.

title: GH#1417: Bookly's stylesheets stay at the end of the page with Kadence
body:
## Summary

With a classic theme such as Kadence, 1.3.185's move of Bookly's booking form stylesheets to the footer (#1414) was undone by WordPress core: from 6.9, `wp_hoist_late_printed_styles()` captures styles enqueued late and inserts them before `</head>`. On one live Kadence site, Bookly's scripts were in the footer, but its 7 stylesheets printed last in the head and still held up the first paint.

`SEOProStack_Bookly_Assets` now prints the styles itself with `wp_styles()->do_items()` right after `wp_print_footer_scripts` (priority + 1), and takes any Bookly styles off the queue just before it (priority − 1) in case Bookly enqueues them again while the form renders. Core's capture never sees them. The page's load event waits for those stylesheets and Bookly's start-up script waits for `readyState` "complete", so the form is still styled when Bookly fills it.

## Files

- `includes/class-seoprostack-bookly-assets.php`: `move()` calls the new `hold()` and hooks `hold()` and `styles()` around `wp_print_footer_scripts`; `styles()` prints with `do_items()` instead of enqueueing again.
- `changelog.txt`, `readme.txt`, `README.md`: Unreleased entries.

## Verification

- Reproduced on the #1414 test site (WordPress 7.1.4, PHP 8.3, Bookly 28.7) with the Kadence theme active: on 1.3.185, head Bookly tags 7 (the same 7 as live).
- Same site with this branch (`scripts/test-site.sh reinstall --ref bugfix/gh-bookly-hoist`): head Bookly tags 0; body has the 12 scripts, then the 7 stylesheets; `window.bookly` is a function; the form rendered its steps (screenshot: step dots, labelled selects and the Next button styled); no console errors.
- `bash scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`: all passed.

Resolves #1417

title: GH#1422: Image loading: a Kadence column's loader goes inside the column, not in the row's grid
body:
## Summary

SEOProStack_Kadence_Rows::around_column() printed the one-time loader script in front of the column when a column's background was the page's first to wait, so the script sat in .kt-row-column-wrap and Kadence's :nth-child(N of *:not(style)) column rules counted it: each column took the next one's margins, mobile order and grid spans. The loader now goes first inside the column (after the column's own opening tag, found with a regex anchored on <div and the column's class so inline CSS naming the class is not mistaken for it); the column's call stays last inside it. Rows unchanged. Header comment, docblock and changelog updated.



## Files Changed

changelog.txt, includes/class-seoprostack-kadence-rows.php

## Decisions

Option A from the review (loader inside the column) rather than wp_head, which would put the script on every page. Anchoring on the column's opening tag rather than the first kt-inside-inner-col string avoids matching Kadence inline CSS. If the opening tag is not found the column is left as Kadence printed it (no waiting), never with the loader in the grid.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium
- **Verification:** self-assessed — bash scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan: all passed. Throwaway PHP harness calling around_column() with WordPress stubbed: first waiting column -> style before the column, loader as the column's first child before .kt-inside-inner-col, call as its last child; second column -> no loader; inline style naming the column class before the column -> call still placed inside the column; prefix uniqueID (15 vs 15_x) -> left unchanged. Client script: box() walks nextElementSibling to .kt-inside-inner-col and the call finds its column through s.parentNode, so neither depends on the inner column being first.

Resolves #1422

body:
## Summary

New Speed feature SEOProStack_Maps_Later (maps_later, on by default). Google Maps embed iframes in block output are printed without src (kept in data-seoprostack-src, with a noscript copy); an inline footer script sets src within 600 px of the screen (IntersectionObserver), on beforeprint, or at once without IntersectionObserver. Maps in the main post's opening top-level block, loading=eager, Image loading's exclusion list (always, whether or not Image loading is on), skip-lazy/no-lazy, REST/AJAX/feeds, and pages whose PHP-sent CSP blocks inline scripts are left alone. Filter seoprostack_maps_later. Registered in Setup and the Speed plan; README and changelog updated.

Second commit: Codacy flagged class complexity 59 (limit 50) and page_view() at 11 (limit 10). Removed redundant branches (admin check already in boot(), `wp_is_json_request()` always exists from WP 6.2, already-held check covered by the missing src and data-no-lazy, `get_the_ID()` instead of `get_post()` plus instanceof). No global first-interaction trigger: IntersectionObserver already fires when a hidden tab/modal map is shown, and loading every map on the first mousemove would bring the cost back on desktop. title: GH#1434: Used CSS handles WP Grid Builder's grid stylesheet and its Google Fonts
body:
Resolves #1434

## What

**Load the CSS each page uses first** (Used CSS) now handles WP Grid Builder's two stylesheets that still held up the first paint:

- `wpgb-grids` (its grid and card stylesheet in `uploads/wpgb/grids/`): `SEOProStack_Used_Css_Links::sources()` adds `wpgb/` in the site's uploads folder.
- `wpgb-fonts` (its cards' and facets' Google Fonts): new `SEOProStack_Used_Css::wpgb_fonts()`, on WP Grid Builder's own `wp_grid_builder/frontend/register_styles` filter (priority 20, after its entries), points a `fonts.googleapis.com/css` or `css2` source at the local copy made by the Kadence theme's loader (`Kadence\get_webfont_url()`) or Kadence Blocks' (`KadenceWP\KadenceBlocks\get_webfont_url()`): the stylesheet and font files in `wp-content/fonts/`, as the theme does for its own Google Fonts. `kadence_fonts()` accepts that file with id `wpgb-fonts-css`. Google's address stays without a Kadence loader or when the copy fails (the loader returns the remote address; `local_fonts()` then returns empty). Bunny Fonts addresses are left alone.

title: GH#1441: integrity checks treat no-open-tag and __halt_compiler uploads .php files as harmless
body:
## What

The daily integrity check (Uploaded PHP) no longer reports two kinds of plugin data file that cannot run code. Resolves #1441.

- **No `<?` anywhere**: PHP prints the file as text (WP Mailster's `uploads/wp-mailster/wpmst.log.php`).
- **First statement `__halt_compiler();`**: PHP parses nothing after it (All In One Security's `uploads/aios/firewall-rules/settings.php`).

## How

`includes/class-seoprostack-integrity-folders.php`:

- New `halts($head)`: tokens at the file's start must be quiet (open tag, comments, whitespace, as `quiet()` allows), then `__halt_compiler`, `(`, `)`, then `;` or a close tag, with only whitespace or comments between them. What follows is never parsed, so no `open_tag_after()` check is needed.
- `harmless()`: after the small-file checks, returns true when `halts()` holds, or when the first 2 KB has no `<?` and `open_tag_after($file, 0)` finds none in the rest (read in parts, up to `MAX_GUARDED_FILE`; unreadable or too long counts as found).
- Unchanged: files that include code when loaded (`uploads/wph/environment.php` behind an ABSPATH check, `smile_fonts` charmap arrays) are still reported; `seoprostack_integrity_ignore` covers them.

README → File and account integrity checks, item 4, lists both cases. Changelog: Unreleased.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`: passed.
- `harmless()` called directly (PHP 8.5 CLI) on 14 files; all gave the expected result:
  - Harmless: the issue's t1 (plain text), t2 (`<?php __halt_compiler(); {"a":1}`) and t3 (`<?php __halt_compiler() ?><?php echo 1;`); the AIOS shape with a doc comment; an upper-case halt with comments inside the brackets; 18 KB of text with no tag; the existing exit-guarded log; the existing silence-is-golden `index.php`.

title: GH#1445: fix: media storage keeps a finished claim index across updates
body:
## What

Media in cloud storage now keeps a finished claim index across plugin updates. Before, every update restarted the build from the top. Until it finished, each upload's `wp_unique_filename()` walked every stored inventory, about a minute per picture on a multisite with about 104,000 attachment IDs.

`includes/features/class-seoprostack-media-storage.php`:

- New `claims_built($state)`: true once a build by any version has finished (`built` is not empty).
- `claims_table(true)` and `claims_due()` use it instead of `SEOPROSTACK_VERSION === built`.
- `build_claims()` returns once built. It starts a new build only when none is running (`building` empty or no cursor). A build that another version started continues from its cursor, so the PSD stack's 1.3.189 build at cursor 76,421 finishes instead of starting again.
- On finish, `built` is still set to `SEOPROSTACK_VERSION`. So 1.3.90–1.3.189, which compare it with their own version, still rebuild after a downgrade, and the next update rebuilds again.
- `CLAIMS_SCHEMA` gets a note: bump it when the hashes, the table or the indexed files change.

Why this is safe: every version since 1.3.90 indexes each inventory it saves. `index_claims()` needs only the schema, not a finished build, so a finished index stays complete through an update. One case is not detected: running a version older than 1.3.90 in between. The updater refuses downgrades without `--allow-downgrade`.

Not changed: the URL index and kept-original table stay keyed to the version. After an update, their step only moves options an older version wrote (a prefix range of `wp_options`, usually empty in one batch), and their lookups read one option each meanwhile. So they are not the slow path the issue measured.

Not done: issue option 3 (a WP-CLI action to finish builds in one run). It is not needed once updates keep the index.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`: passed.
- Disposable site (WordPress 7.1.4, PHP 8.3), with `build_claims()`, `claims_table()` and `unique_filename_files()` called through WP-CLI on attachments with real inventory meta:
  - Fresh build: 5 of 5 attachments indexed; complete.
  - State `built: 1.3.189`: complete, no new build.
  - A 1.3.189 build in progress with the cursor at the 3rd ID: continued and indexed only the 2 IDs below it, then finished.
  - `built` cleared, as an older version does after a downgrade: rebuilt from the top (5 rows).
  - Failed state (`retry` only): lookups not trusted.
  - Lookup with an index built by 1.3.189, while local copies are being removed: one `wp_seoprostack_media_claims` query plus one meta read. `pic1.jpg` and `pic1-scaled.jpg` are still reserved. During a build it walks `wp_postmeta` as before.
- Debug log empty.

Resolves #1445

title: GH#1447: fix: leave out WooCommerce Coming soon fonts the page already loads
body:
## What

In WooCommerce's **Coming soon** mode (even "store pages only"), WooCommerce adds its coming-soon page's fonts, Inter (weights 300–900, a 327 KB variable font) and Cardo, to the theme's theme.json fonts on every request, so WordPress prints them in `<style class="wp-fonts-local">` on every page. Where the theme also loads Inter (Kadence), the browser takes WooCommerce's face and downloads the 327 KB file before the first paint.

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-woo-light.php`: only while `woocommerce_coming_soon` is `yes`, a page buffer (`template_redirect` `PHP_INT_MAX`) removes each `@font-face` rule in `wp-fonts-local` whose file is in WooCommerce's `assets/fonts/` folder **for a family the page also declares without WooCommerce's rules**. A family only WooCommerce gives keeps its rule. The coming-soon screen is skipped: its `wp-block-woocommerce-coming-soon` block, or the `woo-coming-soon-page` meta (classic themes do not print the meta, as WooCommerce adds it after `get_header()`; found by session l3ykgz, whose parallel branch `bugfix/woo-coming-soon-fonts` this replaces).
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-font-fallbacks.php`: the family detection is now public `declared_families($html)` (`@font-face` rules, Google Fonts links, on-site font stylesheets) and the request check public `html_view()`; Font fallbacks behaves as before.
- `README.md` (Lighter WooCommerce pages) and `changelog.txt`.

Not changed: WooCommerce's settings, the admin, the block editor.

## Verification

title: GH#1450: fix: LiteSpeed purge delivery only where LiteSpeed Cache runs
body:
## What

On a network where LiteSpeed Cache is active on some sites only, `SEOProStack_Litespeed::deliver_purge()` ran at the end of every WP-CLI and host-cron run on the other sites too. Such a site can hold a purge in `litespeed.purge.queue` (stored for it from another site), but nothing there takes it: its `admin-ajax.php` answered 400 and the queue stayed, so every run opened it again (`lscache_runner SEOProStack`, through Cloudflare).

- `includes/class-seoprostack-litespeed.php`: new private `running()`: `LSCWP_V` defined and no `switch_to_blog()` in effect, else LiteSpeed Cache active on the current site (`SEOProStack_Feature::stored_active_plugins()`, which still lists a plugin Load plugins only where needed skips on this request) or for the network (`network_active()`). After review: a switched-to site is read for itself, and a CLI request that skips LiteSpeed Cache still delivers. `deliver_purge()` returns `true` (nothing this run can deliver) and the `delivery_args()` filter leaves requests alone unless it is true. `delivery_answered()` needs no change: it acts only on requests `delivery_args()` marked.
- `changelog.txt`: Unreleased entry.

A queue already left on such a site stays until LiteSpeed Cache runs there (setting it to `-1` clears it, as the reporter did on the PSD networks).

Resolves #1450

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`: passed.
- Test site (WordPress 7.1.4, PHP 8.3, multisite, LiteSpeed Cache 7.9.3 active on the main site only), WP-CLI check that marks the server as LiteSpeed, stores a purge in the site's queue, calls `deliver_purge()` and logs every request through `http_api_debug` (`--url` each site):
  - before (main): the subsite opened `/sub/wp-admin/admin-ajax.php` as `lscache_runner SEOProStack` twice (once directly, once at shutdown), `deliver_purge=false`;
  - after: the subsite made no request, `deliver_purge=true`; the main site still opened its `admin-ajax.php` as before (LiteSpeed Cache's own request, then ours).
  - after review (d234c543), with each site's queue and server option set before each call: from the subsite, `switch_to_blog(1)` then `deliver_purge()` opens the main site's `admin-ajax.php`; `switch_to_blog(2)` makes no request; from the main site, switching to sites 2 and 3 makes no request.
  - debug.log empty.

title: GH#1472: fix: no could_not_set log line when a purge moves the batch during a cron run
body:
## What

In cron runs and WP-CLI, removing a scheduled task that the stored list no longer has now counts as done. `wp-cron.php` therefore stops logging "Cron unschedule event error ... could_not_set" when another request has moved or removed a due task during the run. The main case is Keep pages cached: a cache purge moves its next batch later.

- `includes/class-seoprostack-cron-list.php`: new `SEOProStack_Cron_List::unschedule()` on `pre_unschedule_event` at `PHP_INT_MAX`, registered beside `dedupe()` for cron runs and WP-CLI only.
  - If the task (time, hook, hash of its arguments) is missing from the stored list (`stored()`, read past the caches), it returns `true`.
  - If the run's own copy still has the task, it also drops the option caches (new private `forget()`, now shared with `write()`'s #1270 path), so the rest of the run reads the stored list.
  - It checks the stored list rather than the run's copy because each write in the run refreshes that copy. Moving a recurring task first, or writing an earlier task, can already have removed it from the copy.
  - A task still stored, a list that cannot be read, or another filter's result is left to core. Removals on other requests are not changed.
- `changelog.txt` (Unreleased): entries for this fix and for #1455 (PR #1457, merged without one).
- `README.md`: one sentence added to the scheduled tasks list entry under Fixes for other plugins.

## Why

The line comes from WordPress core. `wp-cron.php` reads the due tasks once, at its start. A purge in another request moves the batch (`SEOProStack_Keep_Cached_Queue::save()`). When the run then removes the copy it read, nothing stored changes, `update_option()` reports a failure, and core logs it in the site's language.

`run()` already left the moved batch to its new time (#1362), so no page went unopened. The line was noise, but it hides real errors and the deploy check counts it. Counts on the owner's Hostinger sites: 67 English lines (about 70 with translated ones) on 9 November, after Keep pages cached was turned on for sites that purge many times an hour, against 1 on 8 November.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh`: all passed (php, js, shell, workflows, phpcs, phpstan).
- Test site (`scripts/test-site.sh`, WordPress 7.1.4, PHP 8.3), WP-CLI `eval-file`. The other request's write is made the way `_set_cron_array()` makes it:
  - Single event moved by another request: before `WP_Error could_not_set`, after `true`. The moved copy is kept (1 stored).
  - Single event removed by another request, after an earlier write refreshed the run's copy: before `could_not_set`, after `true`, 0 stored.
  - Recurring event already moved: unschedule before `could_not_set`, after `true`. Reschedule still reports `could_not_set`, as before, which is out of scope.
  - Normal removal (task stored): `true`, removed. Another filter returning `false`: `WP_Error pre_unschedule_event_false`, kept.
- End to end through HTTP `wp-cron.php`, with a test mu-plugin whose first due task moves the second, as a purge does:
  - With the filter removed, `debug.log` shows `Cron unschedule event error for hook: sps_gh1472_second, Error code: could_not_set, ...`, the production line.
  - With the filter on, there is no such line, and the moved task stays at its new time.
- After deploy: watch the sites' `error_log` for new `seoprostack_keep_pages_cached` `could_not_set` lines.

Resolves #1472

title: GH#1476: Image loading: Kadence background copies by the device pixels they paint, without the 10% margin
body:
## What

Image loading's four scripts that choose a copy of a Kadence Blocks background picture (row a page opens with #1221, Advanced Slider slides #1333, the head's preload #1337, rows and columns further down #1341) now take the narrowest copy at least as wide as the device pixels it paints, rounded to the nearest whole pixel, as browsers choose from `srcset`. Before, they multiplied by 1.1 ("10% to spare for fonts and late styles"), which took the next size up whenever a picture painted within 10% under a copy's width.

- PageSpeed's phone (412 px, DPR 1.75): a full-width picture paints 721 device pixels; with the margin 793, so WordPress's 1024 copy instead of the 768.
- 768 px tablet at DPR 2 (1,536) and 1440 px desktop at DPR 1 (1,440): the full upload instead of the 1536 copy.

`Math.round` stops a layout fraction (such as 1,536.0002) from tipping a box that a copy exactly fits up to the next size. All four scripts use the same rule, so the head's copy is still the one the script after the block keeps (fetched once).

**Never less sharp (owner's rule):** every file is still at least as wide as the device pixels it paints. The margin was for boxes that grow later; the existing ResizeObserver and `matchMedia` resolution watch already swap in a larger copy when a box grows or the pixel ratio rises, never a smaller one.

## Evidence

Test site (WordPress 7.1.4, PHP 8.3, Kadence 1.6.0, Kadence Blocks 3.9.0; 2048×1536 pictures with 300/768/1024/1536 copies: 193 KB / 345 KB / full 578 KB), Chromium at five screens, same pages on `origin/main` and this branch:

| Screen | main (× 1.1) | this branch | device px painted |
|---|---|---|---|
| 412×823 @1.75 (3 hero pages) | 1536 | 1024 | 933–963 |
| 768×1024 @2 (3 heroes + column) | full | 1536 | 1,440–1,536 |
| 1440×900 @1 (3 heroes) | full | 1536 | 1,440 |
| 393×852 @3, 1920×1080 @1 | same | same | — |

Every file shown was at least as wide as the pixels painted; each picture fetched once; the 400 px row showed the copy the head preloaded (`seoprostackEarly.i` matched); widening the phone to 1600 still swapped in the full picture; no console errors; `debug.log` empty.

Live Kadence home pages (1.3.192) through a local proxy that removed only the margin: three of seven changed files (phone 1536→1024, 80→19 KB AVIF; 1024→768, 104→77 KB; tablets and 1440/1920 desktops a size smaller), none larger. Local Lighthouse mobile, alternating runs: LCP median 4,023 → 3,710 ms (5 pairs) on one; 3,207–4,385 → 3,543–3,556 ms (3 pairs) on another; other pages unchanged within noise.

title: GH#1471: Keep pages cached shares fill slots per hosting account
body:
## What

Keep pages cached no longer refills every site of a hosting account at once. Three changes, as proposed in the issue:

1. **Account-wide fill slots.** Before a batch opens pages it takes one of two slots (filter `seoprostack_keep_cached_slots`; below 1, no limit): a non-blocking `flock()` on `seoprostack-fill-<uid>-<n>.lock` in `sys_get_temp_dir()`, shared by every install that runs as the same system user. With no slot free the batch opens nothing and is rescheduled `GAP` (60 s) later, without counting as a stop. The slot is released in a `finally` block, and by the system if PHP stops. Only a slot another batch holds counts as taken (`flock()`'s would-block flag, after CodeRabbit's review): where no lock file can be opened or locked, or the temporary folder is outside `open_basedir` (checked first, so no warning is logged), batches run as before. `wp seoprostack keep-cached`, run by hand, takes no slot.
2. **Main pages only where search engines are off.** With `blog_public` = 0 a site plans only its main pages (home, header, footer and home page links, up to `MAIN_MAX`), not up to `MAX` (1,000). Filter `seoprostack_keep_cached_max` (0 = main pages only). A network's second round adds no newer pages for such a site.
3. **Slow pages end the batch.** A page that took more than 8 s per request to build (filter `seoprostack_keep_cached_slow`) ends its batch after it, so the next waits `GAP`.

## Files

- `includes/class-seoprostack-keep-cached-queue.php`: `SLOTS`, `take_slot()`, `may_use()`, `release_slot()`, `no_slot()`. Lock pattern as `SEOProStack_Vulnerability_Feed_Download::fetch()`.
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-keep-pages-cached.php`: `run()` takes and releases the slot; the batch moved to `batch()`; `SLOW`, `slow()`.
- `includes/class-seoprostack-keep-cached-pages.php`: `site_max()`, hidden-site rule in the network second round.
- `README.md`, `changelog.txt`.

## Verification

Test site (`scripts/test-site.sh`; WordPress 7.1.4, PHP 8.3, Apache). The slot checks ran as separate PHP processes of one system user in the web container, as two installs on one account are:

- Two processes holding both slots: a third `take_slot()` returned false. With the filter at 3 it got one; at 0, no limit.
- A holder that exited without `release_slot()` freed its slot: the next process took it.
- After the Codacy complexity fix (`open_slot()` split out of `take_slot()`), re-run on the rebuilt site: A took a slot and a second `take_slot()` in the same process kept it (B still got the other), C got none, and after both exited D got one.
- `no_slot()` kept the queue (2 URLs) and its stop count (2), and scheduled the next batch in 60 s; with an empty queue it scheduled nothing.
- WP-Optimize page cache on, one page sleeping 2 s, slow filter 1 s: the first `run()` opened 8 of 10 pages and ended right after the slow page (8th in order); the next `run()` opened the other 2 and the fill finished (`seoprostack_keep_pages_cached_last` opened 10). The slot was free afterwards.
- `to_open(false)`: 9 pages with search engines on; with `blog_public` 0, only the home page (no menus on that theme); with the max filter at 3, 3 pages.
- `debug.log` empty.
- Hosting account (read-only): PHP CLI `sys_get_temp_dir()` is `/tmp`, private to the account (mode 700, CageFS); `open_basedir` empty in `alt_php.ini`, no per-site override.
- `scripts/lint.sh`: all passed (php, js, shell, workflows, phpcs, phpstan, build).

No new tests added (repository policy: none unless required).

title: GH#1461: Clear Cloudflare’s copies of pages, only this site’s
body:
## Summary

New Speed feature Clear Cloudflare’s copies of pages (off by default): when LiteSpeed Cache or WP-Optimize empties pages, it purges Cloudflare by this site's host name (or folder prefix on a subdirectory network) or by the post's own addresses, never purge_everything. Purges are queued and sent from WP-Cron 15 s later, at most 4 requests a run a minute apart (Free plan: 5/min per zone), retrying 429/5xx up to 6 times, with the last 20 answers in the panel and wp seoprostack cloudflare-purge. Credentials: constants, then per-site token/zone (token field never rendered back), then LiteSpeed Cache's Cloudflare API key. Hosting needs: warns when LiteSpeed's Clear Cloudflare cache would empty a shared zone, when Cloudflare gives browsers a long max-age, when the cache rule skips any-cookie visitors (made-up cookie probe), and when LiteSpeed Cache Mobile is on; no purge advice when the origin's edge time is 10 min or less or the connector is ready. The LiteSpeed preset no longer turns Clear Cloudflare cache on for a site on a subdomain of its zone. Docs: README section with the Cloudflare cache rule, cookie list, Browser TTL and Tiered Cache; readme.txt external service and Unreleased entry; changelog.txt.



## Files Changed

README.md, admin/includes/class-settings-manager.php, changelog.txt, includes/class-seoprostack-litespeed.php, includes/class-seoprostack-setup.php, includes/features/class-seoprostack-cloudflare-purge.php, includes/features/class-seoprostack-hosting-needs.php, includes/features/class-seoprostack-keep-pages-cached.php, presets/litespeed-cache.json, readme.txt, uninstall.php

## Decisions

Purge by host name/prefix/URL instead of Cache-Tag: a host name is unique per site, needs no header kept in LiteSpeed's cached copies, and covers pages cached before the feature was switched on. Cloudflare's Free plan accepted a prefix purge on 10 Nov 2026, so subdirectory networks use prefixes. The token setting is per-site (network:false) and never rendered back; constants remain the preferred route on networks. Not included (as the issue says): creating the cache rule, cache key by device, APO. WP-Optimize single-page purges are covered by transition_post_status rather than a WP-Optimize hook.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Critical
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — bash scripts/lint.sh: php, js, shell, workflows, phpcs, phpstan all passed. Disposable multisite (WordPress 7.1.4, PHP 8.3, LiteSpeed Cache 7.9.3) with a real token and a Free-plan zone: host purge, URL purge and prefix purge (host/about/) all answered success; live pages then went MISS then HIT, other pages stayed HIT. 127.0.0.1 addresses were refused by Cloudflare (1140/1125) and logged as failed in the panel and CLI. No token: panel warns, ready() false, nothing queued. LiteSpeed global key gives X-Auth headers, token gives Authorization. LiteSpeed API + Clear on: litespeed_purged_all queues nothing. cloudflare_clears_zone() true for a shared zone, false without Clear. Preset condition false on a subdomain, true on the zone's own domain. Token field renders empty password input; a space clears the token. cdn_probe() against a live Free-plan zone found the any-cookie rule (cf_cookie true). No PHP warnings in the test site log.

title: GH#1485: Image loading: the logo leaves high fetch priority to the main picture; lazy pictures get sizes=auto
body:
## What

Two changes to Image loading (`includes/features/class-seoprostack-image-loading.php`), from PageSpeed Insights on the fleet's home pages at 1.3.194:

1. **The logo leaves high fetch priority to the main picture.** Core gives `fetchpriority="high"` to the first picture of at least 50,000 px² once the header has started, and a logo whose file is large (an SVG that says 1000×781, a PNG uploaded at 680×250) took it, though it shows about 50 px high. The main picture then had none, and Lighthouse's LCP request discovery failed on it. `core_priority()` now takes core's (not the theme's or author's) `fetchpriority` off an `img` with the `custom-logo` class outside `the_content` and gives core's flag back (`wp_high_priority_element_flag(true)`), so the first large picture after it gets it. The logo still loads straight away (`data-no-lazy="1"`, no `loading="lazy"`).
2. **Pictures made lazy here get `sizes="auto"`.** Core adds `auto` only in `wp_filter_content_tags()`, to tags that already have `loading="lazy"`, before `wp_content_img_tag`. `content_image()` adds `loading="lazy"` later (below the opening block, #1412; and past the budget when LiteSpeed Cache's lazy load turns core's off), so none of those got it, and grid pictures shown 251–382 px wide fetched their 768 px copies. `content_image()` now runs core's `wp_img_tag_add_auto_sizes()` on each picture it makes lazy, and also lazies pictures past the **Load straight away** budget that core left without `loading` (only happens when core's lazy loading is off).

**Never less sharp (owner's rule):** `sizes="auto"` makes the browser pick from `srcset` by the width the picture is shown at, so the copy is still at least as wide as the pixels it paints; browsers without it read the rest of `sizes` as before.

## Evidence

Test site (WordPress 7.1.4, PHP 8.3, Kadence 1.6.0): a 680×250 PNG logo, a page opening with a 1600×1200 Image block, four 1536×1152 Image blocks in columns 1,400 px below; with and without a must-use plugin returning false from `wp_lazy_loading_enabled` (as LiteSpeed Cache's lazy load does).

| | `origin/main` (1.3.194) | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| Logo (desktop) | `fetchpriority="high"` | none |
| Logo (mobile) | none | none |
| Opening picture | none | `fetchpriority="high"`, `data-no-lazy="1"` |
| 4 pictures below, core lazy off | `loading="lazy"`, `sizes="(max-width: 1024px) 100vw, 1024px"` | `loading="lazy"`, `sizes="auto, (max-width: 1024px) 100vw, 1024px"` |
| 4 pictures below, core lazy on | core's `auto` | same |

Live (before): logo with `fetchpriority="high"` on 5 of 13 Kadence home pages and on the regional directory home pages; LCP request discovery failed on 4 of those 5 (desktop) and on the directory pages. On one directory home page, 3 grid pictures whose `sizes` had `auto` fetched ~360 px copies; the 20 without fetched 768 px copies (21–110 KB each).

`scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`: all passed.

Resolves #1485

title: GH#1486: Speed: TranslatePress's head scripts load with defer
body:
## What

New Speed feature, on by default: **Load TranslatePress’s scripts without holding up the page** (`includes/features/class-seoprostack-translatepress-defer.php`).

TranslatePress 3.3.8 prints `trp-language-switcher-js-v2` (16 KB, every page) and, with WooCommerce, `trp-frontend-compatibility` (0.8 KB) in the head with no loading strategy. PageSpeed Insights lists both as render-blocking on every TranslatePress site in the fleet: 120–130 ms on desktop, an estimated 430 ms on mobile. Both only act on `DOMContentLoaded`, which deferred scripts run before, in order.

- At `wp_enqueue_scripts` `PHP_INT_MAX`, each registered handle with a `src` and no strategy gets WordPress's `defer` strategy. WordPress itself keeps a script blocking when a blocking script depends on it or an inline `after` script follows it, so nothing that needs them synchronously breaks.
- Not in the admin, TranslatePress's translation editor (`trp-edit-translation`), feeds, embeds or AMP. Filter `seoprostack_translatepress_defer`. Changing the setting empties the page cache (as Load jQuery at the end of the page does).
- Registered in `SEOProStack_Setup`; in the Recommended speed settings while TranslatePress is active; README.md (Features list, Recommended list, feature section, filters) and changelog.txt.
