title: GH#1490: Visitors' like counts as a GET LiteSpeed Cache keeps, purged per post
body:
## What

**Like, save and share** no longer starts WordPress a second time for each visitor's page view.

The buttons are printed without counts so pages stay cacheable; `assets/post-reactions.js` then asked `admin-ajax.php` for them with a POST (`do=state`), which no page cache keeps. On a directory site on LiteSpeed (LiteSpeed Cache 7.9.3) that took 0.77 to 1.0 s to first byte per view (three runs in a row), for public totals only (`{"counts":…,"user":false}`).

- **Script:** on a page served to a visitor (no `logged-in` body class, no nonce yet), `state` is a GET with the post IDs in numeric order and the page's language (`document.documentElement.lang`), so a page always asks for the same address. Logged-in people still POST.
- **Server:** `SEOProStack_Post_Reactions::ajax()` sends a GET to the new `state_get()`, which answers `state` only (anything else: 405). For a visitor it sends `Cache-Control: no-cache` (browsers always ask, so never show an older count than the server has) and, through LiteSpeed Cache's API, `litespeed_control_set_ttl` (`CACHE_TTL`, a day), `litespeed_control_force_cacheable` and `litespeed_tag_add` with `sps_reactions_<post ID>` per post, as LiteSpeed Cache's own AJAX Cache TTL setting does. A logged-in person's GET is answered as the POST is, never kept.
- **Purge:** with LiteSpeed Cache active (`LSCWP_V`), a change to a post's `_seoprostack_likes` or `_seoprostack_listed` meta (added, updated, deleted) sends `litespeed_purge` for that post's tag only (`totals_changed()`).
- Without LiteSpeed Cache nothing is kept; the GET runs as the POST did. The answer is built by the new `state_data()`, shared by both.
- README.md (Like, save and share) and changelog.txt.

## Evidence

Test site (WordPress 7.1.4, PHP 8.3, Kadence 1.6.0; three posts with the block, one at 4 likes), Chromium:

| | request | result |
|---|---|---|
| Visitor, page load | GET `do=state&posts=5&lang=en-US`, 200, `Cache-Control: no-cache` | shows 4 |
| Visitor, Like | POST `do=like`, as before | shows 5 |
| Logged in, page load | POST `do=state` (lists, nonce) | shows 5 |
| Logged in, Like | POST with nonce | shows 6 |
| Console errors | | none |

With a must-use stand-in for LiteSpeed Cache's API that echoed each call as a header:

- Visitor GET for posts 6,5,4: TTL 86400, forced cacheable, tags `sps_reactions_6`, `_5`, `_4`.
- Visitor like on post 4: purge `sps_reactions_4` only.
- GET with `do=like`: 405.

`scripts/lint.sh php js phpcs phpstan`: all passed.

Not yet shown: LiteSpeed itself serving the kept answer (`x-litespeed-cache: hit` on a second GET). The test sites have no LiteSpeed server; this is checked on a live LiteSpeed site after the release.

Resolves #1490

title: GH#1502: defer SEO Pro Stack's own front-end scripts; reaction counts at low priority
body:
Resolves #1502

## What

SEO Pro Stack's own front-end scripts now load with WordPress's `defer` strategy. Like, save and share asks for its counts (`state`) at low fetch priority.

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `includes/features/class-seoprostack-post-reactions.php` | `post-reactions.js` registered with `array('strategy' => 'defer', 'in_footer' => true)` |
| `includes/features/class-seoprostack-modal-links.php` | `modal-links.js` deferred |
| `includes/class-seoprostack-form-modal.php` | `form-keys.js` deferred; Kadence Blocks Pro's modal script unchanged (still runs first) |
| `includes/features/class-seoprostack-dark-image-contrast.php` | `dark-image-contrast.js` deferred |
| `includes/features/class-seoprostack-wikipedia-previews.php` | `wikipedia-previews.js` deferred |
| `includes/class-seoprostack-link-clicks.php` | `seoprostack-link-clicks.js` deferred |
| `assets/post-reactions.js` | `send()` passes `priority: 'low'` for `state` (visitor GET and logged-in POST); likes, saves, list changes and merge keep the default |
| `README.md`, `changelog.txt` | Documented under Modal links and Like, save and share; `= Unreleased =` entry |

`email-protection.js` is unchanged because it replaces visible text.

## Why

PageSpeed Insights (mobile, 1.3.195, a directory home page) listed SEO Pro Stack's four scripts on that page in the critical request chain, each at about 520 ms. The longest chain (2,630 ms) ended at the reactions' `state` GET. Footer scripts are fetched at medium priority, alongside the page's pictures.

## Safety

- Each script acts only on clicks, focus or pictures as they load, or after `DOMContentLoaded`. Deferred scripts run before that event, in order.
- Each script gets its settings from an inline script printed before it. WordPress drops the strategy only when an inline script follows a script.
- On WordPress before 6.3 the array is read as `in_footer`, as before. The same pattern is already used by the language switcher (`class-seoprostack-language-switcher.php`).
- Browsers that don't support fetch priority ignore the `priority` option.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh`: ok (php, js, shell, workflows, phpcs, phpstan).
- Test site (`scripts/test-site.sh up`, WordPress latest, PHP 8.3) with Like, save and share on posts, Wikipedia previews, Modal links and Dark image contrast on. A must-use plugin adds `color-switch-dark` and a dark background. The test post has a Wikipedia link, a `#sps-modal` link, a footer `<dialog id="sps-modal">` and a black transparent PNG. Results in Chromium, with priorities from the DevTools protocol:
  - The four scripts print with `defer` and `data-wp-strategy="defer"` and are fetched at Low priority.
  - The `state` GET is fetched at Low priority and the `like` POST at High.
  - The count showed 4 after load; Like made it 5 (`aria-pressed="true"`).
  - Hovering the Wikipedia link opened the preview ("Jersey").
  - The black PNG got `data-seoprostack-dark="invert"`.
  - The modal link got `aria-haspopup="dialog"`, and a click opened the dialog.
  - No console errors.
- Not exercised: `form-keys.js` (needs Kadence Blocks Pro) and `seoprostack-link-clicks.js` (link click counting, off for the rollout).

title: GH#1504: Image loading: archive and search thumbnails lazy-load when a cache plugin turned core's off
body:
## What

Image loading now lazy-loads archive and search thumbnails past the first pictures (**Load straight away**) when a cache plugin has turned WordPress's lazy loading off.

LiteSpeed Cache's **Lazy Load Images** turns WordPress's lazy loading off (`wp_lazy_loading_enabled` false). Its own lazy loader then runs only on pages it caches. So on search results, which it never caches, and on every page for people who are logged in, every featured image in the loop loaded with the page. On a directory stack's `/?s=guttering` that was 11 thumbnails 768 px wide.

`content_image()` already handled this for content pictures (#1485). `attachment_image()` now does the same for pictures from `wp_get_attachment_image()` in the main loop:

- It adds `loading="lazy"` to a picture past the budget that has no `loading` or `fetchpriority` and is not excluded.
- It acts only when `wp_lazy_loading_enabled('img', <core's wp_get_attachment_image_context>)` is false (new `core_lazy()`).
- It adds `auto, ` to `sizes`, as core's `wp_get_attachment_image()` does (WordPress 6.7+, respecting `wp_img_tag_add_auto_sizes`).

When WordPress's lazy loading is on, core decides, as before.

## Files

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-image-loading.php`: `attachment_image()`, new `core_lazy()`.
- `README.md`: Image loading, new bullet "Archive and search thumbnails wait too".
- `changelog.txt`: Unreleased entry.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh`: all passed (php, js, shell, workflows, phpcs, phpstan).
- Test site (WordPress 7.1.4, PHP 8.3, Kadence; eight posts with a 1600×1067 featured image), `/?s=guttering`:

| Case | Thumbnails |
|---|---|
| Core lazy on | 3 without `loading` (first `fetchpriority="high"`), 5 `loading="lazy"` + `sizes="auto, …"`: same before and after |
| Core lazy off (mu-plugin, as LiteSpeed), Image loading off | all 8 without `loading` (the gap) |
| Core lazy off, Image loading on | 3 and 5, as with core lazy on |
| Core lazy off, Load straight away 1 | 1 and 7 |
| Single post | featured image keeps `fetchpriority="high"`, no `loading`; Kadence related posts below lazy, as core makes them |

Resolves #1504

title: GH#1506: Robots.txt rules that work with or without an SEO plugin
body:
Resolves #1506

## What

New feature, on by default: **Robots.txt rules** (Links tab, `includes/features/class-seoprostack-robots-txt.php`). It gives `robots.txt` what every site needs, with or without an SEO plugin, and keeps every rule another plugin or the owner wrote.

- A `robots_txt` filter at priority 100000, after Rank Math's editor (10) and Yoast SEO (99999). It adds to each group of rules only the lines that group is missing: the admin path with `admin-ajax.php` allowed, search results (`/*?s=`, `/*&s=`, `/search/`), and, with WooCommerce, its log, upload and add-to-cart lines, which Rank Math's editor drops. Then a `Sitemap:` line when there is none, from `SEOProStack_Litespeed::sitemap_index()` (made public here). It leaves a path a group already names alone, skips a group that blocks the whole site, and never removes or changes another line.
- **Keep search results out of search engines** (on): `noindex, follow` in `wp_robots` and an `X-Robots-Tag` header on search results and their feeds.
- **Hide sites that discourage search engines** (on): `X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow` on every response while `blog_public` is 0. robots.txt never disallows `/` for such a site, because a page crawlers can't fetch can't show them its noindex.
- **Ask AI training crawlers to stay away** (off): one group for GPTBot, ClaudeBot, Google-Extended, Applebot-Extended, CCBot, meta-externalagent and Bytespider. It leaves out any crawler that a group already names, including the site's own groups. Search and answer crawlers are never in it.
- Panel: **Your own rules** (option `seoprostack_robots_txt_rules`, not autoloaded, cleaned to field and comment lines). When a static `robots.txt` file overrides WordPress, the panel says so, shows the file and offers to adopt it. Adopting keeps the file's own lines, drops the lines the feature adds anyway, and renames the file to `robots.txt-<date>.bak`. Both forms save in place (`admin/js/seoprostack-tabs.js`) or through admin-post.php without JavaScript, and check the nonce and `SEOProStack_Settings::can_change()`.
- Caches: a change purges LiteSpeed Cache's copy of `/robots.txt` and, with Clear Cloudflare's copies of pages, Cloudflare's copy. A change to `blog_public` empties the page cache.
- Registered in `SEOProStack_Setup::FEATURES`; `uninstall.php` deletes the own rules and keeps any renamed file. Docs: `README.md` (feature section, on-by-default list), `readme.txt`, `changelog.txt`.

## Testing

- `scripts/lint.sh`: php, js, shell, workflows, phpcs, phpstan, build all pass.
- Disposable test site (`scripts/test-site.sh`, WordPress 7.1.4, PHP 8.3, pretty permalinks):
  - No SEO plugin: search lines and `wp-sitemap.xml` added; `/?s=test` answered `X-Robots-Tag: noindex, follow`.
  - `blog_public` 0: pages, feed and robots.txt answered one `X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow`; robots.txt had no `Disallow: /`.
  - Yoast SEO 28.8: its block, its `Disallow:` and `sitemap_index.xml` kept; admin and search lines added inside it; no second sitemap.
  - Rank Math 1.0.282 editor (a `*` group with `Disallow: /private/`, a Bingbot group with `Crawl-delay: 5`) plus WooCommerce 11.2.2: both groups kept their lines and gained the admin, search and WooCommerce lines; Rank Math's sitemap listed.
  - AI training on with an own GPTBot group: the added group named the other six only (this test found a bug in the order of the check, fixed in this PR).
  - Static `robots.txt`: answered instead of WordPress until the adopt handler (AJAX, as an administrator) kept its own lines, dropped the duplicates and renamed it; WordPress then answered.
  - Debug log: only WooCommerce's own early-translation notice from its install.

## Decisions

- Add rules, never replace them: SEO plugins and owners keep control, and the feature works the same with Rank Math, Yoast, both or neither.
- Search pages get `noindex, follow`, and robots.txt also disallows them. That stops search URLs from being crawled, and the header covers search pages that are already indexed.
- Private sites rely on headers, not `Disallow: /`, so search engines can see the noindex.
- AI-training blocking stays off by default: it is a choice about the site's content, not a safe default for every site.

title: GH#1513: Search custom fields: scalar subquery, so a common word never reads the whole postmeta table
body:
## What

Search custom fields no longer lets a common search word read the whole `wp_postmeta` table.

`SEOProStack_Field_Search::search()` tested field values with a correlated `EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM wp_postmeta AS sps_v … WHERE sps_v.post_id = wp_posts.ID …)`. MariaDB (`exists_to_in`) and MySQL 8.0.16+ may turn that into a semi-join, and with many candidate posts the optimizer filled it first by reading every postmeta row with a `LIKE` on each value (`MATERIALIZED sps_v type=ALL rows=3987653` on a directory site, MariaDB 11.8). `LIMIT 1` inside the `EXISTS` does not stop that.

The field test is now a scalar subquery, which is never made a semi-join and always runs per candidate post through the `post_id` index:

- include: `(SELECT 1 … LIMIT 1) IS NOT NULL`
- exclude (`-word`): `(SELECT 1 … LIMIT 1) IS NULL`, instead of `NOT EXISTS (…)`

Same matches, placeholders and values.

## Files

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-field-search.php`: `search()`, the field test.
- `changelog.txt`: Unreleased entry.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh`: all passed (php, js, shell, workflows, phpcs, phpstan).
- Read-only on the live directory site (about 4 million postmeta rows): the patched class loaded under another name, its SQL compared with the live class's for the page's own main query (captured at `posts_pre_query`), full ID lists without `LIMIT`:

| Search | Plan for `sps_v`, before → after | Full list, before → after | Same IDs, same order |

| `service` | MATERIALIZED ALL 3,987,653 → DEPENDENT ref `post_id` 40 | 4.11–4.99 s → 1.95–3.43 s (13,655) | yes |

title: GH#1470: Fixes for other plugins: the web server answers Tutor LMS Pro's push worker; it unregisters once Notifications is off
body:
## Summary

New SEOProStack_Tutor_Push_Worker (includes/class-seoprostack-tutor-push-worker.php), booted from Fixes for other plugins. From the main site's admin_init it writes /tutor-push-notification.js to get_home_path() with a marker comment: Tutor LMS Pro's own worker while the Notifications add-on is on (on a network only when every site with Tutor LMS Pro has it on), and a self-unregistering worker once it is off and browsers are known to have Tutor's. A check that reaches WordPress with the add-on off is answered at init priority 1 with the unregistering worker (no-cache). Files without the marker are never touched. Rechecked on tutor_addons_config saves, plugin updates and daily; removed on switch-off, deactivation and uninstall. Hosting needs notes an unwritable root, a network with mixed add-on state, and the add-on on with no published courses. README and changelog updated.



## Files Changed

README.md, changelog.txt, includes/class-seoprostack-tutor-push-worker.php, includes/features/class-seoprostack-hosting-needs.php, includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-fixes.php, uninstall.php

## Decisions

The file is Tutor's bytes with one marker comment line first (the issue asks for both byte-identical and a marker; the marker wins, as it guards owner files). Written to get_home_path(), not ABSPATH, because Tutor registers it at home_url(), which differs when WordPress is in a subfolder. Add-on state is read from the stored tutor_addons_config and active plugins list, so a request on which Load plugins only where needed skips Tutor LMS Pro is not taken as add-on off (which would unregister working workers). On subdirectory networks, subsites' worker addresses do not map to the root file and still reach PHP.

- **Verification:** runtime-verified — scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan: all passed. title: GH#1517: Image loading: pictures in Kadence Blocks columns get a sizes for the column's width on a computer
body:
## Summary

Image loading now gives pictures in a Kadence Blocks row's column a `sizes` for the column's width on a computer, so pictures that load straight away (often the page's largest, with `fetchpriority="high"`) are no longer fetched for the whole window. Never less sharp: every value is at least the width the picture paints.

WordPress's `sizes="(max-width: Wpx) 100vw, Wpx"` made a picture in a narrow column fetch the copy for the window. PageSpeed evidence (1.3.195): on one directory home page the main picture, in a two-column `left-golden` row's narrow column, came as its 1024 copy where it showed 406 px wide (205 KiB more); four other Kadence home pages showed 56 to 264 KiB more on their first column pictures. Lazy pictures already had `sizes="auto"` (#1485).

title: GH#1523: Search custom fields: test post type and status first, so result counts skip the field test for attachments and revisions
body:
Resolves #1523

## What

Search custom fields now moves the finished search clause to the end of `WHERE`, so the database tests post type and status before it runs the correlated postmeta field test. Counting a common word's results no longer runs that test for every attachment and revision.

## Why

WordPress adds `$search` to `WHERE` before the post type and status clauses (`wp-includes/class-wp-query.php`, `$where .= $search …`), and MariaDB tests `AND` parts in that order. On a large directory site (106,927 posts: 45,028 attachments, 28,236 revisions), every row that failed the title, excerpt and content tests ran the field subquery, and the type/status test then dropped most of them. The page query stops after 12 matches, so it was cheap; the count for page numbers reads the whole list, and took 1.6–8.3 s.

## How

`includes/features/class-seoprostack-field-search.php`:

- `search()` records each query whose clause it rebuilt (by `spl_object_id`).
- `remember()` (`posts_search`, `PHP_INT_MAX`) keeps that query's clause as the last filter leaves it, because another plugin may wrap it.
- `search_last()` (`posts_where_paged`, `PHP_INT_MAX`) moves the clause to the end of `WHERE` only when all of these hold:
  - it appears once;
  - it starts with `AND`;
  - `and_only()` finds no top-level `OR`, `XOR` or `||`, comment, `;`, or unbalanced bracket or quote in the clause or in the rest of `WHERE`.

  Otherwise `WHERE` is unchanged. `AND` parts give the same rows in any order.

## Evidence

Read-only A/B on the live site (MariaDB 11.8, WordPress 7.1.4): the whole main query and its count, live class against this file loaded under another name, `cache_results` off.

| `/?s=` | Before | After | Results | Same first page |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `service` | 1.80 s (fewest of 4) | 0.38 s | 13,655 both | yes |
| `service -plumber` | 2.23–3.29 s | 0.41–0.48 s | 13,257 both | yes |
| `roof repair` | 0.18 s | 0.18 s | 405 both | yes |
| `plumber` | 0.17 s | 0.17 s | 592 both | yes |
| `guttering` (smaller site) | 0.08 s | 0.09 s | 126 both | yes |

In the patched SQL, the last `wp_posts.post_status = 'publish'` comes before the field subquery. Probe files were removed from the host afterwards.

## Checks

- `bash scripts/lint.sh`: exit 0 (php, js, shell, workflows, phpcs, phpstan).
- No new hooks or settings.

title: GH#1525: Short not-found answer for missing files (llms.txt, pictures, probes) instead of the theme's whole 404 page
body:
## Summary

New Server-tab setting, on by default: **Short not-found answer for missing files** (`SEOProStack_Quick_404`).

A request for a file that is not there (`/llms.txt`, a removed picture, a bot's `.php` or `.env` probe) got the theme's whole not-found page. On two large directory sites that took 6.0 to 9.0 s when the page cache did not have it: parse and main query 0.66 s; the theme's 404 template 2.77 s and 91 of 118 queries. PageSpeed Insights' Agentic Browsing check gives `/llms.txt` 2 s (Lighthouse `fetchResource(url, {timeout: 2_000})`) and fails with "Timed out fetching resource". Any other 4xx answer passes, so a quick 404 is enough.

## How

- `template_include` at `PHP_INT_MAX`, so it runs after every redirect and after every plugin that serves its own file. Those plugins set a 200 status, so they are never touched.
- It acts only when `is_404()` is true, the status is 404 or 410, and the path's last part has a file extension other than `.htm`, `.html`, `.shtml` or `.xhtml` and does not end in `/`.
- The answer is the status text ("Not Found" or "Gone") as `text/plain` with `X-Robots-Tag: noindex`, then `exit`.
- Rank Math's 404 Monitor records from `get_header` (or `wp_head` on block themes), which the short answer skips. So its `capture_404` callback, found on either hook, runs first.
- Filter `seoprostack_quick_404` (bool, path) lets site code keep the theme's page for a path. Listed in `docs/HOOKS.md`.
- Listed in Speed plan defaults and README (On by default → Server; its own section; Server list).
- Also corrects the 1.3.199 changelog line for #1523 to describe the guard as merged (top-level AND only; no OR, XOR, `||`, BETWEEN or CASE).

## Testing

Disposable test site (`scripts/test-site.sh up`: WordPress 7.1.4, PHP 8.3, Apache, pretty links) with Rank Math 1.0.282 (sitemap, llms.txt and 404 Monitor modules on):

| Address | Status | Body | Time |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/llms.txt` (Rank Math module off) | 404 | 10 B text/plain | 0.05 s |
| `/missing.jpg`, `/missing.jpg?ver=1`, `/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/gone.webp`, `/.env` | 404 | 10 B text/plain | 0.02 s |
| `/missing-page/`, `/foo.bar/`, `/old.html` | 404 | 54.7 KB theme page | 0.03–0.6 s |
| `/llms.txt` (Rank Math module on) | 200 | 731 B | unchanged |
| `/sitemap_index.xml`, `/post-sitemap.xml`, `/robots.txt`, `/wp-sitemap.xml` | 200 | unchanged | |
| `/old-brochure.pdf` (410 Gone list) | 410 | "Gone", 5 B text/plain | |
| `/old-page/` (410 Gone list) | 410 | theme page | |

- With the setting off, every address got the theme page again.
- Rank Math's 404 Monitor recorded `missing-photo.jpg` once (short answer), and `missing-page-two` and `old.html` once each (theme page).
- No SEO Pro Stack notices in `debug.log`.
- `scripts/lint.sh`: all passed. `node scripts/check-hooks.mjs`: 157 hooks; all match.

Live check after release: cold `/llms.txt` on the large directory sites, which took 8.8–9.0 s before.

Resolves #1525

title: GH#1533: Website Setup board task for backups, updates and uptime alerts
body:
## What and why

Adds the Website Setup board task "Setup Backups, Updates and Uptime Alerts" after "Setup Payment Processing", with links to Hostinger's guides. A read-only audit of 23 directory sites' boards found no task for backups, for who installs updates, or for knowing when the site is down.

The task covers:
- checking that backups are listed at the right interval (daily for sites that take orders, bookings or messages);
- generating a backup before big changes (entry-level plans need an upgrade; until then, download the latest automatic backup);
- downloading one backup and checking it holds the files and the database, never testing Restore on the live site (it overwrites the site; Hostinger staging can't restore backups, depends on the plan, and doesn't support multisite);
- choosing one updater (Smart or Native auto-updates);
- a monthly update check;
- an hPanel Monitoring alert.

On existing boards, `wp seoprostack starters add fluent-boards` places the task after the payments task when that task is in the same stage and not archived. Otherwise the task goes to the top of its stage (`place_task()`).

Resolves #1533

## How it was tested

- `node scripts/readme-setup-tasks.js --check --dir .`: README matches the 12 Website Setup tasks.
- `starters/fluent-boards.json` parses as JSON.
- Hostinger facts checked against https://docs.hostinger.com/websites/backups and https://docs.hostinger.com/wordpress/staging.

title: GH#1535: 480 pixel picture copy, and AVIF copies only when smaller than WebP (GH#1536)
body:
## What

- **#1535, Image loading:** adds a 480 pixel wide copy (`seoprostack-480`, uncropped). WordPress makes copies 300 and 768 pixels wide and nothing between. Uploads now get the 480 copy. Older pictures that a front-end page shows with a `srcset` get it in the background, and no page is purged for it.
- **#1536, WebP and AVIF images:** a file's AVIF copy is kept only when it is smaller than that file's WebP copy. The AVIF quality description now matches what was measured. Defaults are unchanged.

Resolves #1535
Resolves #1536

## Why

- **#1535:** PageSpeed Insights (mobile) on a Kadence site's home page: six grid pictures painted at 380 device pixels were fetched at 768w, 211 KiB more than needed. Browsers take the smallest `srcset` file at least as wide as the pixels they paint, so a 480 copy is never less sharp.
- **#1536:** browsers that accept AVIF get the AVIF copy whenever there is one. A read-only count found AVIF copies larger than their WebP copies: 2,200 of 34,540 files on one site, 55 of 842 and 25 of 808 on two others.

## How

- `includes/class-seoprostack-picture-sizes.php`:
  - `register()` adds the size.
  - The `srcset()` filter calls the new `want_small()`, which queues the picture as `SMALL_ONLY` (-1) under `_seoprostack_small_tried`. `want()` keeps its two arguments and queues every size. Both go through `look()`, `first_look()`, `due()` and `enqueue()`; `run()` uses `filters()` and `run_one()`. This keeps each method under Codacy's PHPMD limits.
  - When a hero or slide picture lacks only that size, it is queued the same way, without a page refresh.
  - Pictures a page needs every size of run first. When the queue is full, the last picture waiting for the 480 copy alone makes room for one (`add()`).
  - `make()` and `only_these()` make only the sizes asked for.
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-image-loading.php`: registers the size on every request (admin included), so uploads get it. Description updated.
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-nextgen-images.php`:
  - Each file's WebP copy is made first.
  - `convert_file()` and `adopt_compressx_copy()` take the size to beat: the smaller of the original and the WebP copy. `convert_file()` is split into `kept_copy()`, `encode()` and `editor()`, and its own `rename()` no longer hides errors with `@`.
  - An up-to-date AVIF copy that is not smaller is removed and recorded as 0.
  - An AVIF copy recorded 0 is tried again when the WebP copy is made again or WebP copies are switched off.
- `uninstall.php`: deletes `_seoprostack_small_tried`.
- `README.md`, `changelog.txt`: feature docs and Unreleased entries. The short `readme.txt` line is written at release.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`: all passed.
- PHPMD 3.0.0 (`codesize`, `cleancode`) on the two changed classes: the only findings in changed code are class-wide ones that are already on `main`. The remaining `@rename` is in the unchanged `adopt_compressx_copy()`.
- `scripts/test-site.sh` (WordPress 7.1.4, PHP 8.3, ImageMagick 7.1.2), with the evidence in `changelog.txt`:
  - Three uploads got their 480 copies, with WebP and AVIF copies.
  - I removed the 480 copy from one picture. One visit to a page showing it queued `{5: -1}`. One `run()` made the copy (16,254 bytes; WebP 14,110, AVIF 12,209) and emptied the queue, and the page's `srcset` then listed `480w`.
  - Hero `want()`: a picture lacking only the 480 copy was queued as -1. One lacking 1536x1536 too was queued as 0.
  - After the refactor (`2fd84137`, rebuilt test site): calling `want_small()` after `want()` kept 0; calling `want()` after `want_small()` changed -1 to 0. The page-visit → `run()` → `480w` check above passed again with the same byte counts.
  - `add()` with a full queue: a page picture replaced the last -1 entry, and an entry waiting for the 480 copy alone was not added. `run()` takes page pictures first.
  - AVIF: of 23 files, 9 kept no AVIF copy because it was not smaller than the WebP copy (on this encoder build). `Accept: image/avif,image/webp` returned `image/webp`, 33,238 bytes, for such a file, and `image/avif` for another.
  - An old up-to-date 39,424-byte AVIF copy was removed at the next non-forced conversion. With WebP off it was made again, and removed again when WebP was switched back on.
  - `debug.log` stayed empty.

title: GH#1542: refresh pages after their 480 picture copies are made; 9 copies a run
body:
## Summary

Image loading's 480 pixel copy (#1535, 1.3.201) reached visitors only when a cached page expired, up to a week later (LiteSpeed public TTL 604800 s on the sites checked), and pictures seen while the 50-picture queue was full were not looked at again until then.

- `includes/class-seoprostack-picture-sizes.php`: `look()` calls the new `note_page()` when it queues a picture for the 480 copy alone, even when the queue had no room. It remembers the singular post the page shows in `seoprostack_picture_pages` (at most 20, not autoloaded). After a `run()` that made anything, when no picture waits for the 480 copy alone, those posts are refreshed with the existing `refresh()` (purge only those posts, then Keep pages cached opens them again) and forgotten. The refreshed page lists the new copies and queues the pictures that found no room, so a full queue drains page by page.
- A run now makes the 480 copy alone for up to 9 pictures (`SMALL_BATCH`), or every size for up to 3 (`BATCH`, each counting 3). The 20 s budget is unchanged. On one site, three 480 copies with their WebP and AVIF copies took 1 to 2 s in all.
- `uninstall.php`: deletes `seoprostack_picture_pages`.
- `README.md`, `changelog.txt`: feature text and Unreleased entries. This also moves the #1529 changelog line (merged after the v1.3.201 tag) from `= 1.3.201 =` to `= Unreleased =`.



## Files Changed

README.md, changelog.txt, includes/class-seoprostack-picture-sizes.php, uninstall.php

## Decisions

- Pages are refreshed after any batch that made something, when no picture waits for the 480 copy alone, not only after a 480 batch. This way a page whose pictures found the queue full of every-size pictures is not left waiting a week. Each refresh follows a batch that made progress, so the cycle ends.
- Only singular posts and pages are remembered: archives have no post ID to purge by tag, and they list the copy at their next refresh as before.
- Image quality is unchanged: browsers take the smallest file at least as wide as the pixels they paint.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — - `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan build`: all passed.
- `scripts/test-site.sh` (WordPress 7.1.4, PHP 8.3), branch build: 55 pictures without the 480 copy, as image blocks on a static front page (post 59). The purge was observed through `seoprostack_page_cache_purge_post`.
  - 1st anonymous render: queue 50 (all -1), pages `[59]`, 5 dropped.
  - Batches: 9, 9, 9, 9, 9, 5 copies (0.3 to 0.5 s each). Only the batch that emptied the queue purged `[59]`, and the remembered pages were cleared.
  - 2nd render: `480w` in 50 srcsets. It queued the 5 dropped pictures and remembered `[59]`. One batch made them and purged `[59]`.
  - 3rd render: `480w` in all 55 srcsets. Nothing was queued and no page was remembered.
  - Failing copy (watermarked picture lacking 480): purged `[59]` once when the queue drained. After that it was not queued again, not remembered and not purged.
  - Queue full of 50 every-size pictures with `[59]` remembered: batches made 3 each, and the first released and purged `[59]`.
  - `debug.log` empty.

title: GH#1546: purge page caches after Customizer, widget and site identity saves
body:
Resolves #1546

## What

Neither LiteSpeed Cache nor WP-Optimize purges the page cache after a Customizer save, a widget save or a change to the site title, tagline or icon. So a new logo, header or palette stayed off cached pages for LiteSpeed's public TTL (7 days on the directory sites), and off Cloudflare's copies too.

`SEOProStack_Page_Cache` (`includes/class-seoprostack-page-cache.php`) now calls its existing `purge_all()`:

- on `customize_save_after`;
- when `updated_option` or `added_option` reports a changed `blogname`, `blogdescription`, `site_icon`, `sidebars_widgets`, `widget_*`, `theme_mods_<stylesheet>` or `kadence_global_palette`.

It purges once a request, and only from wp-admin, the REST API or WP-CLI. It skips WP-Cron, a front-end page that writes an option, and imports (`WP_IMPORTING`). Clear Cloudflare's copies of pages and Keep pages cached already follow `litespeed_purged_all`, so they need no change.

The Keep pages cached header comment and README said Customizer saves already emptied the cache. They now name this purge.

## Verify

`scripts/test-site.sh` (WordPress 7.1.4, PHP 8.3, LiteSpeed Cache 7.9.3), counting `litespeed_purged_all` from WP-CLI:

| Change | Purges |
|---|---|
| new tagline, theme mod, widget option, palette, `customize_save_after` | 1 each |
| title and tagline in one request | 1 |
| same tagline again, an unrelated option, a change from WP-Cron | 0 |

`vendor/bin/phpcs` clean on both PHP files; debug.log empty.

Purges from content and Customizer saves will run fresh, not stale (the owner's rule), in #1547.

title: GH#1547: a saved post empties its own Cloudflare pages; saves purge fresh, not stale
body:
## What

Resolves #1547.

1. **A saved post empties only its own pages at Cloudflare.** `litespeed_purged_post()` emptied the whole site at Cloudflare whenever LiteSpeed Cache's **Pages** purge rule (`purge-post_p`, on by default) was on. That rule purges the `PGS` tag, which LiteSpeed Cache sets only where `is_page()` (`src/tag.cls.php`, 7.9), so on a directory with 10,000 listings, every saved listing emptied 10,000 Cloudflare copies for a few dozen Pages. Now only **All pages** (`purge-post_all`) empties the site. `post_changed()` sends what the new `post_pages()` lists from LiteSpeed's rules:
   - addresses (`files`): the post (once unpublished or trashed, the address it had), front and home page, the posts page for posts, each published Page, its term, post type, author and date archives;
   - prefixes: each of those lists' pagination (`<list>/page/`), never a list's whole folder, because a listing's own address can sit inside one;
   - new `post_moved()` (`post_updated`): a published post's old address when its slug, parent or date changes;
   - new supported filter `seoprostack_cloudflare_purge_post_urls` (`$files`, `$post`) for add-ons such as SEO Pro Directory (#535 there);
   - `MAX_URLS` 30 → 90 (three requests of `MAX_ITEMS`); above that, the whole site.
   - Without LiteSpeed Cache as the page cache, `RULES` (LiteSpeed's defaults without Pages).
2. **Saves purge fresh, not stale.** With LiteSpeed's **Serve Stale** on, every purge of a request goes out stale. A server that serves the stale copy while it rebuilds could then hand the old page to Cloudflare for its whole edge time (the owner's rule: stale is fine after updates, not after a content or Customizer save). New `SEOProStack_Litespeed::fresh_after_saves()` on `litespeed_conf_load_option_purge-stale` returns false where `saves_content()` finds a save. Detection uses only the request, because LiteSpeed asks on `after_setup_theme`: `post.php` editpost/trash/untrash/delete, `edit.php` bulk actions, `admin-ajax.php` POST inline-save/customize_save/save-widget/widgets-order, POST to `nav-menus.php`/`widgets.php`, and REST writes under `/wp/v2/` or `/batch/v1`. Updates, Purge All and WP-CLI keep Serve Stale.

## Files

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-cloudflare-purge.php`: `RULES`, `post_pages()`, `published_link()`, `post_moved()`, `prefixes()`, `targets()` splitting addresses and prefixes, log wording for several folders.
- `includes/class-seoprostack-litespeed.php`: `fresh_after_saves()`, `saves_content()`.
- `docs/HOOKS.md`, `README.md` (Clear Cloudflare's copies of pages; LiteSpeed Cache preset → Saves purge fresh), `changelog.txt`.

## Verification

Test site from `scripts/test-site.sh` (WordPress 7.1.4, PHP 8.3, LiteSpeed Cache 7.9.3, Serve Stale on):

- A real block-editor save (REST POST `/wp/v2/posts/7` with an application password) answered `X-LiteSpeed-Purge: public,fc6_Po.7,…` without `stale`; the same save from WP-CLI queued `public,stale,…`.
- 16 HTTP requests read with `\LiteSpeed\Control::is_stale()` (a must-use probe on the throwaway site only): 0 for every save listed above, 1 for the front end, REST reads, other REST routes, heartbeat, GET admin-ajax, opening the editor and the posts list.
- With LiteSpeed's default rules (f, h, p, pwrp, a, t, pt, m): a post update queued the post, home, category, tag and month archives and four Pages as files, plus four `/page/` prefixes. The send path (Cloudflare stubbed with `pre_http_request`) sent one `files` and one `prefixes` request. A slug change added the old address; a trashed post queued `/probe-post/`, not its `__trashed` address; a draft queued nothing; All pages on, or 98 published Pages, queued the whole site. Without LiteSpeed as the page cache, the page, home, category and tag.
- `vendor/bin/phpcs` on both PHP files, `scripts/lint.sh phpstan` and `node scripts/check-hooks.mjs`: passed.

Live: the scoped token from this session is on all 24 PSD networks (Clear Cloudflare's copies of pages on). On one network, a URL purge went HIT (age 170) → purge 200 → MISS → HIT, and a host purge went HIT → 200 → MISS. This PR changes which pages a post save sends there.

Holding the merge until the 1.3.202 release PR lands (release session asked to hold merges to main).

title: GH#1545: a one-day Cloudflare edge time while purges reach Cloudflare
body:
## What

Resolves #1545.

New setting **Cloudflare edge time**, under **Speed → Clear Cloudflare's copies of pages**: 1 day by default, or 2 hours, 1 week, 30 days, or none (Cloudflare's own setting). It is sent only while a token and zone are set and Cloudflare's last answer did not refuse them. Edits and updates then empty Cloudflare's copies, so Cloudflare can keep pages longer than its default 2 hours. Before this, sites had two choices: a short edge time, which sends every page back to the server every few minutes, or Cloudflare's default, which serves stale pages for up to 2 hours after a change.

- `SEOProStack_Cloudflare_Purge::send_edge_time()` runs on `template_redirect` at `PHP_INT_MAX - 100`, after redirects, and sends `Cloudflare-CDN-Cache-Control: max-age=<setting>, stale-if-error=86400`. Only Cloudflare reads this header; browsers and LiteSpeed Cache ignore it. `stale-if-error` lets Cloudflare keep serving its copy while the origin returns errors, for example when a shared hosting account hits its CPU limit.
- It is sent only for anonymous `GET` and `HEAD` front-end responses. It is not sent for wp-admin, AJAX, cron or REST requests, logged-in users, previews, 404s, search results, feeds, trackbacks, robots.txt, password-protected posts, `DONOTCACHEPAGE`, or responses that already send `Cache-Control` with `no-store`, `no-cache` or `private` (WooCommerce basket, checkout and account pages).
- An address with a query string gets 5 minutes at most (`EDGE_QUERY`), because a purge by address cannot reach every filtered list or campaign link.
- `check_edge_time()` removes the header at the end of the page when the page turned out not to be cacheable. That covers LiteSpeed's `Control::is_cacheable()` false, a late `DONOTCACHEPAGE`, and a late no-store or private `Cache-Control`. Cloudflare reads this header before `Cache-Control`, so it would otherwise keep those pages. The check runs through LiteSpeed Cache's `litespeed_buffer_after`. Without LiteSpeed Cache (no `litespeed_initing`), it runs through an output buffer of its own.
- `refused()`: when Cloudflare's newest logged answer is a 4xx other than 429 (a wrong token or zone), no edge time is sent, because purges would not reach Cloudflare. Rate limits and outages are retried, so they do not block the edge time.
- New filter `seoprostack_cloudflare_edge_time` (seconds; 0 sends nothing), listed in `docs/HOOKS.md`.
- The Hosting needs advice for "Cloudflare keeps pages and nothing clears them" now points to this setting instead of a hand-made short edge time.

Pages that LiteSpeed Cache already holds were saved with their old headers, so they get the edge time the next time they are cached. A site's own `Cloudflare-CDN-Cache-Control` sent later on `template_redirect` still wins. On the PSD sites, the `psd-edge-cache-time.php` mu-plugin (300 s) keeps control until it is removed after this ships.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`: all passed. `node scripts/check-hooks.mjs`: 158 hooks, all match.
- Test site (WordPress 7.1.4, PHP 8.3, Apache), with Clear Cloudflare's copies of pages on and a placeholder token and zone. Response headers with no page cache plugin and again with LiteSpeed Cache 7.9 active:
  - Home, a post and `HEAD /`: `Cloudflare-CDN-Cache-Control: max-age=86400, stale-if-error=86400`.
  - `/?utm_source=x`: `max-age=300`.
  - Search, 404, feed, password-protected post, preview redirect, logged in (real auth cookie), POST, early `Cache-Control: private`, late `Cache-Control: no-store` (wp_footer) and late `DONOTCACHEPAGE` (wp_footer): no edge header.
  - With LiteSpeed Cache: `litespeed_control_set_nocache` called in wp_footer: no edge header. The same page without it: the edge header is sent.
  - Last logged answer 403: none sent. Last answer 429, or no log: sent.

## Files

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-cloudflare-purge.php`: setting, `edge_options()`, `send_edge_time()`, `check_edge_time()`, `edge_cacheable()`, `refused()`.
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-hosting-needs.php`: advice text.
- `README.md`, `changelog.txt`, `docs/HOOKS.md`.

title: GH#1551: Keep pages cached refills the whole site only with LiteSpeed All pages rule
body:
## What

Resolves #1551.

**Keep pages cached** started a whole-site fill after every saved post when LiteSpeed Cache's **Pages** purge rule was on (it is on by default). The fill covers the main pages, then LiteSpeed Cache's crawler or up to 1,000 pages. But that rule purges only the `PGS` tag, which LiteSpeed Cache sets only where `is_page()`. On a directory with thousands of listings, each save refilled every page after a purge that emptied only the Pages, the post and its lists. #1547 (PR #1550) fixed the same wrong assumption for Cloudflare.

- `SEOProStack_Keep_Pages_Cached::litespeed_post_purged()` now starts the whole fill only when `purge-post_all` is on.
- With only **Pages** on, new `page_urls()` queues the published Pages that have no password, newest first, up to `COVERED_MAX` (50). It runs once per request and queues them alongside `post_changed()`'s post, home page and posts page, a minute later (`POST_DELAY`). The crawler reaches any further Pages.
- Why this option: it is cheaper than a whole-site plan. It needs one ID query and no fetch of the home page's links, and it reopens what the rule actually emptied, which on most sites includes the main pages (About, Contact, hubs).
- README → Keep pages cached and the changelog are updated.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`: all passed. `node scripts/check-hooks.mjs`: all match.
- Test site (WordPress 7.1.4, PHP 8.3, LiteSpeed Cache 7.9.3, `seoprostack_litespeed_server=openlitespeed`, default rules), checking `seoprostack_keep_pages_cached_queue` after `wp post update`:

title: GH#1557: Email protection covers the Kadence header, mobile and footer social buttons
body:
## Summary

Kadence 1.6.0 prints its header, mobile-header and footer social buttons with echo from the kadence_header_social, kadence_mobile_social and kadence_footer_social actions (callbacks at priority 10, no filter), so a social Email button's mailto: address stayed readable in the HTML. Where Cloudflare Email Address Obfuscation is on, Cloudflare rewrote it and injected its parser-blocking cdn-cgi email-decode.min.js, which PageSpeed lists in the Network dependency tree. On 11 November 2026 four Kadence sites (Trinity Joinery, Trinity Windows, EP Carpentry, August Awards) had 2-3 such links on their home pages, their only source of that script. SEOProStack_Email_Protection now buffers those actions (social_start() at priority 9, social_end() at 11) and prints the output through protect(), as content is. If another buffer is open above ours at priority 11, every buffer is left alone, so nothing is lost and the buttons stay plain. Skipped in the Customizer preview because selective refresh redraws without the restoring script. Files: includes/features/class-seoprostack-email-protection.php, README.md (Email protection section), changelog.txt (Unreleased).



## Files Changed

README.md, changelog.txt, includes/features/class-seoprostack-email-protection.php

## Decisions

Output buffering, not a Kadence template override: Kadence has no filter on these buttons, and a template copy would drift with theme updates. The buffer bails out without touching other buffers on a level mismatch, so the worst case is today's behaviour (plain address). Live check after deploy: those four sites' home pages should no longer load cdn-cgi/scripts/.../email-decode.min.js.

## Summary

New Speed feature, on by default: Measure Kadence's scrollbar without holding up the page (SEOProStack_Kadence_Scrollbar). Kadence 1.6.0 prints a wp_footer (priority 2) script that reads document.documentElement.clientWidth while the page is still parsing, forcing a full style and layout (PSI Forced reflow). title: GH#1573: fix: REST requests from cached pages keep working for visitors not logged in after the nonce expires
body:
Resolves #1573

## What

**Fixes for other plugins** (on by default) adds `SEOProStack_Plugin_Fixes::rest_anonymous_nonce()` on `rest_authentication_errors` at priority 101, after core's `rest_cookie_check_errors()` (100). When core refused the nonce (`rest_cookie_invalid_nonce`) and nobody is logged in, the request is answered as core answers one without a nonce: `wp_set_current_user(0)`, `true`, and the no-cache header core added for the error is removed. Logged-in users keep the 403.

## Why

Cached pages keep the REST nonce they were built with. Nonces last 12–24h, but LiteSpeed Cache keeps public pages for 7 days by default and Clear Cloudflare's copies of pages gives Cloudflare 1 day. Kadence Blocks Pro's query loop (`dist/query.js`) sends `kbp_query_loop_rest_endpoint.nonce` as `X-WP-Nonce` for filters and further pages, so on older cached pages those requests failed for anonymous visitors. A nonce guards a logged-in user against forged requests; with no login it guards nothing, and core already accepts the same request without one.

## Evidence

- Live directory subsite (12 Nov 2026): `GET /wp-json/wp/v2/kadence_query/query` with an invalid `X-WP-Nonce`, not logged in → **403** `rest_cookie_invalid_nonce`; without the header → **200**. The cached home page (`x-litespeed-cache: hit`, `cf-cache-status: HIT`) carries `kadence_query/query","nonce":"…"`.
- The method's logic, run with `wp eval-file` against that site's WordPress core (read-only):
  - core, anonymous, bogus nonce: `WP_Error:rest_cookie_invalid_nonce`
  - with the fix, anonymous, bogus nonce: `true`, `rest_send_nocache_headers` false
  - with the fix, logged in, bogus nonce: `WP_Error:rest_cookie_invalid_nonce`
  - with the fix, anonymous, no nonce: `true`
- `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan changelog hooks`: all passed.

## Files

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-fixes.php`: hook in `boot()`, new method, class header and setting description.
- `README.md`: Fixes for other plugins entry, `### Unreleased`.
- `changelog.txt`: `= Unreleased =`.

After deploy: the bogus-nonce request above should return 200 for a visitor who is not logged in.

title: GH#1579: fix: Fluent Forms file removal on cached pages for visitors not logged in
body:
## Summary

On a page cached for longer than a nonce lasts, a visitor who is not logged in could attach a file to a Fluent Forms upload field but not remove it: `403 {"success":false,"data":{"message":"Security check failed"}}`. Fluent Forms prints `file_delete_nonce` into the page, and Fluent Forms Pro's `Uploader::deleteFile()` always verifies it (uploads and submissions don't by default). Same cause as #1573, on an admin-ajax action.

## Change

**Fixes for other plugins** (`includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-fixes.php`):

- New `fluentforms_file_delete_nonce()` on `wp_ajax_nopriv_fluentform_delete_uploaded_file`, priority 9 (Fluent registers its handler at 10 through `addPublicAjaxAction()`; the framework's `hook_prefix` is empty). Registered only on AJAX requests.
- Only when a nonce was sent, nobody is logged in, Fluent Forms is loaded (`wpFluentForm()`), and `wp_verify_nonce(…, 'fluentform_file_delete')` refuses it: a fresh `wp_create_nonce('fluentform_file_delete')` replaces it in `$_GET`/`$_POST` (where present) and `$_REQUEST`, **and** in Fluent's shared request object via `wpFluentForm('request')->set()`. That object is a lazy singleton that copies `$_GET`/`$_POST` when first made (`ComponentBinder::resolveRequest()`), which may already have happened because admin-ajax.php runs `admin_init` before the action, so the superglobals alone would not be enough. `Uploader` reads `$app->request`, the same instance.
- Fluent's own `canDeleteAttachment()` and file-token checks still apply. Logged-in users never reach the nopriv action, so they keep the check.
- Class header paragraph, setting description sentence, README "Fixes for other plugins" entry and Unreleased lines in README.md and changelog.txt.

Checked against Fluent Forms and Fluent Forms Pro 6.2.15 source (`fluentformpro/fluentformpro.php:557`, `src/Uploader.php:934-939`, `vendor/wpfluent/framework/src/WPFluent/Http/Request/Request.php`).

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan changelog hooks`: all passed.
- `scripts/test-site.sh up` (WordPress 7.1.4, PHP 8.3) with Fluent Forms and Fluent Forms Pro 6.2.15, not logged in, `POST /wp-admin/admin-ajax.php action=fluentform_delete_uploaded_file&_fluentform_file_delete_nonce=0123456789`:
  - **Fixes for other plugins** off: `403 {"success":false,"data":{"message":"Security check failed"}}`.
  - On: `200 0` (Fluent's handler ran past the nonce check; no `path`, nothing deleted).
  - On, with `path=../wp-config.php` or `path=abc`: `403 Invalid file token`, Fluent's own token check, so only the nonce gate changes.
  - `wpFluentForm('request') === wpFluentForm()->request` (one shared instance, so `set()` reaches `Uploader`). No PHP messages in the debug log.
- Live after deploy (release with this change): on a directory subsite with Fluent Forms Pro, not logged in, `POST /wp-admin/admin-ajax.php` with `action=fluentform_delete_uploaded_file&_fluentform_file_delete_nonce=0123456789` should no longer answer 403 `Security check failed` (with no `path` it reaches Fluent's handler and deletes nothing).

Resolves #1579

title: GH#1577: feat: health checks and repairs copied font-cache paths on multisite (--repair --network)
body:
## Summary

`wp seoprostack health` returned `not_run` for copied Kadence/WPTT font-cache paths on every multisite, before reading `downloaded_font_files`. A network copied to a new install inherits that network option naming the source server's files, and the stylesheets Kadence then writes in `wp-content/fonts/` name those paths, so headings lose their font. The downstream directory deployment keeps `scripts/kadence-fonts-reset.sh` only for this.

## Change

`includes/class-seoprostack-health-cli.php`:

- `font_paths($repair, $network)`: the same `font_changes()` check runs on multisite, from any site's `--url` (the option and `wp-content/fonts` are shared by the network). title: GH#1578: feat: wp seoprostack rank-math identity adopts Site Identity on a copied site
body:
## Summary

**Keep Rank Math’s site identity in sync** (#1068) could not take over a copied site's identity: `sync_identity()` replaces only fields that are empty, already Site Identity's, or still its last write (`rank_math_identity_previous`). A copy kept the source's Rank Math names, logo and Open Graph image for good, and on a synced site a domain search-replace rewrote Rank Math's image URLs but not the base64 record, stranding the pairs. The directory deployment writes these with a per-site script for now.

## Change

`includes/features/class-seoprostack-rank-math-defaults.php`:

- New `wp seoprostack rank-math identity [--dry-run|--adopt] [--format=table|json]` (`cli_identity()`, registered in `boot()` on WP-CLI). Lists each field (`knowledgegraph_name`, `website_name`, `knowledgegraph_logo(_id)`, `open_graph_image(_id)`) with Rank Math's value, Site Identity's and `same`/`differs`/`no site value`. `--adopt` needs Rank Math defaults and the sync on (turns nothing on; errors otherwise), writes Site Identity's values with image URL and ID together, checks the save, then records them as synced so later changes follow. A field with no Site Identity value (no PNG logo/icon) keeps its value, recorded as synced.
- `sync_identity()` split into `identity_targets()`, `identity_previous()`/`save_identity_previous()` and `claimable()`; behaviour unchanged except that stored image URLs are compared by `image_key()`: the path from `/uploads/` on, without host or `sites/<id>/`, or the whole path outside uploads. title: GH#1590: fix: Readabler's reading mask covers the page when no height is saved
body:
## Summary

Readabler 2.0.20 prints `readingMaskHeight: "0"` on sites whose Readabler settings were never saved, so its ADHD Friendly profile (and Reading Mask) put a mask over the whole window that takes every click. **Fixes for other plugins** now gives Readabler's Design tab settings its own default height, 100 px, while none is saved.

title: GH#1593: feat: Keep pages cached fills TranslatePress's other languages
body:
## Summary

**Keep pages cached** now fills TranslatePress's other published languages too. TranslatePress serves each language under its slug (`/en/`, `/fr/`), which LiteSpeed caches as separate pages; until now only the default language was filled, so every translated page waited for its first visitor after each purge (uncached builds of 7–8 s on a 9-language site).

## Changes

- `includes/class-seoprostack-keep-cached-pages.php`
  - `of_site()`: the main pages (default language, order unchanged), then `translations()` of those pages, page-major (each page in every language before the next), then the rest of the site in the default language; capped at `MAX` (1,000 addresses).
  - `translations()` / `languages()`: languages from the current site's `trp_settings` (`publish-languages`, `url-slugs`; the default too with `add-subdirectory-to-default-language`), only with TranslatePress active there.
  - Addresses from TranslatePress's own `TRP_Url_Converter::get_url_for_language()` (follows SEO Pack's translated slugs) when it runs for the current site; when the main site plans another network site (TranslatePress holds the main site's settings), `language_url()` builds them from that site's settings, as the converter does without translated slugs.
  - `network()`: the first round stays default-language only; the second adds translations. A site whose list no longer fits the queue is planned whole in a later batch, not cut.
  - New public `with_translations()`.
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-keep-pages-cached.php`: `post_changed()` queues the post's page, the home page and the posts page in every language. The LiteSpeed **Pages** purge-rule refill stays default-language, so one save does not open up to 50 Pages × N languages.
- README → Keep pages cached, changelog (Unreleased).

## Verification

On a shared hosting account's TranslatePress networks (LiteSpeed Cache 7.9.3, TranslatePress 3.3.8 + Business 1.8.8, SEO Pack on), with the changed class loaded under another name through `wp eval-file`:

- Settings-based addresses matched TranslatePress's converter for all 3,333 page × language pairs checked on 2-, 3- and 9-language sites (0 different).
- Plans: 150 main pages became 294 addresses (2 languages) and 436 (3); 9 languages reach the 1,000 cap (143 default, about 107 each other). Single-site and network plans agree.
- `trp_converter()`: used on the site itself and when switched to itself; not used when switched to another network site.
- A saved page queues `/`, `/account/`, `/fr/`, `/en/`, `/fr/account/`, `/en/account/` (3-language site).
- 1,350 converter calls took 1.6 s, once per fill.
- `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan hooks changelog`: all passed.

Test files removed from the server afterwards. Not deployed.

Resolves #1593

title: GH#1599: fix: Readabler's Design features print empty styles when no Design settings are saved
body:
## Summary

Readabler's Cognitive Disability Mode seemed to do nothing on sites whose Readabler settings were never saved. The profile turned on `mdp-readabler-highlight-titles` and `-links`, but the page printed `--readabler-highlight-titles-style: ;` and `--readabler-highlight-titles-width: px;`, so the outline was invalid and computed to `none`. The cause is the same as #1590: Readabler collects each Design default only when the settings it already has turn the feature on. Highlight Hover, Highlight Focus, Reading Guide, Text Magnifier and the Virtual Keyboard had the same gap.

`SEOProStack_Plugin_Fixes::readabler_design_defaults()` replaces `readabler_mask_height()` on the same `option_` / `default_option_mdp_readabler_design_settings` filters. It gives every Design setting that is missing or empty Readabler 2.0.20's own default (`READABLER_DESIGN_DEFAULTS`). I read the defaults from `TabDesign`'s `fields_*()` with every feature on. The text magnifier background is spelt `rgba` (Readabler's own default is the invalid `rbga`). Nothing is stored, and saved values are left alone.

Files: `includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-fixes.php`, `README.md` (the Plugin fixes entry now covers #1590 and #1599; Unreleased), `changelog.txt`.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan changelog hooks`: all passed.
- Playwright on a live site (1.3.210) as a new visitor with Cognitive Disability Mode turned on: the body classes are set, the custom properties read `style="" width="px" color=""`, and headings and links show `outline-style: none`.
- WP-CLI on that site (only `reading_mask_height` saved), with the old filter removed, then this branch's filter added and Readabler's settings reloaded:
  - Without: `--readabler-highlight-titles-style: ; ... -width: px; ... --readabler-text-magnifier-bg-color: ; --readabler-reading-guide-height: px`, `virtual_keyboard_layout=null`.
  - With: `solid`, `#639af9`, `2px`, `2px` for titles and links, `rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.9)`, `12px`, `["english"]`.
  - The stored option is unchanged (`a:1:{s:19:"reading_mask_height";s:3:"100";}`) before and after.
- WP-CLI on a site with all 35 Design settings saved (custom colours, a 200 px mask, keyboard layout `"english"`): the output is identical with and without the filter.

title: GH#1604: fix: explicit nullable parameter for PHP 8.4+
body:
For #1604. Follow-up to #1605, before tagging 1.3.214.

## Why

`scripts/preflight-release.sh --no-docker` on the release commit (local PHP 8.5) failed the PHP syntax check of both zips:
